title: Create a ticket manually
aliases: log a ticket for a phone call
open a ticket on behalf of a customer
body:
Use this when a customer contacts you by phone or in person.
1. Select **New ticket** at the top of the screen.
2. In **Requester**, start typing the customer's name or email and select them from the list.
3. Enter a **Subject** and a description of the issue.
4. Set the **Priority** and **Assignee** if needed.
5. Select **Submit as Open**.

title: Reply to a customer on a ticket
body:
1. Open the ticket from **Tickets** or a view.
2. Select **Reply** below the conversation.
3. Type your message. The reply goes to the requester and any CC recipients.
4. Choose a status from the **Submit as** menu.
5. Select **Send**.

title: Add an internal note to a ticket
aliases: write a note only agents can see
add a comment for my team
body:
Internal notes are never sent to the requester.
1. Open the ticket.
2. Select **Add note** below the conversation.
3. Type your note. Use @ followed by a name to mention a colleague.
4. Select **Add note** to save it.

title: Assign a ticket to an agent
aliases: hand over a ticket to a colleague
body:
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select the **Assignee** field.
3. Choose the agent from the list, or select **Take it** to assign the ticket to yourself.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Assign a ticket to a group
aliases: send a ticket to a team
change the group on a ticket
route a ticket to another queue
body:
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select the **Group** field.
3. Choose the group, such as **Billing** or **Technical Support**.
4. Leave **Assignee** blank to let the group pick it up, or choose an agent.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Merge two tickets
aliases: merge a duplicate ticket into another
consolidate tickets from the same customer
body:
The duplicate ticket is closed after the merge.
1. Open the ticket you want to keep as the main ticket.
2. Select the **More actions** menu, then **Merge**.
3. Search for the duplicate ticket by number or subject and select it.
4. Choose whether to add the duplicate's comments as a public reply or an internal note.
5. Select **Merge tickets**.

title: Split a message into a new ticket
aliases: break out a reply into its own ticket
separate a second issue from a ticket
create a new ticket from a comment
body:
The original ticket stays as it is and links to the new one.
1. Open the ticket and find the message that raises the separate issue.
2. Select the **More** menu on that message, then **Create ticket from message**.
3. Review the subject and requester on the new ticket.
4. Select **Create ticket**.

title: Close a ticket
body:
Closed tickets are locked. Use a follow-up ticket if the customer writes in again.
1. Open the ticket.
2. Select **Reply** or **Add note** if you want to leave a final message.
3. Open the **Submit as** menu and select **Closed**.
4. Select **Send** or **Add note**.

title: Reopen a closed ticket
aliases: customer wrote back on a closed ticket
body:
Tickets that have been closed for more than 60 days cannot be reopened. Create a follow-up ticket instead.
1. Search for the ticket and open it.
2. Select **Reopen ticket** at the top of the page.
3. Choose **Open** or **Pending** as the new status.
4. Select **Confirm**.

title: Delete a ticket
body:
Deleted tickets stay in **Deleted tickets** for 30 days, then are removed permanently.
1. Open the ticket.
2. Select the **More actions** menu.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete ticket** to confirm.

title: Restore a deleted ticket
aliases: get a ticket back from the bin
I deleted a ticket by mistake
body:
You can restore a ticket within 30 days of deleting it. After that it is gone permanently.
1. Go to **Tickets**, then select **Deleted tickets**.
2. Find the ticket in the list.
3. Select **Restore** next to it.

title: Export tickets to CSV
aliases: get a CSV of all tickets
body:
Only admins can export ticket data.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Data export**.
2. Select **Tickets**.
3. Choose a date range and the fields to include.
4. Select **Export to CSV**.
5. Open the email we send you and download the file within 48 hours.

title: Attach a file to a reply
aliases: add an attachment to a ticket
send a document to the customer
upload a file on a ticket
include a screenshot in a reply
body:
Each reply can include files up to 20 MB in total.
1. Open the ticket and select **Reply**.
2. Select the paperclip icon, or drag the file into the reply box.
3. Wait for the upload to finish.
4. Select **Send**.

title: Add a CC recipient to a ticket
aliases: copy someone in on a ticket
include another person in the email
cc a colleague of the customer
body:
CC recipients receive all public replies on the ticket until you remove them.
1. Open the ticket and select **Reply**.
2. Select **CC** above the message box.
3. Enter the email address of the person to copy in.
4. Select **Send**.

title: Follow a ticket
aliases: keep an eye on a ticket
body:
Followers receive an email each time the ticket is updated.
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select **Followers**.
3. Select **Add me**, or search for a colleague's name to add them.

title: Update several tickets at once
body:
You can update up to 100 tickets at a time.
1. Open a view from **Views** and tick the checkbox next to each ticket you want to change.
2. Select **Bulk edit** at the top of the list.
3. Change the **Status**, **Priority**, **Group** or **Assignee**.
4. Select **Submit**.

title: Set a due date on a ticket
aliases: add a deadline to a ticket
body:
Tickets past their due date show a red clock in views.
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select **Due date**.
3. Pick a date from the calendar.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Forward a ticket by email
aliases: send a ticket to someone outside Harbour Desk
email a ticket to a supplier
share a ticket with a third party
body:
A note is added to the ticket recording who it was forwarded to.
1. Open the ticket.
2. Select the **More actions** menu, then **Forward by email**.
3. Enter the recipient's address and edit the message if needed.
4. Select **Send**.

title: Link a ticket to a problem ticket
aliases: connect tickets to a known issue
body:
When you solve the problem ticket you can solve all linked tickets in one step.
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select **Link to problem**.
3. Search for the problem ticket by number or subject.
4. Select it, then select **Save**.

title: Change the requester on a ticket
aliases: switch who the ticket is from
body:
Future replies go to the new requester.
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select the name under **Requester**.
3. Select **Change requester** and search for the correct customer.
4. Select them, then select **Save**.

title: Add a new requester
body:
1. Go to **Requesters** in the left menu.
2. Select **Add requester**.
3. Enter the **Name** and **Email**.
4. Add a **Phone** number and **Organisation** if you have them.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Update a requester's phone number
aliases: new phone number for a customer
body:
1. Go to **Requesters** and search for the person.
2. Open their profile.
3. Select **Edit** beside **Phone**.
4. Enter the new number, including the area code.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Change a requester's primary email address
body:
The old address is kept as a secondary identity so existing tickets stay linked.
1. Go to **Requesters** and open the person's profile.
2. Select **Edit** in the **Contact details** panel.
3. Enter the new address in **Email**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Add a secondary email address to a requester
aliases: add another email for a customer
body:
Tickets sent from any of the person's addresses will be linked to this profile.
1. Open the requester's profile from **Requesters**.
2. Select **Add email** under **Contact details**.
3. Enter the additional address.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Delete a requester
body:
Their tickets are kept, but the requester name is shown as **Deleted user**.
1. Go to **Requesters** and open the person's profile.
2. Select the **More actions** menu.
3. Select **Delete requester**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.

title: Merge duplicate requesters
body:
Tickets and email addresses from the duplicate move to the profile you keep. This cannot be undone.
1. Open the profile you want to keep.
2. Select the **More actions** menu, then **Merge**.
3. Search for the duplicate requester and select them.
4. Select **Merge requesters**.

title: Import requesters from a CSV file
body:
The file must include an **Email** column. You will be emailed a summary when the import finishes.
1. Go to **Requesters**, then select **Import**.
2. Select **Choose file** and pick your CSV.
3. Match each column to a field, such as **Name** and **Email**.
4. Select **Start import**.

title: Export requesters to CSV
aliases: get all contacts in a spreadsheet
body:
Only admins can export requesters.
1. Go to **Requesters**.
2. Select **Export**.
3. Choose the fields to include.
4. Select **Export to CSV**, then download the file from the email we send you.

title: Add a note to a requester's profile
aliases: write a note on a customer
add a comment to a contact
body:
Notes appear next to every ticket from this person, and only agents can see them.
1. Open the requester's profile.
2. Select the **Notes** box in the side panel.
3. Type your note.
4. Select outside the box to save it.

title: Create an organisation
body:
1. Go to **Organisations** in the left menu.
2. Select **Add organisation**.
3. Enter the **Name**.
4. Add a **Domain**, **Address** and **Notes** if needed.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Add a requester to an organisation
aliases: put a customer in a company
assign a contact to an organisation
link a person to a client
body:
A requester can belong to one organisation at a time.
1. Open the requester's profile.
2. Select **Edit** beside **Organisation**.
3. Search for the organisation and select it.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Remove a requester from an organisation
aliases: take a customer out of a company
unlink a person from an organisation
body:
1. Open the requester's profile.
2. Select **Edit** beside **Organisation**.
3. Select the **x** next to the organisation name.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it. If you cannot see this option, ask an admin to check your role permissions.

title: Rename an organisation
body:
Existing tickets show the new name straight away.
1. Go to **Organisations** and open the organisation.
2. Select **Edit** at the top of the profile.
3. Change the **Name**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Delete an organisation
body:
Its requesters are kept but no longer belong to an organisation.
1. Go to **Organisations** and open the organisation.
2. Select the **More actions** menu.
3. Select **Delete organisation**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.

title: Assign requesters to an organisation by email domain
aliases: match contacts to companies by email
body:
Only new requesters are matched. Existing requesters stay as they are.
1. Open the organisation from **Organisations**.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Enter the email domain, for example **example.com.au**, in **Domains**.
4. Tick **Add new requesters automatically**.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Block a requester
body:
Emails from blocked requesters do not create tickets. To undo this, select **Unblock requester** from the same menu.
1. Open the requester's profile.
2. Select the **More actions** menu.
3. Select **Block requester**.
4. Select **Block** to confirm.

title: View a requester's ticket history
aliases: see all tickets from a customer
body:
1. Go to **Requesters** and open the person's profile.
2. Select the **Tickets** tab.
3. Use the **Status** filter to show open, solved or all tickets.
4. Select a ticket to open it.

title: Set a requester's language and time zone
body:
Automatic replies and due dates use these settings.
1. Open the requester's profile.
2. Select **Edit** in the **Contact details** panel.
3. Choose a **Language** and **Time zone** from the lists.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Set an organisation's billing contact
aliases: change the primary contact for a company
body:
The billing contact is shown at the top of the organisation profile.
1. Open the organisation from **Organisations**.
2. Select the **Requesters** tab.
3. Select the **More** menu beside the person.
4. Select **Set as billing contact**.

title: Update an organisation's address
body:
1. Go to **Organisations** and open the organisation.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Update the **Address** field.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it. If you cannot see this option, ask an admin to check your role permissions.

title: Create a view
body:
Your new view appears in the **Views** list straight away.
1. Go to **Views** and select **Add view**.
2. Enter a **Title**.
3. Under **Conditions**, add the rules, such as **Status is Open** and **Group is Billing**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Edit a view
body:
1. Go to **Views** and hover over the view.
2. Select the pencil icon.
3. Change the **Title**, **Conditions** or **Columns**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Delete a view
aliases: get rid of a saved list
body:
Deleting a view does not delete any of the tickets in it.
1. Go to **Views** and hover over the view.
2. Select the pencil icon.
3. Select **Delete view**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.

title: Share a view with a group
aliases: make a view available to my team
body:
Choose **All agents** to share the view with everyone. Only admins can share views with all agents.
1. Go to **Views** and open the view's edit page.
2. Under **Available to**, choose **Group** and select the group.
3. Select **Save**.

title: Change the order of views
aliases: put a view at the top
body:
1. Go to **Views** and select **Manage views**.
2. Drag a view by the handle on its left.
3. Drop it where you want it.
4. Select **Save order**.

title: Add a column to a view
aliases: show another field in a ticket list
body:
Drag columns to change their order.
1. Go to **Views** and open the view's edit page.
2. Under **Columns**, select **Add column**.
3. Choose the field, such as **Organisation** or **Priority**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Change how a view is sorted
body:
To keep a sort order every time, set **Order by** on the view's edit page.
1. Go to **Views** and open the view.
2. Select a column heading, such as **Updated**, to sort by it.
3. Select the heading again to switch between ascending and descending.

title: Export a view to CSV
aliases: save a ticket list as a spreadsheet
body:
The file includes the columns shown in the view, up to 5,000 tickets.
1. Go to **Views** and open the view.
2. Select the **More actions** menu.
3. Select **Export to CSV**.
4. Download the file from the email we send you.

title: Search tickets by keyword
body:
1. Select the **Search** box at the top of the screen.
2. Type a word or phrase from the subject or message.
3. Press **Enter**.
4. Select **Tickets** to see ticket results only.

title: Search for tickets from an email address
body:
1. Select the **Search** box.
2. Type **requester:** followed by the email address, for example **requester:sam@example.com.au**.
3. Press **Enter**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it. If you cannot see this option, ask an admin to check your role permissions.

title: Search tickets by date range
body:
1. Select the **Search** box and enter your keywords, if any.
2. Select **Filters** on the results page.
3. Choose **Created** or **Updated**, then pick **From** and **To** dates.
4. Select **Apply**.

title: Save a search as a view
aliases: turn a search into a view
body:
The new view appears under **My views** and updates as tickets change.
1. Run your search and set any filters.
2. Select **Save as view** above the results.
3. Enter a **Title**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Search tickets by tag
body:
Add a minus sign before the word, such as **-tags:refund**, to leave those tickets out.
1. Select the **Search** box.
2. Type **tags:** followed by the tag, for example **tags:refund**.
3. Press **Enter**.

title: Search tickets by status
body:
Use **status<solved** to find tickets that are not yet solved.
1. Select the **Search** box.
2. Type **status:** followed by the status, for example **status:pending**.
3. Press **Enter**.

title: Search for an exact phrase
body:
Without quotation marks, results include tickets containing any of the words.
1. Select the **Search** box.
2. Type your phrase inside double quotation marks, for example **"refund request"**.
3. Press **Enter**.

title: Search for an organisation
body:
1. Select the **Search** box at the top of the screen.
2. Type the organisation's name or domain.
3. Press **Enter**, then select **Organisations**.
4. Select the organisation to open it.

title: Search for a requester by phone number
body:
Phone numbers must match exactly, so try the number with and without the leading zero if you get no results.
1. Go to **Requesters**.
2. Select the search box above the list.
3. Enter the phone number without spaces.
4. Press **Enter**.

title: Clear your recent searches
body:
This only affects your own search history.
1. Select the **Search** box.
2. Select **Clear recent searches** below the list.
3. Select **Clear** to confirm.

title: Set your default view
body:
1. Select your profile picture, then **Preferences**.
2. Under **Agent workspace**, find **Default view**.
3. Choose a view from the list.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Duplicate a view
aliases: make a copy of a view
base a new view on an existing one
body:
1. Go to **Views** and hover over the view.
2. Select the pencil icon.
3. Select **Clone**.
4. Rename the copy, adjust the conditions if needed, then select **Save**.

title: Add a tag to a ticket
aliases: put a keyword on a ticket
body:
Tags are lower case and cannot contain spaces. Use hyphens instead.
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select the **Tags** field.
3. Type a tag and press **Enter**. Repeat for more tags.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Remove a tag from a ticket
aliases: delete a tag from one ticket
body:
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, find the **Tags** field.
3. Select the **x** next to the tag.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Rename a tag
body:
Every ticket with the old tag is updated.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Tags**.
2. Find the tag in the list.
3. Select **Rename**.
4. Enter the new name and select **Save**.

title: Delete a tag
aliases: erase a label from all tickets
body:
The tag is removed from all tickets that use it.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Tags**.
2. Find the tag in the list.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete tag** to confirm.

title: Add a tag to many tickets at once
body:
1. Open a view or search results.
2. Tick the checkbox next to each ticket.
3. Select **Bulk edit**, then **Add tags**.
4. Enter the tag and select **Submit**.

title: See how often each tag is used
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Tags**.
2. Read the **Tickets** column to see how many tickets use each tag.
3. Select a column heading to sort the list.
4. Select a tag name to open a search for its tickets.

title: Set the priority on a ticket
aliases: mark a ticket as high priority
body:
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select the **Priority** field.
3. Choose **Low**, **Normal**, **High** or **Urgent**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Escalate a ticket to urgent
body:
Urgent tickets appear at the top of the **Urgent now** view.
1. Open the ticket.
2. Set **Priority** to **Urgent** in the **Properties** panel.
3. Select **Add note** and explain why the ticket is urgent.
4. Mention your team lead with @ and their name.
5. Select **Add note**.

title: Change the default priority for new tickets
body:
This applies to new tickets created by email or the web form.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Settings**, then **Tickets**.
2. Find **Default priority**.
3. Choose **Low** or **Normal**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Rename a priority level
body:
Only the display name changes. Search still uses the original name.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Settings**, then **Priorities**.
2. Select **Edit** beside the priority.
3. Enter the new **Display name**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Change a ticket's status
aliases: move a ticket to another status
body:
1. Open the ticket.
2. Select the arrow beside the **Submit** button.
3. Choose the status, such as **Open** or **Pending**.
4. Select **Submit**.

title: Create a custom status
aliases: new status like waiting on supplier
body:
The category decides how the status behaves in reports and automations.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Settings**, then **Statuses**.
2. Select **Add status**.
3. Enter a **Name** and choose a **Category**, such as **Pending** or **On hold**.
4. Pick a colour.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Edit a custom status
body:
Standard statuses such as **Open** and **Closed** cannot be renamed.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Settings**, then **Statuses**.
2. Select **Edit** beside the status.
3. Change the **Name** or **Description**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Delete a custom status
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Settings**, then **Statuses**.
2. Select **Delete** beside the custom status.
3. Choose a replacement status for tickets that currently use it.
4. Select **Delete status**.

title: Put a ticket on hold
body:
Use on hold when you are waiting on someone inside your organisation. Use **Pending** when you are waiting on the customer.
1. Open the ticket.
2. Select the arrow beside the **Submit** button.
3. Choose **On hold**.
4. Select **Submit**.

title: Set a ticket to pending
body:
If the customer replies, the ticket changes back to **Open** automatically.
1. Open the ticket and select **Reply**.
2. Write your message asking for more information.
3. Select the arrow beside **Submit** and choose **Pending**.
4. Select **Send**.

title: Mark a ticket as solved
body:
Solved tickets close automatically after the period set in **Settings**.
1. Open the ticket.
2. Write a final reply if needed.
3. Select the arrow beside **Submit** and choose **Solved**.
4. Select **Send**.

title: Change when solved tickets close automatically
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Settings**, then **Tickets**.
2. Find **Close solved tickets after**.
3. Enter a number of days between 1 and 28.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Add tags automatically based on keywords
aliases: set up a rule to label tickets
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Automations**, then **Triggers**.
2. Select **Add trigger** and enter a name.
3. Under **Conditions**, choose **Subject or description contains** and enter the keyword.
4. Under **Actions**, choose **Add tags** and enter the tag.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Change the colour of a status
aliases: make statuses easier to tell apart
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Settings**, then **Statuses**.
2. Select **Edit** beside the status.
3. Select the **Colour** swatch and choose a new colour.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Create a macro
body:
A macro applies several changes to a ticket in one click.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Select **Add macro**.
3. Enter a **Title** that agents will recognise.
4. Under **Actions**, add the actions you want, such as **Comment text** or **Set status**.
5. Select **Create**.

title: Edit a macro
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Find the macro and select **Edit**.
3. Change the **Title** or **Actions**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it. If you cannot see this option, ask an admin to check your role permissions.

title: Delete a macro
body:
Tickets already updated by the macro are not affected.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Select the **More** menu beside the macro.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete macro** to confirm.

title: Apply a macro to a ticket
body:
1. Open the ticket.
2. Select **Apply macro** below the reply box.
3. Search for the macro or pick it from the list.
4. Check the reply and properties it fills in, edit as needed, then select **Submit**.

title: Apply a macro to several tickets
aliases: use a macro on multiple tickets
body:
Macros that add a public reply send it to every requester.
1. Open a view and tick the checkbox next to each ticket.
2. Select **Bulk edit**, then **Apply macro**.
3. Choose the macro.
4. Select **Submit**.

title: Make a macro available to all agents
body:
To share with one team only, choose **Group** instead.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Select **Edit** beside the macro.
3. Under **Available for**, choose **All agents**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Create a personal macro
aliases: make a macro just for me
body:
Only you can see and use a personal macro.
1. Select your profile picture, then **My macros**.
2. Select **Add macro**.
3. Enter a **Title** and add your actions.
4. Select **Create**.

title: Add the requester's name to a macro
body:
The placeholder is replaced with the customer's first name when the macro is applied.
1. Open the macro from **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. In the **Comment text** action, place your cursor where the name should appear.
3. Type **{{ticket.requester.first_name}}**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Set a status in a macro
body:
1. Open the macro from **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Under **Actions**, select **Add action**.
3. Choose **Set status** and pick the status, such as **Solved**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Add a tag in a macro
aliases: put a tag action in a macro
body:
1. Open the macro from **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Select **Add action**.
3. Choose **Add tags** and enter the tag.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Deactivate a macro
body:
Deactivated macros are kept under **Inactive** and can be turned back on with **Activate**.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Select the **More** menu beside the macro.
3. Select **Deactivate**.

title: Duplicate a macro
aliases: reuse a macro as a template
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Select the **More** menu beside the macro.
3. Select **Clone**.
4. Rename the copy and select **Create**.

title: Organise macros into categories
body:
Macros with the same category name appear together in the **Apply macro** list.
1. Open the macro from **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. In the **Title** field, type a category name followed by two colons, then the macro name, for example **Billing::Refund approved**.
3. Select **Save**.

title: Find a macro
body:
Inside a ticket, select **Apply macro** and type in the search box to find it.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Type part of the macro's title in the search box.
3. Select **Edit** to view its actions.

title: Save a canned reply
body:
Unlike macros, canned replies only insert text and do not change ticket properties.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Canned replies**.
2. Select **Add canned reply**.
3. Enter a **Name** and the **Message**.
4. Choose who it is **Available to**.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Insert a canned reply into a ticket
body:
1. Open the ticket and select **Reply**.
2. Select the **Canned replies** icon above the message box, or type **/** in the box.
3. Search for the reply and select it.
4. Edit the text if needed, then select **Send**.

title: Edit a canned reply
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Canned replies**.
2. Select the reply's name.
3. Change the **Name** or **Message**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it. If you cannot see this option, ask an admin to check your role permissions.

title: Delete a canned reply
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Canned replies**.
2. Select the **More** menu beside the reply.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete reply** to confirm.

title: Add an attachment to a macro
aliases: send a file with a macro
attach a document to a macro
include a PDF in a macro
body:
Files can be up to 7 MB. The file is attached to the public reply when the macro is applied.
1. Open the macro from **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Under **Actions**, select **Add action**, then **Attachment**.
3. Select **Upload file** and choose the file.
4. Select **Save**.

title: See how often a macro is used
body:
Macros that are never used are good candidates for deactivating.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Select **Usage** at the top of the list.
3. Choose a period, such as **Last 30 days**.
4. Sort by **Times used** to see the most popular macros.

title: Invite a new agent
aliases: send an invite to a new team member
body:
Only admins can invite agents.

1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Agents**.
2. Select **Invite agent**.
3. Enter the agent's name and work email address.
4. Choose a **Role**, then select a **Team** if you want to add them straight away.
5. Select **Send invite**.

The invite link expires after 7 days. You can resend it from the agent's row.

title: Update an agent's phone number
aliases: fix phone number on agent profile
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Agents**.
2. Select the agent's name to open their profile.
3. Select **Edit profile**.
4. Enter the new number in the **Phone** field.
5. Select **Save changes**.

Agents can also update their own number from **My profile**.

title: Change an agent's email address
aliases: edit the login email for an agent
body:
Changing the email also changes the address the agent uses to sign in.

1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Agents**.
2. Open the agent's profile.
3. Select **Edit profile**.
4. Replace the address in the **Email** field.
5. Select **Save changes**.
6. Ask the agent to confirm the new address using the link we send.

title: Deactivate an agent
body:
Deactivating an agent stops them signing in but keeps their ticket history.

1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Agents**.
2. Select the agent's name.
3. Select **More actions** > **Deactivate agent**.
4. Choose who should receive their open tickets.
5. Select **Deactivate**.

title: Reactivate a deactivated agent
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Agents**.
2. Select the **Deactivated** filter.
3. Open the agent's profile.
4. Select **More actions** > **Reactivate agent**.
5. Confirm their **Role** and **Team**, then select **Reactivate**.

The agent will receive an email asking them to set a new password.

title: Create a team
aliases: set up a new support team
start a team for billing queries
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Teams**.
2. Select **New team**.
3. Enter a **Team name** and an optional description.
4. Choose the agents to include.
5. Select **Create team**.

Teams can be used as assignment targets in routing rules and reports.

title: Add an agent to a team
aliases: put an agent in a team
add a member to a team
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Teams**.
2. Select the team's name.
3. Select **Add members**.
4. Tick the agents you want to add.
5. Select **Add to team**.

An agent can belong to more than one team.

title: Remove an agent from a team
aliases: take someone out of a team
kick an agent out of a group
agent no longer on this team
body:
Removing an agent from a team does not deactivate their account.

1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Teams**.
2. Select the team's name.
3. Find the agent in the **Members** list.
4. Select **Remove** next to their name.
5. Select **Confirm**.

title: Rename a team
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Teams**.
2. Select the team you want to rename.
3. Select **Edit team**.
4. Type the new name in **Team name**.
5. Select **Save changes**.

Existing routing rules and reports will pick up the new name automatically.

title: Delete a team
body:
Deleting a team does not delete its agents or their tickets.

1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Teams**.
2. Select the team's name.
3. Select **More actions** > **Delete team**.
4. Choose a team to receive any tickets still assigned to this one.
5. Select **Delete team**.

title: Change an agent's role
body:
Roles control what an agent can see and change. The built-in roles are **Agent**, **Supervisor** and **Admin**.

1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Agents**.
2. Open the agent's profile.
3. Select **Edit profile**.
4. Pick a new option from the **Role** list.
5. Select **Save changes**.

title: Create a custom role
aliases: build a role with limited access
body:
1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Roles**.
2. Select **New role**.
3. Name the role, for example **Billing specialist**.
4. Switch on the permissions this role needs, such as **View reports** or **Edit knowledge base**.
5. Select **Save role**.

You can then choose the new role when you invite or edit an agent.

title: Set your availability status
body:
Your status decides whether new tickets and chats can be assigned to you.

1. Select your profile picture at the top right.
2. Select the current status, such as **Available**.
3. Choose **Away**, **Busy** or **Offline**.
4. Optionally add a note, such as "Back at 2pm".

Select **Available** again when you return.

title: Add an email signature to your profile
aliases: sign off replies with my name
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Select your profile picture, then **My profile**.
2. Open the **Signature** tab.
3. Type your signature in the editor. You can use bold text and line breaks.
4. Select **Save**.

Your signature is added to email replies you send from the **Inbox**.

title: Set a maximum number of open tickets for an agent
aliases: stop an agent getting too many tickets
body:
Once an agent reaches the limit, automatic assignment skips them.

1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Agents**.
2. Open the agent's profile.
3. Select **Workload**.
4. Enter a number in **Maximum open tickets**.
5. Select **Save changes**.

Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

title: Export your agent list to CSV
aliases: download all agents as a spreadsheet
get a list of agents in Excel
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Agents**.
2. Use the filters if you only need some agents, for example a **Team**.
3. Select **Export**.
4. Choose **CSV** and select **Download**.

The file includes name, email, phone, role, team and status.

title: Add an internal note to an agent's profile
aliases: leave a note about an agent
write a note on a team member
record training notes for an agent
add a comment to agent record
body:
Notes on a profile are visible to admins and supervisors only.

1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Agents**.
2. Open the agent's profile.
3. Select the **Notes** tab.
4. Type your note in the box.
5. Select **Add note**.

Changes are saved straight away.

title: Create an SLA policy
aliases: set up a service level agreement
make an SLA for premium customers
body:
An SLA policy sets the time targets your team works to.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Service levels** > **SLAs**.
2. Select **New SLA policy**.
3. Enter a **Policy name**.
4. Under **Applies to**, add conditions such as **Customer plan** is **Premium**.
5. Set your targets, then select **Save policy**.

title: Edit an SLA policy
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Service levels** > **SLAs**.
2. Select the policy name.
3. Change the conditions or targets.
4. Select **Save policy**.

Changes apply to new tickets. Tickets already open keep their original targets unless you select **Apply to open tickets**.

title: Delete an SLA policy
aliases: get rid of a service level policy
body:
Tickets that used the policy keep their breach history in reports.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Service levels** > **SLAs**.
2. Select the **More** menu on the policy's row.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Confirm**.

title: Duplicate an SLA policy
aliases: make a copy of an existing SLA
reuse an SLA as a template
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Service levels** > **SLAs**.
2. Select the **More** menu on the policy you want to copy.
3. Select **Duplicate**.
4. Rename the copy and adjust its conditions.
5. Select **Save policy**.

The copy is created switched off until you turn it on.

title: Set a first response target
aliases: how fast should we first reply
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Service levels** > **SLAs** and open a policy.
2. Find the **First response time** section.
3. Enter a time for each priority: **Low**, **Normal**, **High** and **Urgent**.
4. Choose **Business hours** or **Calendar hours**.
5. Select **Save policy**.

title: Set a resolution target
aliases: how long to solve a ticket
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Service levels** > **SLAs** and open a policy.
2. Find the **Resolution time** section.
3. Enter a target time for each priority.
4. Select **Business hours** or **Calendar hours** under **Count time by**.
5. Select **Save policy**.

title: Use different SLA targets for each priority
aliases: set shorter targets for urgent tickets
body:
A single policy can hold a separate target for every priority level.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Service levels** > **SLAs** and open a policy.
2. Select **Different targets per priority**.
3. Enter first response and resolution times for **Low**, **Normal**, **High** and **Urgent**.
4. Select **Save policy**.

title: Create a business hours schedule
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Service levels** > **Business hours**.
2. Select **New schedule**.
3. Name the schedule, for example **Sydney weekdays**.
4. Choose a **Time zone**.
5. Set opening and closing times for each day, then select **Save schedule**.

title: Edit business hours
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Service levels** > **Business hours**.
2. Select the schedule you want to change.
3. Adjust the times for the days affected, or switch a day off with the **Open** toggle.
4. Select **Save schedule**.

SLA clocks use the new hours straight away.

title: Change the time zone of a schedule
aliases: wrong time zone on business hours
switch schedule to another time zone
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Service levels** > **Business hours**.
2. Select the schedule.
3. Open the **Time zone** list and choose the correct one.
4. Select **Save schedule**.

Opening times stay the same in the new time zone, so check them after you save.

title: Add a holiday to a schedule
aliases: mark a public holiday as closed
body:
Tickets received on a holiday do not count against SLA targets.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Service levels** > **Business hours**.
2. Select the schedule.
3. Open the **Holidays** tab and select **Add holiday**.
4. Enter a name and choose the date or date range.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Delete a holiday from a schedule
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Service levels** > **Business hours**.
2. Select the schedule and open the **Holidays** tab.
3. Select the **Delete** icon next to the holiday.
4. Select **Confirm**.

Changes are saved straight away.

title: Assign a business hours schedule to a team
aliases: use different hours for a team
apply opening hours to a team
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Go to **Admin** > **People** > **Teams**.
2. Select the team's name.
3. Select **Edit team**.
4. Choose a schedule from the **Business hours** list.
5. Select **Save changes**.

title: Pause the SLA clock while waiting for the customer
body:
When a ticket is set to **Pending**, you can stop the clock so waiting time is not counted against your team.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Service levels** > **SLAs**.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Switch on **Pause SLA when status is Pending**.
4. Select **Save**.

The clock restarts when the customer replies.

title: Send an alert before an SLA is breached
aliases: warn me about tickets about to breach
body:
1. Go to **Admin** > **Service levels** > **SLAs** and open a policy.
2. Select **Alerts**.
3. Choose how long before the target the alert is sent, for example **30 minutes**.
4. Pick who to notify: the **Assignee**, the **Team supervisor** or both.
5. Select **Save policy**.

title: See tickets at risk of breaching their SLA
aliases: which tickets are about to be late
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Go to **Inbox**.
2. Select the **Views** menu.
3. Choose **At risk of SLA breach**.
4. Sort by **Time remaining** to see the most urgent first.

Breached tickets appear in red. Changes are saved straight away.

title: Export your holiday list to CSV
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Service levels** > **Business hours**.
2. Select the schedule and open the **Holidays** tab.
3. Select **Export**.
4. Select **Download CSV**.

The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

title: Create a knowledge base article
aliases: add an article to the knowledge base
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Go to **Knowledge base**.
2. Select **New article**.
3. Enter a **Title** and write the content in the editor.
4. Choose a **Category**.
5. Select **Save draft** to keep it private, or **Publish** to make it live.

title: Edit a knowledge base article
aliases: fix a typo in an article
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Go to **Knowledge base**.
2. Search for the article or browse to its category.
3. Select the article, then **Edit**.
4. Make your changes in the editor.
5. Select **Save**.

Published articles update straight away.

title: Delete a knowledge base article
aliases: take down an article for good
body:
Deleted articles can be restored from the **Trash** for 30 days. To hide an article without deleting it, unpublish it instead.

1. Go to **Knowledge base**.
2. Open the article.
3. Select **More actions** > **Delete**.
4. Select **Move to Trash**.

Changes are saved straight away.

title: Publish a draft article
aliases: go live with a help article
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Go to **Knowledge base** and select the **Drafts** tab.
2. Open the article.
3. Check the content and **Category**.
4. Select **Publish**.

Customers can find the article in the help centre straight away.

title: Unpublish an article
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Go to **Knowledge base**.
2. Open the published article.
3. Select **More actions** > **Unpublish**.
4. Select **Confirm**.

The article moves back to **Drafts**, and keeps its content and history.

title: Schedule an article to publish later
aliases: publish an article at a set time
set a go-live date for an article
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Go to **Knowledge base** and open a draft.
2. Select the arrow next to **Publish**.
3. Choose **Schedule**.
4. Pick a date and time.
5. Select **Schedule article**.

title: Create a knowledge base category
aliases: set up a folder for articles
make a new help topic section
add a section to the help centre
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Go to **Knowledge base** > **Categories**.
2. Select **New category**.
3. Enter a **Name** and a short description.
4. Select **Save**.

Changes are saved straight away.

title: Rename a knowledge base category
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Go to **Knowledge base** > **Categories**.
2. Select **Edit** next to the category.
3. Type the new **Name**.
4. Select **Save**.

The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

title: Delete a knowledge base category
aliases: get rid of a help section
body:
A category must be empty before it can be deleted.

1. Go to **Knowledge base** > **Categories**.
2. Move or delete any articles inside it.
3. Select **More** next to the category.
4. Select **Delete category**.

Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

title: Move an article to another category
aliases: put article in a different folder
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Go to **Knowledge base**.
2. Open the article.
3. Select **Edit**.
4. Choose a new option from the **Category** list.
5. Select **Save**.

If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role. Changes are saved straight away.

title: Add an image to an article
aliases: insert a screenshot into a help article
upload a picture to an article
put a photo in the knowledge base
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Open the article and select **Edit**.
2. Place the cursor where you want the image.
3. Select **Insert** > **Image**.
4. Upload a file from your computer. Images up to 5 MB are supported.
5. Add **Alt text**, then select **Save**.

title: Make an article visible to agents only
aliases: hide article from customers but keep it for staff
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Go to **Knowledge base** and open the article.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Open the **Visibility** list.
4. Choose **Agents only**.
5. Select **Save**.

Agents can still find it when replying to tickets.

title: Restore a previous version of an article
aliases: go back to an earlier version
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Go to **Knowledge base** and open the article.
2. Select **History**.
3. Choose the version you want from the list.
4. Select **Restore this version**.
5. Select **Confirm**.

Restoring creates a new version, so no history is lost.

title: Add a translation to an article
aliases: make an article available in another language
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Go to **Knowledge base** and open the article.
2. Select **Translations**.
3. Select **Add translation** and choose a language.
4. Enter the translated title and content.
5. Select **Publish translation**.

title: Add an internal note to an article
aliases: leave a comment on an article
write a reminder on a help article
body:
Notes are only visible to agents with permission to edit the knowledge base.

1. Open the article in **Knowledge base**.
2. Select **Notes** in the side panel.
3. Type your note.
4. Select **Add note**.

Changes are saved straight away.

title: Export knowledge base articles to CSV
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Go to **Knowledge base**.
2. Use the **Category** and **Status** filters if you only need some articles.
3. Select **Export**.
4. Choose **CSV** and select **Download**.

The file lists titles, categories, status and last updated date.

title: Insert a knowledge base article into a reply
aliases: send a help article to a customer
link an article in my response
share an FAQ in a ticket reply
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Open the ticket in your **Inbox**.
2. Select **Reply**.
3. Select the **Articles** icon in the editor toolbar.
4. Search for the article and select **Insert link**.
5. Select **Send**.

title: Add the chat widget to your website
aliases: put the chat button on my site
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Live chat**.
2. Select **Widget**, then **Install**.
3. Copy the code snippet.
4. Paste it just before the closing body tag on every page where you want chat to appear.
5. Select **Verify installation**.

title: Change the chat widget colour
aliases: change the colour of live chat
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Live chat** > **Widget**.
2. Select **Appearance**.
3. Enter a hex code in **Accent colour**, or choose from the picker.
4. Select **Save**.

The preview on the right shows how the widget will look.

title: Edit the chat welcome message
aliases: set what customers see when chat opens
write an opening message for live chat
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Live chat** > **Widget**.
2. Select **Messages**.
3. Edit the text in **Welcome message**.
4. Select **Save**.

The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

title: Show an offline message when no agents are available
aliases: what customers see after hours in chat
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Live chat** > **Widget**.
2. Select **Messages**.
3. Edit the text in **Offline message**.
4. Switch on **Let visitors leave a message** if you want to collect an email address.
5. Select **Save**.

Messages left offline become tickets.

title: Set up a pre-chat form
aliases: ask for name and email before chat
collect details before starting a chat
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Live chat** > **Widget**.
2. Select **Pre-chat form**.
3. Switch on the fields you want to ask for, such as **Name**, **Email** and **Topic**.
4. Mark any field as **Required**.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Transfer a chat to another agent or team
aliases: pass a live chat to someone else
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Open the chat from your **Inbox**.
2. Select **Transfer**.
3. Choose an **Agent** or a **Team**.
4. Add a short note explaining the context.
5. Select **Transfer chat**.

Changes are saved straight away.

title: End a live chat
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Open the chat from your **Inbox**.
2. Select **End chat**.
3. Select **End chat** again to confirm.

The customer sees a message that the chat has finished, and the conversation stays in the ticket history.

title: Send a chat transcript to a customer
aliases: email a copy of the chat
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Open the finished chat from your **Inbox**.
2. Select **More actions** > **Send transcript**.
3. Check the customer's email address.
4. Select **Send**.

You can also switch on **Send transcript automatically** in the live chat settings.

title: Create a saved reply for chat
aliases: add a shortcut for common answers
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Live chat** > **Saved replies**.
2. Select **New saved reply**.
3. Enter a **Shortcut**, such as /refund.
4. Type the message text.
5. Select **Save**.

Agents type the shortcut in a chat to insert the message.

title: Delete a saved reply
aliases: get rid of a quick reply
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Live chat** > **Saved replies**.
2. Find the reply using the search box.
3. Select the **Delete** icon.
4. Select **Confirm**.

Changes are saved straight away.

title: Block a chat visitor
aliases: prevent a person from starting chats
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Open the chat with the visitor.
2. Select **More actions** > **Block visitor**.
3. Choose **Block by email** or **Block by IP address**.
4. Select **Block**.

To undo this, go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Live chat** > **Blocked visitors** and select **Unblock**.

title: Set how many chats an agent can handle at once
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Live chat** > **Routing**.
2. Enter a number in **Maximum concurrent chats**.
3. Select **Save**.

Agents at their limit will not be offered new chats until one ends.

title: Convert a chat into a ticket
aliases: turn a chat into a ticket
follow up on a chat later by email
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Open the chat from your **Inbox**.
2. Select **More actions** > **Convert to ticket**.
3. Set the **Priority** and **Assignee**.
4. Select **Create ticket**.

If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role. Changes are saved straight away.

title: Allow customers to send files in chat
aliases: let customers upload attachments in chat
turn on file sharing in live chat
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Live chat** > **Widget**.
2. Select **Features**.
3. Switch on **File uploads**.
4. Choose the maximum file size.
5. Select **Save**.

Changes are saved straight away.

title: Turn on desktop notifications for new chats
aliases: get a sound when a chat arrives
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Select your profile picture, then **My profile**.
2. Open the **Notifications** tab.
3. Switch on **New chat** under **Desktop**.
4. Allow notifications when your browser asks.

You can choose a sound in the same section.

title: Ask customers to rate a chat
aliases: enable thumbs up and down rating
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Live chat** > **Widget**.
2. Select **Features**.
3. Switch on **Satisfaction rating**.
4. Edit the rating question if you wish.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Connect a support email address
aliases: link a mailbox to Harbour Desk
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Email**.
2. Select **Add email address**.
3. Enter the address, for example support@yourcompany.com.
4. Choose the **Default team** to receive tickets.
5. Select **Save**, then follow the forwarding instructions shown.

title: Forward emails to Harbour Desk
aliases: forward support emails to the helpdesk address
body:
1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Email** and open your address.
2. Copy the **Forwarding address**.
3. In your email provider's settings, create a forwarding rule to that address.
4. Return to Desk and select **Send test email**.

The status changes to **Connected** once the test email arrives.

title: Verify your sending domain
body:
Verifying your domain helps customers receive your replies in their inbox.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Email** > **Domains**.
2. Select **Add domain** and enter your domain name.
3. Copy the DNS records shown.
4. Add them with your domain provider.
5. Select **Verify**.

title: Set the default email signature for a channel
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Email** and open the address.
2. Select **Signature**.
3. Edit the text in the editor. Use **{{agent.name}}** to include the agent's name.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Turn on the automatic acknowledgement email
aliases: send a confirmation when a ticket is received
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Email** > **Auto-replies**.
2. Switch on **Acknowledge new tickets**.
3. Edit the **Subject** and message.
4. Select **Save**.

The message is sent once, when a customer first emails you.

title: Update a customer's phone number
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Go to **Customers**.
2. Search for the customer and open their record.
3. Select **Edit**.
4. Enter the new number in **Phone**.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Add a customer
aliases: add a client to the helpdesk
body:
Customers are usually created automatically when they email you. You can also add one yourself.

1. Go to **Customers**.
2. Select **New customer**.
3. Enter the **Name** and **Email**. Phone and **Organisation** are optional.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Delete a customer record
aliases: delete a requester and their data
get rid of a client record
body:
Deleting a customer also removes their tickets after 30 days. This cannot be undone once that period has passed.

1. Go to **Customers**.
2. Open the customer's record.
3. Select **More actions** > **Delete customer**.
4. Type **DELETE** to confirm.
5. Select **Delete**.

Changes are saved straight away.

title: Block an email sender
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Open a ticket from the sender.
2. Select **More actions** > **Block sender**.
3. Choose **This address** or **Entire domain**.
4. Select **Block**.

Future emails from them are discarded and no tickets are created.

title: Restore a ticket from spam
aliases: rescue a real email from spam
move ticket out of spam folder
recover a ticket wrongly marked as spam
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Go to **Inbox** > **Spam**.
2. Open the ticket.
3. Select **Not spam**.
4. Select **Confirm**.

The ticket returns to the **New** view and the sender is allowed to email you again.

title: Route emails to a team by address
aliases: send emails from sales@ to a certain team
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Go to **Admin** > **Channels** > **Email** > **Routing**.
2. Select **New rule**.
3. Under **If**, choose **Recipient address** is the address you want.
4. Under **Then**, choose **Assign to team** and pick the team.
5. Select **Save rule**.

title: Add a private note to a ticket
aliases: leave an internal comment on a ticket
write a note only agents see
body:
Private notes are never sent to the customer.

1. Open the ticket in your **Inbox**.
2. Select **Add note** above the reply box.
3. Type your note. Use @ to mention a colleague.
4. Select **Save note**.

title: View the reports dashboard
aliases: check how the team is doing
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Select **Reports** in the left menu.
2. Open **Overview**.
3. Use the **Date range** list at the top to choose a period.
4. Scroll to see ticket volume, response times and satisfaction.

title: Create a custom report
aliases: make a new report with chosen metrics
set up a custom analytics report
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Go to **Reports** > **Custom reports**.
2. Select **New report**.
3. Choose a **Metric**, such as **Tickets created**, and a **Group by** option.
4. Add any filters.
5. Select **Save report** and give it a name.

title: Duplicate a report
aliases: make a version of an existing report
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Go to **Reports** > **Custom reports**.
2. Select the **More** menu on the report.
3. Select **Duplicate**.
4. Rename the copy and adjust its filters.
5. Select **Save report**.

title: Delete a custom report
aliases: get rid of a saved report
body:
Deleting a report also removes any schedules attached to it.

1. Go to **Reports** > **Custom reports**.
2. Select the **More** menu on the report.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Confirm**.

Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

title: Export a report to CSV
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Go to **Reports** and open the report.
2. Set the **Date range** and any filters.
3. Select **Export**.
4. Choose **CSV** and select **Download**.

If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role. Changes are saved straight away.

title: Schedule a report by email
aliases: email me this report every Monday
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Go to **Reports** and open the report.
2. Select **Schedule**.
3. Choose how often it is sent: **Daily**, **Weekly** or **Monthly**.
4. Enter the recipients' email addresses.
5. Select **Save schedule**.

title: Share a report with a colleague
aliases: give someone access to a report
let a supervisor see my report
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Go to **Reports** and open the report.
2. Select **Share**.
3. Enter the name of an agent or team.
4. Choose **Can view** or **Can edit**.
5. Select **Share**.

title: Change the date range of a report
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Open any report in **Reports**.
2. Select the **Date range** list at the top.
3. Choose a preset, such as **Last 30 days**, or select **Custom**.
4. Select **Apply**.

title: Filter a report by team
aliases: only see my team in reports
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Open any report in **Reports**.
2. Select **Filters** > **Team**.
3. Tick one or more teams.
4. Select **Apply**.

Changes are saved straight away.

title: View agent performance
aliases: how many tickets did each agent solve
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Go to **Reports** > **Agents**.
2. Choose a **Date range**.
3. Review tickets solved, average first response time and satisfaction for each agent.
4. Select an agent's name for a detailed breakdown.

title: View customer satisfaction results
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Go to **Reports** > **Satisfaction**.
2. Choose a **Date range**.
3. See the overall score and the split of **Good** and **Bad** ratings.
4. Select **Comments** to read what customers wrote.

title: View SLA compliance
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Go to **Reports** > **SLAs**.
2. Choose a policy from the **SLA policy** list.
3. Review the percentage of tickets that met first response and resolution targets.
4. Select a bar in the chart to list the breached tickets.

title: View first response time
body:
If you can't see this option, ask an admin to check your role.

1. Go to **Reports** > **Response times**.
2. Choose a **Date range**.
3. Select **Group by** > **Channel**, **Team** or **Agent**.
4. Read the average and median times in the table.

Times are shown in business hours if the ticket uses a schedule.

title: See ticket volume by channel
aliases: how many tickets come from email vs chat
body:
Changes are saved straight away.

1. Go to **Reports** > **Overview**.
2. Open the **Tickets created** chart.
3. Select **Group by** > **Channel**.
4. Hover over a bar to see the count for each channel.

title: Add a chart to your dashboard
aliases: pin a report to the overview
put a chart on my dashboard
show a report on the home page
body:
The action is recorded in the audit log under **Admin** > **Audit log**.

1. Open a report in **Reports**.
2. Select **Add to dashboard**.
3. Choose the dashboard and a chart type such as **Bar** or **Line**.
4. Select **Add**.

title: See which knowledge base articles are viewed most
body:
Your administrator controls who has permission to do this.

1. Go to **Reports** > **Knowledge base**.
2. Choose a **Date range**.
3. Sort the table by **Views**.
4. Select an article title to see searches that led to it.

title: Add a customer
body:
Create a customer record before you invoice or quote them.

1. Go to **Customers**.
2. Select **New customer**.
3. Enter the **Customer name** and **Email**.
4. Add a **Billing address** and any **Payment terms** if needed.
5. Select **Save customer**.

title: Add a billing contact to a customer
aliases: add another person to receive invoices
add a second email for invoices
body:
Billing contacts receive invoices, quotes and reminders for a customer.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select the **Contacts** tab.
3. Select **Add billing contact**.
4. Enter the contact's **Name**, **Email** and **Phone**.
5. Select **Save contact**.

title: Update a billing contact's phone number
aliases: new mobile number for a contact
body:
1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select the **Contacts** tab.
3. Select the contact's name.
4. Edit the **Phone** field.
5. Select **Save contact**.
6. The new number appears on the customer's statements straight away.

title: Update a billing contact's email address
aliases: invoices going to the wrong email
new email for a billing contact
body:
Future invoices and reminders will go to the new address. Emails already sent are not changed.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select the **Contacts** tab.
3. Select the contact's name.
4. Replace the address in the **Email** field.
5. Select **Save contact**.

title: Delete a customer
aliases: get rid of a customer record
body:
You can only delete a customer who has no invoices or quotes. Otherwise, archive them instead.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select **More actions**.
3. Select **Delete customer**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.

title: Delete a billing contact
body:
A customer must always keep at least one billing contact, so add a replacement first if you are removing the last one.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select the **Contacts** tab.
3. Select the contact's name.
4. Select **Delete contact**.
5. Select **Delete** to confirm.

title: Export customers to CSV
body:
The export includes names, billing contacts, addresses and payment terms.

1. Go to **Customers**.
2. Use **Filter** to narrow the list, or leave it as is to export everyone.
3. Select **Export**.
4. Choose **CSV**.
5. Select **Download**. The file saves to your device.

title: Import customers from CSV
body:
Use this to add many customers at once.

1. Go to **Customers**.
2. Select **Import**.
3. Select **Download template** and fill it in.
4. Select **Choose file** and upload your CSV.
5. Match your columns to Harbour fields, then select **Import customers**.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Add a note to a customer
aliases: write a note on a customer
leave a comment on a client
record a call with a customer
body:
Notes are internal. Customers never see them.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select the **Notes** tab.
3. Select **Add note**.
4. Type your note.
5. Select **Save note**. Your name and the date are added automatically.

title: Change a customer's status
body:
A customer can be **Active**, **On hold** or **Inactive**. You cannot create new invoices for customers on hold or inactive.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select the **Status** drop-down at the top of the page.
3. Choose the new status.
4. Select **Update status**.

title: Set a primary billing contact
aliases: make a contact the main one
body:
The primary contact is the default recipient when you send an invoice or quote.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select the **Contacts** tab.
3. Find the contact you want.
4. Select the three dots, then **Make primary**.

title: Update a customer's billing address
body:
Draft invoices pick up the new address. Issued invoices keep the address they were sent with.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select **Edit details**.
3. Update the fields under **Billing address**.
4. Select **Save customer**.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Merge duplicate customers
body:
Merging moves all invoices, quotes and contacts into one record. This cannot be undone.

1. Go to **Customers**.
2. Tick the two duplicate customers.
3. Select **Merge**.
4. Choose which record to **Keep**.
5. Select **Merge customers**.

title: Set payment terms for a customer
aliases: change how many days a customer has to pay
default due date for a client
body:
New invoices for this customer will use these terms unless you change them.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select **Edit details**.
3. Under **Payment terms**, choose an option such as **Net 14** or **Net 30**.
4. Select **Save customer**.

title: Add a customer's ABN
body:
The ABN appears on invoices and quotes you send to this customer.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select **Edit details**.
3. Enter the number in the **ABN** field. We check it as you type.
4. Select **Save customer**.

title: Set a customer's default currency
aliases: invoice a customer in another currency
body:
You can only change the currency before the customer has any invoices.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select **Edit details**.
3. Choose a currency from the **Currency** list.
4. Select **Save customer**.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: View a customer statement
body:
1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select the **Statement** tab.
3. Choose a **Date range**.
4. Review invoices, payments, credits and the closing balance.
5. Select **Download PDF** to share it.

title: Turn on automatic reminders for a customer
body:
Harbour will email the customer's billing contacts when an invoice becomes overdue.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select **Edit details**.
3. Switch on **Automatic reminders**.
4. Choose when to send them, such as **3 days after due date**.
5. Select **Save customer**.

title: Add a tag to a customer
body:
Tags help you filter your customer list and reports.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select **Edit details**.
3. Click in the **Tags** box.
4. Type a tag or pick an existing one, then press Enter.
5. Select **Save customer**.

title: Restore an archived customer
body:
Archived customers are hidden from your list but keep their history.

1. Go to **Customers**.
2. Select **Filter**, then **Archived**.
3. Open the customer.
4. Select **Restore customer**.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Create an invoice
body:
1. Go to **Invoices**.
2. Select **New invoice**.
3. Choose a **Customer**.
4. Select **Add line item** and pick a product, or type a description.
5. Check the **Due date** and tax.
6. Select **Save as draft** or **Approve and send**.

title: Send an invoice by email
aliases: email an invoice to a customer
body:
The invoice is sent to the customer's primary billing contact unless you choose others.

1. Go to **Invoices** and open the invoice.
2. Select **Send**.
3. Check the **To** addresses and edit the message if you like.
4. Select **Send invoice**.

title: Send a payment reminder
body:
Reminders are only available for invoices that have been sent and are not yet paid.

1. Go to **Invoices** and select the **Overdue** tab.
2. Open the invoice.
3. Select **Send reminder**.
4. Edit the message if needed.
5. Select **Send**. The reminder is logged in the invoice history.

title: Record a payment on an invoice
body:
Use this when a customer pays you outside Harbour, such as by bank transfer or cash.

1. Go to **Invoices** and open the invoice.
2. Select **Record payment**.
3. Enter the **Amount**, **Date** and **Payment method**.
4. Select **Save payment**. The status changes to **Paid** once the balance is zero.

title: Edit a draft invoice
body:
You can only edit invoices with a **Draft** status. For sent invoices, void and reissue or issue a credit note.

1. Go to **Invoices** and select the **Drafts** tab.
2. Open the invoice.
3. Select **Edit**.
4. Make your changes.
5. Select **Save as draft**.

title: Void an invoice
body:
Voiding cancels the invoice but keeps it on record. It cannot be voided if it has payments.

1. Go to **Invoices** and open the invoice.
2. Select **More actions**.
3. Select **Void invoice**.
4. Enter a reason if you want one.
5. Select **Void** to confirm.

title: Delete a draft invoice
body:
Only drafts can be deleted. Deleted invoices cannot be recovered.

1. Go to **Invoices** and select the **Drafts** tab.
2. Open the invoice.
3. Select **More actions**.
4. Select **Delete draft**.
5. Select **Delete** to confirm.

title: Duplicate an invoice
body:
The copy is saved as a new draft with today's date.

1. Go to **Invoices** and open the invoice.
2. Select **More actions**.
3. Select **Duplicate**.
4. Change the customer or line items if needed.
5. Select **Save as draft**.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Download an invoice as a PDF
body:
1. Go to **Invoices** and open the invoice.
2. Select **Download**.
3. Choose **PDF**.
4. The file saves to your device, ready to print or attach to an email.

You need the **Admin** or **Billing** role to do this.

title: Export invoices to CSV
body:
You can export all invoices or only those matching your filters.

1. Go to **Invoices**.
2. Use **Filter** to choose a date range or status.
3. Select **Export**.
4. Choose **CSV**.
5. Select **Download**.

title: Add a note to an invoice
aliases: write an internal note on an invoice
add a memo to an invoice
body:
Internal notes are only visible to your team. To add a message the customer sees, use the **Notes to customer** box instead.

1. Go to **Invoices** and open the invoice.
2. Select the **History** tab.
3. Select **Add note**.
4. Type your note.
5. Select **Save note**.

title: Change an invoice's due date
body:
You can change the due date on draft and sent invoices.

1. Go to **Invoices** and open the invoice.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Pick a new **Due date**.
4. Select **Save changes**. If the invoice was sent, choose whether to notify the customer.

title: Apply a discount to an invoice
body:
This discounts the invoice total. To discount a single item, see line item discounts.

1. Go to **Invoices** and open the draft invoice.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Select **Add discount** under the line items.
4. Choose **Percentage** or **Amount** and enter the value.
5. Select **Save as draft**.

title: Issue a credit note
body:
A credit note reduces what the customer owes.

1. Go to **Invoices** and open the sent invoice.
2. Select **More actions**.
3. Select **Issue credit note**.
4. Enter the **Amount** or select the items to credit.
5. Select **Approve credit note**.

title: Set up a recurring invoice
body:
Harbour will create the invoice on your schedule.

1. Go to **Invoices** and select **Recurring**.
2. Select **New recurring invoice**.
3. Choose the **Customer** and add line items.
4. Set the **Frequency** and **Start date**.
5. Choose **Send automatically** or **Save as draft**, then select **Save schedule**.

title: Pause a recurring invoice
body:
Pausing stops new invoices from being created. Existing invoices are not affected.

1. Go to **Invoices** and select **Recurring**.
2. Open the schedule.
3. Select **Pause**.
4. Select **Resume** whenever you want to start again.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Add a late fee to an invoice
body:
1. Go to **Invoices** and open the overdue invoice.
2. Select **More actions**.
3. Select **Add late fee**.
4. Enter a **Percentage** or **Fixed amount**.
5. Select **Apply fee**. It is added as a new line item.

title: Change the invoice number format
body:
Changes apply to new invoices only.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Invoice settings**.
2. Under **Numbering**, edit the **Prefix**, such as INV-.
3. Enter the **Next number**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Refund a payment
aliases: give money back to a customer
body:
Recording a refund in Harbour does not move money. You will still need to send it through your bank or card provider.

1. Go to **Invoices** and open the paid invoice.
2. Find the payment under **Payments**.
3. Select **Refund**.
4. Enter the **Amount** and **Date**.
5. Select **Record refund**.

title: Attach a file to an invoice
aliases: add a document to an invoice
upload a pdf to an invoice
body:
Attachments are sent with the invoice email. Each file can be up to 10 MB.

1. Go to **Invoices** and open the draft invoice.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Scroll to **Attachments** and select **Add file**.
4. Choose a file from your device.
5. Select **Save as draft**.

title: Create a quote
aliases: write a quote for a customer
body:
1. Go to **Quotes**.
2. Select **New quote**.
3. Choose a **Customer**.
4. Add line items using **Add line item**.
5. Check the **Expiry date**.
6. Select **Save as draft** or **Approve and send**.

title: Send a quote by email
body:
The customer gets a link to view the quote online and can accept it with one click.

1. Go to **Quotes** and open the quote.
2. Select **Send**.
3. Check the **To** addresses and message.
4. Select **Send quote**. The status changes to **Sent**.

title: Convert a quote to an invoice
aliases: turn a quote into an invoice
body:
All line items, discounts and tax carry across to a new draft invoice.

1. Go to **Quotes** and open an accepted quote.
2. Select **Convert to invoice**.
3. Review the draft invoice.
4. Select **Approve and send**.

title: Edit a quote
body:
If the quote has already been sent, the customer will see the updated version.

1. Go to **Quotes** and open the quote.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Change the line items, dates or notes.
4. Select **Save changes**.
5. Select **Resend** if you want to notify the customer.

title: Duplicate a quote
body:
The copy is saved as a draft with a new quote number.

1. Go to **Quotes** and open the quote.
2. Select **More actions**.
3. Select **Duplicate**.
4. Change the customer or items.
5. Select **Save as draft**.

title: Mark a quote as accepted
aliases: approve quote on behalf of customer
body:
Use this when the customer agrees outside of Harbour, for example by phone.

1. Go to **Quotes** and open the quote.
2. Select **Mark as accepted**.
3. Choose the **Date accepted**.
4. Select **Confirm**.

title: Mark a quote as declined
body:
1. Go to **Quotes** and open the quote.
2. Select **Mark as declined**.
3. Choose a **Reason**, such as **Price** or **Went elsewhere**.
4. Select **Confirm**.

If you can't see an option, check that your role has the right permissions. Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Change a quote's expiry date
body:
Expired quotes cannot be accepted by the customer until you extend them.

1. Go to **Quotes** and open the quote.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Pick a new **Expiry date**.
4. Select **Save changes**.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Delete a quote
body:
You can delete quotes that are in **Draft** status or have been declined. Sent or accepted quotes must be declined or archived first.

1. Go to **Quotes** and open the quote.
2. Select **More actions**.
3. Select **Delete quote**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.

title: Export quotes to CSV
body:
1. Go to **Quotes**.
2. Use **Filter** to choose a status or date range.
3. Select **Export**.
4. Choose **CSV**.
5. Select **Download**.

Harbour records the change in the activity history so your team can see who made it.

title: Add a note to a quote
aliases: write a note about a quote
body:
Notes are internal and are never shown to the customer.

1. Go to **Quotes** and open the quote.
2. Select the **History** tab.
3. Select **Add note**.
4. Type your note and select **Save note**.

title: Download a quote as a PDF
body:
1. Go to **Quotes** and open the quote.
2. Select **Download**.
3. Choose **PDF**.
4. The file saves to your device.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving. You need the **Admin** or **Billing** role to do this.

title: Add a discount to a quote
aliases: offer a discount on an estimate
take a percentage off a quote
body:
1. Go to **Quotes** and open the quote.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Select **Add discount** under the line items.
4. Choose **Percentage** or **Amount** and enter a value.
5. Select **Save changes**.

You need the **Admin** or **Billing** role to do this.

title: Set the default quote expiry
body:
New quotes will expire after this many days unless you change the date.
