1. Go to **Settings** and select **Quote settings**.
2. Enter the number of days under **Default expiry**.
3. Select **Save**.

title: Set the quote number format
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Quote settings**.
2. Under **Numbering**, edit the **Prefix**, such as QUO-.
3. Enter the **Next number**.
4. Select **Save**.

If you can't see an option, check that your role has the right permissions. Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Add terms and conditions to a quote
body:
Terms appear at the bottom of the quote. You can save them as a default for future quotes.

1. Go to **Quotes** and open the draft quote.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Type your wording in the **Terms** box.
4. Tick **Use as default** if you want to reuse it.
5. Select **Save changes**.

title: Request a deposit on a quote
body:
When the customer accepts, Harbour creates a deposit invoice automatically.

1. Go to **Quotes** and open the draft quote.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Switch on **Request deposit**.
4. Enter a **Percentage** or **Fixed amount**.
5. Select **Save changes**.

title: Reopen a declined quote
aliases: put a quote back to sent
body:
1. Go to **Quotes** and select the **Declined** tab.
2. Open the quote.
3. Select **Reopen**.
4. The quote returns to **Draft** so you can edit and resend it.

title: Send a quote follow-up
aliases: remind a customer about an estimate
body:
Follow-ups are available while a quote is **Sent** and has not expired.

1. Go to **Quotes** and open the quote.
2. Select **Send follow-up**.
3. Edit the message if needed.
4. Select **Send**.

title: Attach a file to a quote
aliases: add a document to an estimate
upload a drawing to a quote
body:
Each file can be up to 10 MB.

1. Go to **Quotes** and open the draft quote.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Under **Attachments**, select **Add file**.
4. Choose a file from your device.
5. Select **Save changes**.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Add a product
body:
Saved products can be added to invoices and quotes in one click.

1. Go to **Products**.
2. Select **New product**.
3. Enter a **Name** and **Price**.
4. Choose a **Tax rate**.
5. Select **Save product**.

title: Add a service
body:
Services are billed by time or job rather than by item count.

1. Go to **Products**.
2. Select **New product**.
3. Set **Type** to **Service**.
4. Enter a **Name** and **Price**, and choose **Hour** or **Job** under **Unit**.
5. Select **Save product**.

title: Edit a product
body:
Edits do not change invoices or quotes you have already created.

1. Go to **Products**.
2. Select the product.
3. Select **Edit**.
4. Update the details.
5. Select **Save product**.

title: Change a product's price
body:
Existing drafts keep their original price. New line items use the new price.

1. Go to **Products**.
2. Select the product.
3. Select **Edit**.
4. Enter the new **Price**.
5. Select **Save product**.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Delete a product
body:
You can only delete a product that has never been used on an invoice or quote. Otherwise, archive it.

1. Go to **Products**.
2. Select the product.
3. Select **More actions**.
4. Select **Delete product**.
5. Select **Delete** to confirm.

title: Archive a product
body:
Archived products no longer appear when adding line items, but stay on past documents.

1. Go to **Products**.
2. Select the product.
3. Select **More actions**.
4. Select **Archive product**.
5. Select **Archived** in the filter to find it again.

title: Import products from CSV
body:
1. Go to **Products**.
2. Select **Import**.
3. Select **Download template** and fill it in.
4. Upload your CSV with **Choose file**.
5. Match the columns, then select **Import products**.

title: Export products to CSV
body:
1. Go to **Products**.
2. Select **Export**.
3. Choose **CSV**.
4. Select **Download**.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving. You need the **Admin** or **Billing** role to do this.

title: Add a product category
body:
Categories help you filter products and report on sales.

1. Go to **Products** and select **Categories**.
2. Select **New category**.
3. Enter a **Name**.
4. Select **Save**.
5. Open a product and choose the category under **Category**.

title: Add a line item to an invoice
aliases: add a product to an invoice
put an item on an invoice
body:
1. Go to **Invoices** and open the draft invoice.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Select **Add line item**.
4. Search for a product, or type a description.
5. Check the **Quantity** and **Price**.
6. Select **Save as draft**.

title: Remove a line item
aliases: delete a row from an invoice
body:
You can remove line items from drafts only.

1. Go to **Invoices** or **Quotes** and open the draft.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Select the bin icon at the end of the row.
4. Select **Save as draft**.

title: Reorder line items
body:
1. Go to **Invoices** or **Quotes** and open the draft.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Drag the handle at the start of a row to a new position.
4. Select **Save as draft**.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Add a one-off line item
aliases: bill something not in my product list
add a line without a product
body:
The item is only used on this document and is not saved to **Products**.

1. Go to **Invoices** or **Quotes** and open the draft.
2. Select **Edit**, then **Add line item**.
3. Type a description instead of choosing a product.
4. Enter a **Quantity**, **Price** and **Tax rate**.
5. Select **Save as draft**.

title: Change a line item's quantity
body:
1. Go to **Invoices** or **Quotes** and open the draft.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Change the number in the **Quantity** column.
4. The total updates automatically.
5. Select **Save as draft**.

title: Set a product code
body:
Product codes appear on invoices and can be searched.

1. Go to **Products**.
2. Select the product, then **Edit**.
3. Enter a code in the **SKU** field.
4. Select **Save product**.

title: Set a default tax rate for a product
body:
This rate is used whenever you add the product to an invoice or quote.

1. Go to **Products**.
2. Select the product, then **Edit**.
3. Choose a rate from the **Tax rate** list.
4. Select **Save product**.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Apply a discount to a line item
aliases: reduce the price of one line
body:
1. Go to **Invoices** or **Quotes** and open the draft.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Enter a percentage in the **Disc %** column of the row.
4. Select **Save as draft**.

You need the **Admin** or **Billing** role to do this.

title: Set a unit of measure
aliases: bill per hour or per kilo
body:
The unit shows beside the quantity on invoices, such as 3 hours or 10 kg.

1. Go to **Products**.
2. Select the product, then **Edit**.
3. Choose a value from **Unit**, or select **Add unit** to create one.
4. Select **Save product**.

title: Add a note to a product
aliases: write a note about a product
body:
Internal notes are never shown to customers.

1. Go to **Products** and select the product.
2. Select the **Notes** tab.
3. Select **Add note**.
4. Type your note and select **Save note**.

title: Set a customer-specific price
body:
The special price is used automatically when you add this product to that customer's invoices and quotes.

1. Go to **Products** and select the product.
2. Select the **Pricing** tab.
3. Select **Add customer price**.
4. Choose the **Customer** and enter the **Price**.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Add a tax rate
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Tax**.
2. Select **New tax rate**.
3. Enter a **Name**, such as GST.
4. Enter the **Rate** as a percentage.
5. Select **Save**.

You need the **Admin** or **Billing** role to do this.

title: Edit a tax rate
body:
Changes apply to new drafts only. Issued invoices keep the rate they were created with.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Tax**.
2. Select the tax rate.
3. Update the **Name** or **Rate**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Delete a tax rate
aliases: get rid of a tax rate
body:
You can only delete rates that have never been used. Otherwise, select **Archive** instead.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Tax**.
2. Select the tax rate.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.

title: Set the default tax rate
body:
New line items use the default unless the product has its own rate.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Tax**.
2. Find the rate you want.
3. Select the three dots, then **Make default**.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Enter your business ABN
body:
Your ABN is required to issue tax invoices in Australia.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Business details**.
2. Enter your number in the **ABN** field.
3. Select **Verify**.
4. Select **Save**.

You need the **Admin** or **Billing** role to do this.

title: Turn on GST
body:
Turn this on once you are registered for GST.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Tax**.
2. Switch on **Charge GST**.
3. Enter the **Effective date**.
4. Select **Save**. A 10% GST rate is added.

title: Switch between tax inclusive and exclusive prices
body:
This setting only affects new invoices and quotes.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Tax**.
2. Under **Prices**, choose **Tax inclusive** or **Tax exclusive**.
3. Select **Save**.

If you can't see an option, check that your role has the right permissions. Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Make a customer tax exempt
body:
New invoices for this customer will have no tax applied.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select **Edit details**.
3. Switch on **Tax exempt**.
4. Enter an **Exemption reason**.
5. Select **Save customer**.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Create a tax group
body:
A tax group adds several rates together and shows one combined rate on documents.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Tax**.
2. Select **New tax group**.
3. Enter a **Name**.
4. Select the rates to include.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Apply a tax rate to a line item
aliases: set gst free for one item
pick a tax for a line
body:
1. Go to **Invoices** or **Quotes** and open the draft.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Choose a rate from the **Tax** column of the row.
4. Select **Save as draft**.

title: Export the tax report to CSV
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and select **Tax summary**.
2. Choose a **Date range**.
3. Select **Export**.
4. Choose **CSV**.
5. Select **Download**.

If you can't see an option, check that your role has the right permissions. Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Run a tax summary report
aliases: see how much gst I collected
body:
The report shows tax collected on sales for the period you choose.

1. Go to **Reports** and select **Tax summary**.
2. Choose a **Date range**, or select a quarter.
3. Select **Run report**.
4. Review totals by tax rate.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Set your tax reporting period
body:
This sets the default periods in your tax reports.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Tax**.
2. Under **Reporting period**, choose **Monthly**, **Quarterly** or **Annually**.
3. Select **Save**.

You need the **Admin** or **Billing** role to do this.

title: Change how tax is rounded
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Tax**.
2. Under **Rounding**, choose **Per line** or **On total**.
3. Select **Save**. New documents will use this method.

Harbour records the change in the activity history so your team can see who made it.

title: Add a tax exemption reason
aliases: tax note for an exempt line
body:
The reason prints on invoices where no tax is charged.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Tax**.
2. Select the tax rate, such as **GST free**.
3. Type your wording in **Reason on invoice**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Show your tax number on invoices
body:
Invoices with GST must show your ABN and the words Tax invoice.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Invoice settings**.
2. Under **Layout**, switch on **Show tax number**.
3. Switch on **Use "Tax invoice" heading**.
4. Select **Save**.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Apply reverse charge to an invoice
body:
Use this when the customer accounts for the tax.

1. Go to **Invoices** and open the draft invoice.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Switch on **Reverse charge**.
4. Select **Save as draft**. Tax is removed and a notice is added.

title: Mark a product as GST free
body:
1. Go to **Products** and select the product.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Choose **GST free** from **Tax rate**.
4. Select **Save product**.

Harbour records the change in the activity history so your team can see who made it.

title: Set a tax rate for a region
body:
Customers in the region will use this rate automatically.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Tax**.
2. Select **Regional rates**.
3. Select **Add region** and choose a country or state.
4. Pick the **Tax rate**.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Change the tax rate on a draft invoice
body:
Sent invoices cannot be changed. Void them or issue a credit note.

1. Go to **Invoices** and open the draft.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Select **Change tax** above the line items.
4. Choose the new rate.
5. Select **Save as draft**.

Select **Cancel** at any point to leave without saving.

title: Record a payment against an invoice
aliases: customer paid me, how do I record it
body:
Use this when a customer pays by bank transfer, cash or cheque outside Harbour.

1. Go to **Invoices** and open the invoice.
2. Select **Record payment**.
3. Enter the **Amount**, **Payment date** and **Method**.
4. Add a reference such as the transfer number in **Notes** if you like.
5. Select **Save payment**.

The invoice status updates to **Paid** or **Part paid**.

title: Record a part payment
aliases: customer paid only some of the invoice
body:
1. Open the invoice from **Invoices**.
2. Select **Record payment**.
3. Change the **Amount** to the portion received. Harbour fills in the full balance by default.
4. Choose the **Payment date** and **Method**.
5. Select **Save payment**.

The invoice shows **Part paid** and the remaining **Balance due** is updated.

title: Delete a payment entered by mistake
body:
Only payments recorded manually can be deleted. Card payments must be refunded instead.

1. Open the invoice and scroll to **Payment history**.
2. Select the three dots next to the payment.
3. Choose **Delete payment**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Delete**.

The invoice balance and status are recalculated straight away.

title: Change the date of a payment
aliases: edit when the payment was received
body:
1. Go to **Payments** and find the payment using the search box.
2. Select the payment to open it.
3. Select **Edit**.
4. Change the **Payment date**.
5. Select **Save changes**.

Changing the date can move the payment into a different reporting period, so check your reports afterwards.

title: Connect a card payment gateway
body:
You need to be an account **Owner** or **Admin** to do this.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Payment gateways**.
2. Select **Connect** next to your gateway.
3. Sign in to the gateway and approve the connection.
4. Choose which currencies to accept.
5. Select **Save**.

Your invoices now show a **Pay now** button to customers.

title: Turn off online payments for one invoice
aliases: disable card payment on an invoice
body:
1. Open the invoice from **Invoices**.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Under **Payment options**, clear **Allow online payment**.
4. Select **Save**.

The customer will see your bank details only. Other invoices are not affected.

title: Add bank details to your invoices
aliases: put my BSB and account number on invoices
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Payment details**.
2. Enter your **Account name**, **BSB** and **Account number**.
3. Add any extra wording, such as a payment reference, in **Instructions**.
4. Select **Save**.

The details appear in the footer of every new invoice that uses your default template.

title: Set default payment terms
aliases: how long customers have to pay
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Invoice defaults**.
2. Under **Payment terms**, choose an option such as **Net 14** or **Net 30**.
3. Select **Save**.

New invoices use these terms. Existing invoices keep their current due date, and you can still change the due date on any single invoice.

title: Refund a card payment
aliases: give the money back to customer's card
body:
Refunds go back to the original card and usually take 5 to 10 business days to appear.

1. Go to **Payments** and open the card payment.
2. Select **Refund**.
3. Enter the amount to return. You can refund less than the full payment.
4. Choose a **Reason**.
5. Select **Confirm refund**.

title: Import a bank statement to match payments
body:
1. Go to **Payments** and select **Import**.
2. Choose **Bank statement (CSV)** and upload your file.
3. Match the columns for **Date**, **Amount** and **Description**.
4. Review the suggested matches and untick any that are wrong.
5. Select **Apply payments**.

Unmatched lines stay in **Needs review** so you can match them by hand.

title: Export payments to CSV
body:
1. Go to **Payments**.
2. Use the **Date range** and **Method** filters to narrow the list.
3. Select **Export** and choose **CSV**.
4. Open the file from your downloads when it is ready.

The export includes the customer name, invoice number, amount, method and reference.

title: Save a card on a customer's profile
body:
The customer must have approved card storage, either at checkout or by an emailed request.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select the **Payments** tab.
3. Select **Request card**.
4. Choose the billing contact to email.

Once the customer completes the form, the card appears under **Saved cards**.

title: Remove a saved card from a customer
body:
1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select the **Payments** tab.
3. Next to the card under **Saved cards**, select **Remove**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Remove card**.

Any recurring invoices set to charge this card will switch to emailing the invoice instead.

title: Apply a customer's prepayment to an invoice
aliases: apply credit on account to invoice
body:
1. Open the invoice from **Invoices**.
2. Select **Apply credit**.
3. Pick the prepayment or overpayment from the list.
4. Enter the amount to apply.
5. Select **Apply**.

Any unused amount stays on the customer's account.

title: Add a card surcharge to invoices
aliases: add a surcharge for credit card
body:
Check your local rules on surcharging before turning this on.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Payment gateways**.
2. Select **Surcharge settings**.
3. Turn on **Add surcharge** and enter a percentage.
4. Select **Save**.

The surcharge appears as a separate line when the customer chooses to pay by card.

title: Send a payment receipt
body:
1. Go to **Payments** and open the payment.
2. Select **Send receipt**.
3. Check the billing contact's email address, or add another.
4. Select **Send**.

Harbour attaches a PDF receipt. Card payments also send one automatically.

title: Set up automatic payment reminders
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Reminders**.
2. Turn on **Automatic reminders**.
3. Select **Add reminder** and choose when it is sent, for example **3 days before due** or **7 days after due**.
4. Choose a template for each reminder.
5. Select **Save**.

Reminders stop as soon as an invoice is paid.

title: Pause reminders on one invoice
aliases: don't remind customer about this one
body:
Use this when you have agreed a payment date with the customer.

1. Open the invoice from **Invoices**.
2. Select **More**, then **Reminder settings**.
3. Turn off **Send automatic reminders**.
4. Select **Save**.

You can turn them back on at any time.

Need to undo this later?

title: Pause reminders for a customer
aliases: stop all reminders to a client
body:
1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Under **Preferences**, clear **Send payment reminders**.
4. Select **Save**.

This applies to all of the customer's invoices, including future ones.

title: Edit a reminder email template
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Reminders**.
2. Open the **Templates** tab.
3. Select the template you want to change.
4. Edit the **Subject** and **Message**. Use fields such as **{customer_name}** and **{amount_due}**.
5. Select **Save template**.

title: View all overdue invoices
body:
1. Go to **Invoices**.
2. Select the **Overdue** tab.
3. Sort by **Days overdue** to see the oldest first.

Use the search box to narrow the list to one customer.

title: Set up a payment plan on an overdue invoice
body:
1. Open the overdue invoice.
2. Select **More**, then **Payment plan**.
3. Choose the number of instalments and the first due date.
4. Review the schedule.
5. Select **Create plan**.

Each instalment gets its own due date and reminder.

title: Add a late fee to an overdue invoice
body:
1. Open the overdue invoice.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Select **Add line item** and enter your late fee description and amount.
4. Select **Save**.

To add the fee automatically, go to **Settings**, select **Reminders**, and turn on **Late fees**.

title: Add a note after calling about an overdue invoice
aliases: record a phone call with customer
write down what the customer said
body:
Notes are internal and are never shown to the customer.

1. Open the invoice from **Invoices**.
2. Select the **Notes** tab.
3. Type your note, such as the date the customer promised to pay.
4. Select **Add note**.

title: Write off an unpayable invoice
body:
1. Open the invoice from **Invoices**.
2. Select **More**, then **Write off**.
3. Enter a **Reason**.
4. Select **Confirm write-off**.

The invoice status changes to **Written off** and reminders stop. The amount appears in your **Bad debts** report.

Need to undo this later?

title: Change who reminders are sent from
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Reminders**.
2. Select **Sender details**.
3. Enter the **From name** and **Reply-to email**.
4. Select **Save**.
5. Check the confirmation email sent to the new address.

The new reply-to address is used once it is confirmed.

title: Update a customer's phone number
body:
1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Change the number in the **Phone** field.
4. Select **Save**.

To change a billing contact's number instead, open the **Contacts** tab and edit the contact.

Need to undo this later?

title: Create a recurring invoice
body:
1. Go to **Recurring** and select **New recurring invoice**.
2. Choose the customer.
3. Add your line items.
4. Under **Schedule**, choose how often to invoice and the **Start date**.
5. Select **Save**.

Harbour creates each invoice on the schedule you set.

title: Turn an existing invoice into a recurring one
body:
1. Open the invoice from **Invoices**.
2. Select **More**, then **Make recurring**.
3. Choose the frequency and the **Next invoice date**.
4. Select **Create recurring invoice**.

The original invoice stays as it is.

title: Cancel a recurring invoice
body:
1. Go to **Recurring** and open the schedule.
2. Select **More**, then **End schedule**.
3. Pick the **End date** and select **Confirm**.

Invoices already created are not changed. An ended schedule can be viewed under **Ended**.

Need to undo this later?

title: Skip the next recurring invoice
body:
1. Go to **Recurring** and open the schedule.
2. Under **Upcoming invoices**, find the next one.
3. Select **Skip**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Skip invoice**.

The schedule continues as normal after the skipped date.

title: Change how often a recurring invoice is sent
body:
1. Go to **Recurring** and open the schedule.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Under **Schedule**, choose a new **Frequency**.
4. Check the **Next invoice date**.
5. Select **Save**.

The change applies from the next invoice.

title: Change the amount on a recurring invoice
body:
1. Go to **Recurring** and open the schedule.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Change the **Unit price** or **Quantity** on the line items.
4. Select **Save**.

Only future invoices use the new amount. Invoices already sent keep the old one.

title: Set an end date for a recurring invoice
aliases: stop after a number of invoices
body:
1. Go to **Recurring** and open the schedule.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Under **Ends**, choose **On a date** or **After a number of invoices**.
4. Enter the date or number.
5. Select **Save**.

Need to undo this later?

title: Send recurring invoices automatically
body:
1. Go to **Recurring** and open the schedule.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Under **When created**, choose **Approve and email**.
4. Select **Save**.

If you prefer to check each invoice, choose **Save as draft** instead.

title: Review recurring invoices saved as drafts
aliases: where do draft recurring invoices go
body:
1. Go to **Invoices** and select the **Drafts** tab.
2. Filter by **Source**, then choose **Recurring**.
3. Open a draft and check the details.
4. Select **Approve and send**.

title: Charge a saved card on a recurring invoice
aliases: bill card on file each month
body:
The customer must already have a saved card.

1. Go to **Recurring** and open the schedule.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Under **Payment**, turn on **Charge saved card**.
4. Choose the card.
5. Select **Save**.

If the charge fails, Harbour emails the invoice and tells you under **Notifications**.

title: See upcoming recurring invoices
aliases: what will be billed next month
body:
1. Go to **Recurring**.
2. Select the **Upcoming** tab.
3. Pick a date range using the **Next 30 days** menu.

Each row shows the customer, the date and the expected amount.

Need to undo this later?

title: Change the customer on a recurring invoice
body:
1. Go to **Recurring** and open the schedule.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Select the current customer name and choose a different **Customer**.
4. Select **Save**.

Future invoices go to the new customer's billing contacts.

title: Add a purchase order number to a recurring invoice
body:
1. Go to **Recurring** and open the schedule.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Enter the number in **Reference**.
4. Select **Save**.

The reference is printed on each new invoice.

title: Delete a recurring invoice schedule
body:
Deleting removes the schedule only. Invoices it created are kept.

1. Go to **Recurring** and open the schedule.
2. Select **More**, then **Delete**.
3. Select **Delete schedule** to confirm.

If you may need it later, end the schedule instead so you can still view it.

title: Copy a recurring invoice for another customer
body:
1. Go to **Recurring** and open the schedule.
2. Select **More**, then **Duplicate**.
3. Choose the new **Customer**.
4. Adjust the dates if needed and select **Save**.

Need to undo this later?

title: Create a credit note
body:
1. Go to **Credit notes** and select **New credit note**.
2. Choose the customer.
3. Add line items and amounts to credit.
4. Select **Approve**.

The credit note appears on the customer's account and can be applied to an invoice or refunded.

title: Create a credit note from an invoice
body:
1. Open the invoice from **Invoices**.
2. Select **More**, then **Create credit note**.
3. Remove any lines you do not want to credit, or change the quantities.
4. Select **Approve**.

The credit note is linked to the invoice.

title: Apply a credit note to an invoice
body:
1. Go to **Credit notes** and open the credit note.
2. Select **Apply to invoice**.
3. Tick the invoice and enter the amount.
4. Select **Apply**.

Any leftover amount stays available on the credit note.

title: Record a refund paid by bank transfer
body:
Use this after you have sent the money yourself.

1. Go to **Credit notes** and open the credit note.
2. Select **Record refund**.
3. Enter the **Amount**, **Date** and **Method**.
4. Select **Save refund**.

The credit note balance is reduced by the amount refunded.

Need to undo this later?

title: Void a credit note
body:
A credit note can only be voided if nothing has been applied or refunded against it.

1. Open the credit note from **Credit notes**.
2. Select **More**, then **Void**.
3. Select **Confirm**.

title: Email a credit note to a customer
aliases: customer wants a copy of credit note
body:
1. Go to **Credit notes** and open the credit note.
2. Select **Send**.
3. Check the recipients and edit the message.
4. Select **Send credit note**.

Need to undo this later?

title: Edit a credit note before it is approved
body:
1. Go to **Credit notes** and select the **Drafts** tab.
2. Open the credit note.
3. Make your changes to the lines, dates or reference.
4. Select **Save**.

Approved credit notes cannot be edited. Void it and create a new one.

title: Refund an overpayment
body:
1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select the **Account** tab and find the **Overpayment** line.
3. Select **Refund**.
4. Enter the amount and choose **Card** or **Bank transfer**.
5. Select **Confirm**.

title: See credit notes that have not been used
body:
1. Go to **Credit notes**.
2. Select the **Open** tab.
3. Sort by **Remaining credit** to see the largest balances first.

Select any row to apply or refund it.

title: Export credit notes to CSV
body:
1. Go to **Credit notes**.
2. Filter by date or status.
3. Select **Export**, then **CSV**.

The file lists the number, customer, date, total and remaining credit.

Need to undo this later?

title: Change the credit note numbering
aliases: start numbering at a different number
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Numbering**.
2. Under **Credit notes**, change the **Prefix** or **Next number**.
3. Select **Save**.

Numbers already issued do not change.

If something looks wrong afterwards, contact Harbour Support from **Help** and include a screenshot.

title: Add a reason to a credit note
body:
1. Open the credit note from **Credit notes**.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Choose a **Reason**, or select **Custom** to type your own.
4. Select **Save**.

The reason is printed on the credit note PDF.

title: Add an internal note to a credit note
body:
1. Open the credit note from **Credit notes**.
2. Select the **Notes** tab.
3. Type your note.
4. Select **Add note**.

Customers never see internal notes.

title: Cancel a pending card refund
body:
You can only cancel a refund while its status is **Pending**.

1. Go to **Payments** and select the **Refunds** tab.
2. Open the pending refund.
3. Select **Cancel refund**.
4. Select **Confirm**.

Need to undo this later?

title: Run a sales report
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and select **Sales**.
2. Choose a **Date range**.
3. Group by **Month**, **Customer** or **Item** using the **Group by** menu.
4. Select **Run report**.

If something looks wrong afterwards, contact Harbour Support from **Help** and include a screenshot.

title: Export the aged receivables report
aliases: who owes me and for how long
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and select **Aged receivables**.
2. Pick an **As at** date.
3. Select **Run report**.
4. Select **Export** and choose **CSV** or **PDF**.

Balances are grouped as current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90 and over 90 days.

title: Export your invoice list to CSV
body:
1. Go to **Invoices**.
2. Apply any filters, such as **Status** or **Date range**.
3. Select **Export** and choose **CSV**.
4. Open the file when your download finishes.

title: Export your customer list to CSV
aliases: get client list into a spreadsheet
body:
1. Go to **Customers**.
2. Select **Export**.
3. Choose **CSV** and tick the fields to include, such as **Phone** and **Billing contacts**.
4. Select **Download**.

Need to undo this later?

title: Import customers from a CSV file
body:
1. Go to **Customers** and select **Import**.
2. Download the sample file if you need the format.
3. Upload your CSV and match each column to a Harbour field.
4. Review the preview and select **Import customers**.

Rows with an existing customer name are updated rather than duplicated.

title: View a tax summary report
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and select **Tax summary**.
2. Choose the tax period and the **Basis**, either **Accrual** or **Cash**.
3. Select **Run report**.

Use **Export** to save a copy for your accountant.

title: Run a statement for one customer
aliases: what does customer owe in total
body:
1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select **Statement**.
3. Choose the date range.
4. Select **Send** to email it, or **Download PDF**.

Your changes are recorded in the account **Audit log**, so your team can see who made them and when. Need to undo this later?

title: Schedule a report to be emailed
aliases: email me the aged receivables each Monday
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and run the report you want.
2. Select **Schedule**.
3. Choose the frequency, time and recipients.
4. Select **Save schedule**.

Manage scheduled reports under **Reports**, then **Scheduled**.

Need to undo this later?

title: Save a report with your filters
body:
1. Run the report with the filters you want.
2. Select **Save view**.
3. Name the view and select **Save**.

Your saved views appear under **Reports**, then **My views**.

If something looks wrong afterwards, contact Harbour Support from **Help** and include a screenshot.

title: Run a payments received report
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and select **Payments received**.
2. Choose a **Date range**.
3. Group by **Method** or **Customer**.
4. Select **Run report**.

If you cannot see this option, ask an account Owner or Admin to check your role under **Settings**, then **Users**.

title: See the history of an invoice
body:
1. Open the invoice from **Invoices**.
2. Select the **Activity** tab.
3. Scroll to view each email, view, payment and edit with its date and user.

Use this to confirm a customer has viewed an invoice.

title: Export a recurring revenue report
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and select **Recurring revenue**.
2. Choose the number of months to forecast.
3. Select **Run report**.
4. Select **Export** to download a CSV.

Need to undo this later?

title: Run a bad debts report
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and select **Bad debts**.
2. Choose a **Date range**.
3. Select **Run report**.

The report lists each written-off invoice with the date, customer and reason.

If something looks wrong afterwards, contact Harbour Support from **Help** and include a screenshot.

title: Run a report in another currency
aliases: see totals in my base currency
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and open the report.
2. Open the **Currency** menu.
3. Choose **Base currency** to convert everything, or pick a single currency.
4. Select **Run report**.

Amounts are converted using the rate on each invoice.

title: Download a report as a PDF
body:
1. Run the report you need.
2. Select **Export**.
3. Choose **PDF**.
4. Save the file or print it from your browser.

Your changes are recorded in the account **Audit log**, so your team can see who made them and when. Need to undo this later?

title: See your top customers by revenue
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and select **Sales**.
2. Set **Group by** to **Customer**.
3. Choose a **Date range**.
4. Select **Run report**, then sort by **Total**.

Need to undo this later?

title: Update your business name and address
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Business details**.
2. Edit the **Business name**, **Address** or **Tax number**.
3. Select **Save**.

Changes appear on new invoices. Existing invoices keep the details they were sent with.

title: Upload your logo to invoices
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Templates**.
2. Open your default template.
3. Under **Logo**, select **Upload** and choose a PNG or JPG file.
4. Select **Save**.

A logo at least 400 pixels wide gives the sharpest result.

title: Change the colours on your invoice template
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Templates**.
2. Open the template.
3. Under **Style**, choose an **Accent colour** or enter a hex code.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Create a new invoice template
aliases: new template for a different brand
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Templates**.
2. Select **New template**.
3. Name the template and choose a starting layout.
4. Adjust the sections, colours and footer.
5. Select **Save**.

Need to undo this later?

title: Duplicate an invoice template
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Templates**.
2. Select the three dots next to the template.
3. Choose **Duplicate**.
4. Rename the copy and select **Save**.

If something looks wrong afterwards, contact Harbour Support from **Help** and include a screenshot.

title: Set the default invoice template
aliases: choose which template new invoices use
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Templates**.
2. Select the three dots next to the template you want.
3. Choose **Set as default**.

You can still pick another template on any individual invoice.

title: Use a different template for one customer
body:
1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Under **Invoice template**, choose the template.
4. Select **Save**.

Your changes are recorded in the account **Audit log**, so your team can see who made them and when. Need to undo this later?

title: Edit the email that sends with an invoice
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Email templates**.
2. Select **Invoice**.
3. Edit the **Subject** and **Message**.
4. Select **Save**.

Need to undo this later? You can come back to the same screen and change it again at any time.

title: Add a footer message to invoices
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Templates**.
2. Open the template.
3. Type your text in **Footer**.
4. Select **Save**.

If something looks wrong afterwards, contact Harbour Support from **Help** and include a screenshot.

title: Change the invoice numbering
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Numbering**.
2. Under **Invoices**, change the **Prefix** or **Next number**.
3. Select **Save**.

Harbour will not let you reuse a number that already exists.

title: Invite a team member
aliases: add an employee to the account
body:
Only an **Owner** or **Admin** can invite users.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Users**.
2. Select **Invite user**.
3. Enter their email and choose a **Role**.
4. Select **Send invite**.

The invite link is valid for 7 days.

title: Change a team member's role
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Users**.
2. Select the user.
3. Choose a new **Role**, such as **Admin**, **Standard** or **Read only**.
4. Select **Save**.

Need to undo this later?

title: Remove a team member
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Users**.
2. Select the user.
3. Select **Remove user**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Remove**.

Their past activity stays in the invoice history.

If something looks wrong afterwards, contact Harbour Support from **Help** and include a screenshot.

title: Change your login email
aliases: I changed jobs and need a new login
body:
1. Select your name at the bottom of the left menu, then **My profile**.
2. Enter your new **Email**.
3. Select **Save**.
4. Open the confirmation email and select the button inside it.

You will keep signing in with the old address until you confirm.

title: Reset your password
body:
1. On the sign-in page, select **Forgot password**.
2. Enter your email and select **Send reset link**.
3. Open the email and select **Choose new password**.
4. Enter and confirm your new password.

If you are already signed in, go to **My profile** and select **Change password**.

title: Download a backup of your account data
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Account**.
2. Select **Export all data**.
3. Choose the data to include, then select **Request export**.

We email a download link when it is ready. It expires after 48 hours.

Need to undo this later?

title: Archive a customer
aliases: hide a client I no longer bill
body:
Customers with invoices cannot be deleted, but they can be archived.

1. Go to **Customers** and open the customer.
2. Select **More**, then **Archive**.
3. Select **Archive customer**.

Archived customers are hidden from lists. Find them with the **Archived** filter and select **Restore** to bring them back.

title: Change your default currency
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Invoice defaults**.
2. Choose a **Default currency**.
3. Select **Save**.

This applies to new invoices only. Existing invoices keep their currency.

Need to undo this later?

title: See which reminders were sent for an invoice
aliases: did the customer get a reminder
body:
1. Open the invoice from **Invoices**.
2. Select the **Activity** tab.
3. Select the **Reminders** filter to see each reminder with its date and recipient.

A reminder that bounced is marked **Failed**, so you can fix the billing contact's email and resend it.

title: Update a subscriber's email address
aliases: fix a typo in someone's email
body:
Use this when a subscriber tells you their email address has changed.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers**.
2. Search for the subscriber and select their name.
3. Select **Edit profile**.
4. Type the new address in the **Email** field.
5. Select **Save changes**.

The subscriber keeps their history and list memberships.

title: Update a subscriber's phone number
aliases: edit phone number on a contact
body:
Keep mobile numbers current so text messages reach the right person.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers** and open the subscriber's profile.
2. Select **Edit profile**.
3. Enter the new number in **Mobile phone**, including the country code, for example +61.
4. Select **Save changes**.

If the subscriber had opted in to SMS, their opt-in carries over to the new number.

title: Add a subscriber manually
aliases: add a customer to my audience
body:
Add a single person without preparing an import file.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers**.
2. Select **Add subscriber**.
3. Enter at least an **Email** or **Mobile phone**.
4. Choose one or more lists under **Add to lists**.
5. Tick **This person has given consent** and select **Save**.

You cannot save a subscriber without confirming consent.

title: Delete a subscriber
body:
Deleting removes the subscriber and their activity from your account.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers**.
2. Select the subscriber's name.
3. Select **More actions** > **Delete subscriber**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.

Deleted subscribers cannot be recovered. If you only want to stop mailing someone, archive them instead.

title: Archive a subscriber
aliases: change a subscriber's status to archived
body:
Archiving keeps the record and its history but excludes the person from all sends.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers**.
2. Open the subscriber's profile.
3. Select **Status** and choose **Archived**.
4. Select **Save**.

Archived subscribers do not count towards your plan's subscriber limit.

title: Restore an archived subscriber
body:
You can bring an archived subscriber back to your active audience.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers**.
2. Select the **Status** filter and choose **Archived**.
3. Open the subscriber's profile.
4. Select **Status** > **Subscribed**, then **Save**.

Only restore people who have not unsubscribed.

title: Add a note to a subscriber
aliases: write a note on a contact
leave a comment on a customer
record a call on someone's profile
body:
Notes are visible to your team and never to the subscriber.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers** and open the subscriber's profile.
2. Select the **Notes** tab.
3. Select **Add note**.
4. Type your note.
5. Select **Save note**.

Each note shows who wrote it and when.

title: Merge duplicate subscribers
body:
Merge profiles when one person has been added twice.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers**.
2. Tick the two duplicate subscribers.
3. Select **More actions** > **Merge**.
4. Choose which profile to keep as the **Primary** record.
5. Select **Merge subscribers**.

Tags, list memberships and activity from both profiles are combined.

title: Add a tag to a subscriber
aliases: apply a tag to one person
body:
Tags are quick labels you can use later to build segments.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers** and open the subscriber's profile.
2. Select **Tags** in the right-hand panel.
3. Start typing a tag name and choose it, or press Enter to create a new one.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Remove a tag from a subscriber
aliases: take a label off a customer
body:
Removing a tag does not delete the tag itself or affect other subscribers.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers** and open the subscriber's profile.
2. Find **Tags** in the right-hand panel.
3. Select the **x** beside the tag you want to remove.
4. Select **Save**.

Segments that use the tag will update automatically.

title: Edit a subscriber's name
aliases: fix spelling of a customer name
update first name and last name
body:
Names are used for personalisation, so correct spellings matter.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers**.
2. Select the subscriber.
3. Select **Edit profile**.
4. Update **First name** and **Last name**.
5. Select **Save changes**.

New emails will use the updated name straight away.

title: Create a custom field
aliases: add a new field to contacts
body:
Custom fields let you store details such as birthday, company or membership number.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Fields**.
2. Select **Create field**.
3. Enter a **Field name**.
4. Choose a **Field type**: **Text**, **Number**, **Date** or **Dropdown**.
5. Select **Save field**.

The field appears on every subscriber profile.

title: Update a custom field value on a subscriber
aliases: fix company name on a profile
set a custom field for one person
body:
Change a stored detail for a single subscriber.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers** and open the subscriber's profile.
2. Select **Edit profile**.
3. Scroll to **Custom fields**.
4. Update the value you need.
5. Select **Save changes**. Changes are saved to the profile history.

title: View a subscriber's activity
body:
The activity timeline shows how someone has engaged with your messages.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers** and open the subscriber's profile.
2. Select the **Activity** tab.
3. Use the **Filter** menu to show **Emails**, **SMS** or **Forms**.
4. Select an item to see the campaign it came from.

Activity is listed with the newest first.

title: Find a subscriber
body:
Search works across names, email addresses and mobile numbers.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers**.
2. Type a name, email address or number in the **Search** box.
3. Press Enter.
4. Select a result to open the profile.

Use **Filters** beside the search box to narrow results by status, list or tag.

title: Change a subscriber's preferred language
body:
The preferred language decides which version of translated forms and unsubscribe pages a person sees.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers** and open the subscriber's profile.
2. Select **Edit profile**.
3. Choose a language from **Preferred language**.
4. Select **Save changes**.

title: See which lists a subscriber belongs to
aliases: check list membership for a contact
what lists is this customer on
body:
Check this before removing or moving someone.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers**.
2. Open the subscriber's profile.
3. Select the **Lists** tab.
4. Review the lists and the date they joined each one.

Select a list name to open it.

title: Clear a bounce status from a subscriber
body:
Subscribers are marked **Cleaned** when an email address bounces repeatedly. If you know the address works again, you can clear the status.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers**.
2. Filter **Status** by **Cleaned** and open the subscriber.
3. Select **More actions** > **Clear bounce status**.
4. Select **Confirm**.

If the address bounces again it will be cleaned again.

title: Update a team member's mobile number
aliases: edit my own mobile for sign-in codes
body:
Your mobile number receives sign-in codes and sending alerts.

1. Select your initials at the top right, then choose **My account**.
2. Select **Security**.
3. Under **Mobile number**, select **Change**.
4. Enter the new number and select **Send code**.
5. Enter the code you receive, then select **Verify**.

Account owners can update other team members from **Settings** > **Team**.

title: Update the billing contact for your account
body:
Invoices and payment reminders go to the billing contact.

1. Go to **Settings** > **Billing**.
2. Select **Billing contact**.
3. Select **Edit**.
4. Update the **Name** and **Email**.
5. Select **Save**.

Only account owners can change the billing contact. The new contact will be copied on future payment reminders and receipts.

title: Create a list
body:
Lists are the main way to organise who receives your campaigns.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Lists**.
2. Select **Create list**.
3. Enter a **List name** and a short **Description**.
4. Confirm the **Default sender** name and email.
5. Select **Save list**.

You can add subscribers once the list is created.

title: Rename a list
aliases: change the name of a list
body:
Renaming a list does not affect its subscribers or past campaigns.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Lists**.
2. Select the list you want to change.
3. Select **Settings**.
4. Edit the **List name**.
5. Select **Save**. The new name shows everywhere, including forms and the campaign audience picker.

title: Delete a list
body:
Deleting a list removes the grouping, not the people on it.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Lists**.
2. Select **More** beside the list.
3. Choose **Delete list**.
4. Choose whether to keep subscribers in your account or delete those who are on no other list.
5. Select **Delete**.

Scheduled campaigns that use the list will be paused.

title: Archive a list
aliases: retire a list but keep it
body:
Archive a list you no longer send to but want to keep for reporting.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Lists**.
2. Select **More** beside the list.
3. Choose **Archive list**.
4. Select **Archive** to confirm.

Archived lists appear under the **Archived** filter and can be restored at any time.

title: Add existing subscribers to a list
aliases: add customers to a mailing list
subscribe existing people to a list
body:
Use this for people already in your account.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers**.
2. Tick the subscribers you want.
3. Select **Add to list**.
4. Choose the list.
5. Select **Add**.

Only add people who have consented to receive messages from that list.

title: Remove a subscriber from a list
aliases: take a contact off a list
drop a customer from a mailing list
body:
Removing someone from a list does not delete them or unsubscribe them from other lists.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Lists** and open the list.
2. Find the subscriber.
3. Tick the box beside their name.
4. Select **Remove from list**.
5. Select **Remove** to confirm.

title: Move subscribers to another list
aliases: shift customers to a different list
body:
Moving adds people to the new list and removes them from the old one.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Lists** and open the current list.
2. Tick the subscribers you want to move.
3. Select **More actions** > **Move to list**.
4. Choose the destination list.
5. Select **Move**.

title: Copy subscribers to another list
aliases: duplicate contacts onto a second list
put the same people on two lists
body:
Copying keeps people on their original list as well.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Lists** and open the list.
2. Tick the subscribers you want to copy.
3. Select **More actions** > **Copy to list**.
4. Choose the destination list.
5. Select **Copy**.

title: Merge two lists
aliases: join two mailing lists into one
body:
Merging combines the members of two lists. Duplicates are counted once.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Lists**.
2. Tick the two lists you want to combine.
3. Select **Merge lists**.
4. Choose which list to keep and name the merged list.
5. Select **Merge**.

The list you do not keep is archived.

title: Create a segment
aliases: filter my audience into a group
target a section of my list
body:
Segments update automatically as subscribers meet your conditions.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Segments**.
2. Select **Create segment**.
3. Enter a **Segment name**.
4. Select **Add condition** and choose a field, such as **Tag** or **Country**.
5. Set the rule, then select **Save segment**.

Add more conditions and choose **Match all** or **Match any**.

title: Create a static segment from selected subscribers
aliases: make a fixed group of contacts
body:
A static segment is a fixed group that does not change when subscriber details change.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers**.
2. Tick the subscribers you want.
3. Select **Save as segment**.
4. Choose **Static**.
5. Enter a name and select **Save**.

title: Edit a segment's conditions
aliases: modify who is in a segment
body:
Changes apply to future sends and to the segment's member count straight away.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Segments**.
2. Select the segment.
3. Select **Edit conditions**.
4. Change, add or remove conditions.
5. Select **Save segment**.

Campaigns already sent are not affected.

title: Duplicate a segment
body:
Duplicating saves you rebuilding conditions from scratch.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Segments**.
2. Select **More** beside the segment.
3. Choose **Duplicate**.
4. Rename the copy and select **Save**.

The copy keeps all conditions and can be edited separately. This is handy when you want to test a slightly different audience.

title: Delete a segment
aliases: get rid of a saved filter
body:
Deleting a segment does not delete the subscribers inside it.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Segments**.
2. Select **More** beside the segment.
3. Choose **Delete segment**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.

Draft campaigns that target the segment will need a new audience.

title: Segment subscribers by engagement
aliases: target people who opened my emails
body:
Engagement segments help you reward active readers or win back quiet ones.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Segments** and select **Create segment**.
2. Select **Add condition** > **Campaign activity**.
3. Choose **Opened** or **Clicked** and set a time period, such as **in the last 30 days**.
4. Select **Save segment**.

Choose **Did not open** to find subscribers who have gone quiet.

title: Segment subscribers by location
aliases: group contacts by state or country
send to people in one region
body:
Location comes from the address fields on a profile or the sign-up form.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Segments** and select **Create segment**.
2. Select **Add condition** > **Location**.
3. Choose **Country**, **State** or **City**.
4. Enter the value, for example **Victoria**.
5. Select **Save segment**.

title: Preview who is in a segment
body:
Always check the size of a segment before you send.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Segments**.
2. Select the segment.
3. Select the **Members** tab to see the list of people.
4. Check the count shown at the top of the page.

The count refreshes automatically every few minutes.

title: Set the default sender for a list
aliases: change the from name on a list
update sender email for a list
body:
New campaigns sent to the list will use these details.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Lists** and open the list.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Under **Default sender**, update **From name**, **From email** and **Reply-to**.
4. Select **Save**.

The sender email must be on a verified domain.

title: Turn on double opt-in for a list
aliases: require email confirmation on a list
body:
With double opt-in, new subscribers must confirm by email before they are added.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Lists** and open the list.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Switch on **Require confirmation**.
4. Select **Edit confirmation email** to adjust the wording.
5. Select **Save**.

This applies to forms and manually added subscribers.

title: Import subscribers from a CSV file
aliases: bulk add customers from a spreadsheet
body:
Your file needs a header row and at least one column for email or mobile number.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Import**.
2. Select **Upload file** and choose your CSV.
3. Select **Next**, then match your columns to Harbour fields.
4. Confirm the consent statement.
5. Select **Start import**.

You will get an email when the import finishes.

title: Import subscribers from an Excel file
body:
Excel files (.xlsx) can be imported directly. Only the first sheet is read.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Import**.
2. Select **Upload file** and choose your .xlsx file.
3. Check the preview and select **Next**.
4. Map your columns and confirm consent.
5. Select **Start import**.

For very large files, CSV is faster.

title: Map columns during an import
body:
Mapping tells Harbour Mail which column holds which detail.

1. On the **Map columns** step of an import, find each column from your file.
2. Select the drop-down beside it and choose a field, such as **Email** or **Mobile phone**.
3. Choose **Do not import** for columns you do not need.
4. Select **Next**.

Select **Create custom field** to import data that has no matching field.

title: Choose a list when importing
aliases: add imported contacts to a list
body:
Choosing a list during import saves you adding people afterwards.

1. Start an import from **Audience** > **Import**.
2. Upload your file and map columns.
3. On the **Destination** step, choose **Add to existing list** or **Create new list**.
4. Select the list.
5. Select **Start import**.

title: Add tags during an import
aliases: label a batch of subscribers on upload
body:
Tagging imports makes it easy to find a batch later.

1. Start an import from **Audience** > **Import**.
2. On the **Destination** step, find **Tags**.
3. Type one or more tags, such as **Expo 2026**.
4. Select **Start import**.

All imported subscribers receive the tags, including those who already existed.

title: Update existing subscribers with an import
aliases: bulk edit phone numbers via csv
body:
You can update many profiles at once by importing a file with the new details.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Import** and upload your file.
2. Include a column for **Email** so rows can be matched.
3. On the **Existing subscribers** step, choose **Update existing**.
4. Select **Start import**.

Blank cells in your file are ignored and will not erase current values.

title: Download an import error report
aliases: why did rows fail to import
body:
Rows that cannot be imported are saved in an error report.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Import** and select **History**.
2. Find the import and select **View details**.
3. Select **Download error report**.
4. Correct the rows listed and import the corrected file.

Common causes are invalid email addresses and missing country codes on phone numbers.

title: Import mobile numbers for SMS
body:
Mobile numbers must include the country code, for example +61412345678.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Import** and upload your file.
2. Map the number column to **Mobile phone**.
3. Select **Default country** if your numbers do not start with a plus sign.
4. Confirm that you hold SMS consent for everyone in the file.
5. Select **Start import**.

title: Import an unsubscribe list
aliases: add suppressed emails from another system
body:
Bring over opt-outs from your old system so those people are never emailed.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Suppression**.
2. Select **Import**.
3. Upload a CSV with one email or number per row.
4. Select **Import to suppression list**.

Suppressed addresses are blocked from every send, even if they appear on a list.

title: View import history
aliases: check when a file was imported
body:
Import history shows every file uploaded, who uploaded it and the result.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Import**.
2. Select the **History** tab.
3. Select an import to see how many subscribers were added, updated or skipped.

History is kept for 12 months.

title: Undo an import
body:
Undoing removes only the subscribers added by that import. Existing subscribers stay as they are.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Import** > **History**.
2. Find the import.
3. Select **More** > **Undo import**.
4. Select **Undo** to confirm.

You can undo an import within 7 days of running it.

title: Export all subscribers to CSV
body:
Exports include every subscriber on your account.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers**.
2. Select **Export**.
3. Choose **All subscribers** and the **CSV** format.
4. Select **Start export**.

We email you a download link when the file is ready. Large exports can take a few minutes, so you can keep working while it runs.

title: Export a list
body:
Export just the people on one list.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Lists**.
2. Open the list.
3. Select **Export**.
4. Choose the fields to include.
5. Select **Start export**. The file is a CSV that opens in Excel or Google Sheets, and it includes each subscriber's status.

title: Export a segment
aliases: get a CSV of filtered contacts
body:
Segment exports reflect who matches at the moment you export.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Segments**.
2. Open the segment.
3. Select **Export**.
4. Choose the **CSV** format.
5. Select **Start export**. The file is a CSV that opens in Excel or Google Sheets. It includes each person's status and tags.

title: Export campaign results
aliases: get opens and clicks in a spreadsheet
body:
Campaign exports list each recipient with their opens, clicks and bounces.

1. Go to **Campaigns** and open a sent campaign.
2. Select the **Reports** tab.
3. Select **Export results**.
4. Choose **Recipients** or **Summary** and select **Export**. Choose **Recipients** for one row per person, or **Summary** for the totals only. The file arrives by email as a CSV.

title: Export your unsubscribes
body:
Keep a copy of opt-outs for your own records.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Suppression**.
2. Select the **Unsubscribed** tab.
3. Select **Export**.
4. Select **Start export**.

The file includes the date and the reason, where one was given. Keep the file somewhere secure, as it contains personal details.

title: Choose which fields to export
body:
Choose only the details you need in your file.

1. Select **Export** from any subscriber, list or segment page.
2. Select **Choose fields**.
3. Tick the fields to include, such as **Email**, **Mobile phone** and **Tags**.
4. Select **Start export**.

Your choices are remembered for next time.

title: Schedule a recurring export
body:
Recurring exports are emailed to you on a set day.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Export**.
2. Select **Schedule export**.
3. Choose the audience, fields and file format.
4. Set **Frequency** to **Daily**, **Weekly** or **Monthly**.
5. Select **Save schedule**.

title: Download a previous export
body:
Export files are kept for 14 days.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Export**.
2. Select the **History** tab.
3. Find your export and select **Download**.

If the file has expired, run the export again. Any team member with access to the **Audience** area can download it.

title: Sync subscribers from Harbour CRM
body:
Harbour Mail can bring over customer contacts from Harbour CRM.

1. Go to **Settings** > **Integrations**.
2. Select **Harbour CRM**, then **Connect**.
3. Choose the CRM contacts or groups to sync.
4. Choose the destination list.
5. Select **Start sync**.

Only contacts with marketing consent in the CRM are imported.

title: Create a sign-up form
body:
Forms add new subscribers straight to a list.

1. Go to **Forms**.
2. Select **Create form**.
3. Choose a type: **Embedded**, **Pop-up** or **Landing page**.
4. Choose the **Destination list**.
5. Select **Create**.

Then edit fields and styling before you publish.

title: Embed a form on your website
aliases: put signup form on my site
add subscribe box to a web page
body:
Embedding places the form directly on a page of your site.

1. Go to **Forms** and open the form.
2. Select **Publish**.
3. Select **Embed on website**.
4. Select **Copy embed snippet**.
5. Paste it where you want the form to appear on your page.

You do not need to paste it again after editing the form. Changes appear automatically.

title: Add a field to a form
aliases: ask for more info on signup
body:
Keep forms short to get more sign-ups.

1. Go to **Forms** and open the form.
2. Select **Fields**.
3. Select **Add field** and choose one, such as **Last name** or a custom field.
4. Drag it into position and select **Save**.

title: Remove a field from a form
aliases: take a box off the signup form
body:
The email field cannot be removed unless the form collects mobile numbers only.

1. Go to **Forms** and open the form.
2. Select **Fields**.
3. Hover over the field and select the **bin** icon.
4. Select **Save**. Removing a field does not delete any answers already collected. They stay on the subscriber profiles.

title: Change a form's colours and fonts
body:
Match the form to your website branding.

1. Go to **Forms** and open the form.
2. Select **Design**.
3. Choose a **Background**, **Button** and **Text** colour.
4. Choose a **Font**.
5. Select **Save**.

Use **Preview** to check the form on desktop and mobile.

title: Edit the thank-you message on a form
body:
This message appears after someone submits the form.

1. Go to **Forms** and open the form.
2. Select **Messages**.
3. Edit the text under **Thank-you message**.
4. Select **Save**.

If double opt-in is on, remind people to check their inbox.

title: Redirect to a page after sign-up
aliases: send people to a thank you page
body:
Send new subscribers to a page on your own site instead of a message.

1. Go to **Forms** and open the form.
2. Select **Messages**.
3. Switch on **Redirect after sign-up**.
4. Enter the page address.
5. Select **Save**. This replaces the thank-you message, so make sure the page tells people what happens next.

title: Create a pop-up form
body:
Pop-ups appear over your page after a trigger you choose.

1. Go to **Forms** and select **Create form**.
2. Choose **Pop-up**.
3. Under **Display**, choose a trigger: **After a delay**, **On scroll** or **On exit**.
4. Choose the **Destination list** and select **Create**.

Publish it with the website snippet from the **Publish** tab.

title: Collect mobile numbers on a form
aliases: get sms subscribers from a form
body:
Add a mobile field so people can join your SMS lists.

1. Go to **Forms** and open the form.
2. Select **Fields** > **Add field** > **Mobile phone**.
3. Switch on **SMS consent checkbox**.
4. Select **Save**.

The SMS consent checkbox is unticked by default, as required by law.

title: Add a consent checkbox to a form
aliases: add a tick box for permission
body:
A checkbox records clear permission from each subscriber.

1. Go to **Forms** and open the form.
2. Select **Fields** > **Add field** > **Consent checkbox**.
3. Edit the wording, for example **I agree to receive marketing emails**.
4. Switch on **Required**.
5. Select **Save**.

The wording is saved against each subscriber's consent history.

title: Change the list a form adds to
aliases: send signups to a different list
body:
New sign-ups go to whichever list is selected here.

1. Go to **Forms** and open the form.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Under **Destination list**, choose a different list.
4. Select **Save**.

Existing subscribers are not moved. The change applies to everyone who signs up from now on, including visitors who already have the form open.

title: Tag new subscribers from a form
aliases: label people who sign up on this form
body:
Tags tell you where each subscriber came from.

1. Go to **Forms** and open the form.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Under **Tags for new subscribers**, type one or more tags.
4. Select **Save**. You can then build a segment from the tag to see everyone who joined through this form.

title: Duplicate a form
aliases: make a variant of my form
body:
Duplicating is the quickest way to make a variant for A/B testing or another page.

1. Go to **Forms**.
2. Select **More** beside the form.
3. Choose **Duplicate**.
4. Rename the copy and select **Save**.

The copy starts as a draft.

title: Delete a form
body:
Deleting a form does not remove the subscribers who signed up through it.

1. Go to **Forms**.
2. Select **More** beside the form.
3. Choose **Delete form**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.

Any copies of the form on your website will stop working.

title: Unpublish a form
body:
Unpublishing stops the form accepting new sign-ups without deleting it.

1. Go to **Forms** and open the form.
2. Select **Publish**.
3. Select **Unpublish**.

Visitors will see a message that the form is closed. You can publish again at any time.

title: View form submissions
aliases: list people who used a form
body:
Submissions show everyone who has used the form.

1. Go to **Forms** and open the form.
2. Select the **Submissions** tab.
3. Use the date filter to narrow results.
4. Select a name to open the subscriber profile.

Select **Export** to download the submissions as a CSV.

title: Add spam protection to a form
body:
Spam protection reduces fake sign-ups.

1. Go to **Forms** and open the form.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Switch on **Spam protection**.
4. Choose **Invisible check** or **Tick-box check**.
5. Select **Save**. The invisible check works for most sites. If you still see fake sign-ups, switch to the tick-box check.

title: Edit the welcome email sent after sign-up
body:
This email is sent when someone subscribes through the form.

1. Go to **Forms** and open the form.
2. Select **Messages** > **Welcome email**.
3. Edit the subject and body.
4. Select **Send test** to check it.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Change a form's language
body:
You can show the form in a different language.

1. Go to **Forms** and open the form.
2. Select **Settings** > **Language**.
3. Choose the language.
4. Review the button and error messages.
5. Select **Save**. The form's button text, error messages and confirmation prompts all change to the language you choose.

title: Create a text-to-join keyword
aliases: set up a keyword for signups
body:
People send a keyword to your SMS number to join a list.

1. Go to **Forms** and select **Create form** > **Text to join**.
2. Enter a **Keyword**, for example **JOIN**.
3. Choose the **Destination list**.
4. Edit the **Reply message**, which must state how to opt out.
5. Select **Activate**.

Keywords must be unique to your account.

title: Unsubscribe a subscriber manually
aliases: a customer asked to be removed from emails
body:
Use this when someone asks you directly to stop receiving messages.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Subscribers** and open the subscriber's profile.
2. Select **Status** and choose **Unsubscribed**.
3. Choose the **Reason**, such as **Requested by email**.
4. Select **Save**.

The change takes effect immediately across all lists.

title: Resubscribe a subscriber
body:
You can only resubscribe someone who has asked to be added back.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Suppression** > **Unsubscribed**.
2. Select the subscriber.
3. Select **Resubscribe**.
4. Record how they gave permission, then select **Confirm**.

We recommend sending a confirmation email.

title: Customise the unsubscribe page
aliases: edit what people see when they opt out
body:
This is the page subscribers see after they select the unsubscribe link.

1. Go to **Settings** > **Compliance**.
2. Select **Unsubscribe page**.
3. Edit the **Heading**, **Message** and **Logo**.
4. Select **Save**.

Use **Preview** to check how it looks. Keep the page short. You can also add a link to your preference centre.

title: Add an unsubscribe link to an email
body:
Every marketing email must include an unsubscribe link.

1. Open the campaign in the editor.
2. Select the footer block.
3. Select **Insert** > **Unsubscribe link**.
4. Edit the link text if you like.
5. Select **Save**.

You will not be able to send a campaign without one.

title: View the unsubscribe list
body:
Review everyone who has opted out.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Suppression**.
2. Select the **Unsubscribed** tab.
3. Use **Search** or the date filter to find a person.

The list shows the date, channel (email or SMS) and the reason.

title: Add an address to the suppression list
aliases: block an email from ever being mailed
body:
Suppressed addresses are excluded from all sends.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Suppression**.
2. Select **Add address**.
3. Enter the email address or mobile number.
4. Choose a **Reason**.
5. Select **Add**. Use this for complaints, role addresses or anyone who has asked never to be contacted. The entry applies to every list.

title: Remove an address from the suppression list
aliases: take someone off do not contact
body:
Only remove addresses where the person has given fresh permission.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Suppression**.
2. Find the address.
3. Select **Remove** and confirm.

The person will not be added to a list automatically. The address will be sendable again straight away, so check you have fresh consent first.

title: Record consent for a subscriber
body:
Keep a record of when and how each person agreed to hear from you.

1. Open the subscriber's profile.
2. Select the **Consent** tab.
3. Select **Add consent record**.
4. Choose the **Channel**, **Source** and **Date**.
5. Select **Save**. Consent records are time-stamped and show which team member added them.

title: View a subscriber's consent history
aliases: see when a contact opted in
body:
The consent history is a time-stamped log of every opt-in and opt-out.

1. Open the subscriber's profile.
2. Select the **Consent** tab.
3. Review each entry, including the source and IP address.

Entries cannot be edited or deleted. You can show this to a regulator or the subscriber if they ask for proof of consent.

title: Set up SMS consent
body:
You need clear consent before sending marketing texts.

1. Go to **Settings** > **Compliance**.
2. Select **SMS consent**.
3. Switch on **Only send SMS to subscribers with recorded consent**.
4. Select **Save**.

Subscribers without SMS consent will be skipped in SMS campaigns.

title: Set up opt-out keywords for SMS
body:
Subscribers can reply to a text to opt out.

1. Go to **Settings** > **SMS**.
2. Select **Opt-out keywords**.
3. Add words such as **STOP** and **UNSUBSCRIBE**.
4. Edit the **Auto-reply** message.
5. Select **Save**.

STOP is always active and cannot be removed.

title: Delete a subscriber's data on request
body:
Use this when someone formally asks you to erase their personal data.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Privacy requests**.
2. Select **New request** > **Erase data**.
3. Enter the subscriber's email address.
4. Select **Erase permanently**.

Their address is kept in a hashed form on the suppression list so they are not re-added by mistake.

title: Export a subscriber's data on request
aliases: send someone a copy of their data
body:
Use this to respond to a data access request.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Privacy requests**.
2. Select **New request** > **Export data**.
3. Enter the subscriber's email address.
4. Select **Generate file**.

The file is a ZIP that you can send to the person.

title: Set up a preference centre
body:
A preference centre lets people choose what they hear about instead of unsubscribing.

1. Go to **Settings** > **Compliance**.
2. Select **Preference centre**.
3. Switch on **Enable preference centre**.
4. Tick the lists people can choose from.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Update a subscriber's list preferences for them
aliases: edit what a customer opted in to
body:
If a subscriber asks, you can change their preferences on their behalf.

1. Open the subscriber's profile.
2. Select the **Lists** tab.
3. Switch on or off each list.
4. Add a note about how the request was made.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Change the unsubscribe confirmation message
body:
This is the message shown after someone has successfully unsubscribed.

1. Go to **Settings** > **Compliance**.
2. Select **Unsubscribe page**.
3. Edit **Confirmation message**.
4. Select **Save**. Keep it short and polite, and avoid asking people to reconsider. Use **Preview** to check how it looks on mobile before you save.

title: View unsubscribe reasons
body:
If you ask why people leave, you can see the answers in one place.

1. Go to **Reports** > **Unsubscribes**.
2. Choose a date range.
3. Review the chart of **Reasons**.
4. Select **Export** to download the details. Reasons are only collected if you switched on the question on the unsubscribe page.

title: Turn on one-click unsubscribe
aliases: let mail apps show an unsubscribe button
body:
One-click unsubscribe adds a button in supported inbox apps.

1. Go to **Settings** > **Compliance**.
2. Switch on **One-click unsubscribe**.
3. Select **Save**.

This is recommended for all senders and helps your deliverability. Subscribers can then unsubscribe from the inbox app without opening your unsubscribe page, which also reduces spam complaints.

title: Set SMS quiet hours
body:
Quiet hours stop texts being sent at inconvenient times.

1. Go to **Settings** > **SMS**.
2. Select **Quiet hours**.
3. Choose a start and end time.
4. Choose the **Time zone** to use: yours or the subscriber's.
5. Select **Save**.

Messages scheduled in quiet hours are sent when they end.

title: Set the consent expiry period
aliases: stop mailing people after a long time
body:
Subscribers whose consent is older than your set period are paused automatically.

1. Go to **Settings** > **Compliance**.
2. Select **Consent expiry**.
3. Choose a period, for example **24 months**.
4. Choose whether to **Pause** or **Archive** expired subscribers.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Search for a subscriber within a list
aliases: find a contact on one list
look up a customer in a mailing list
body:
Searching inside a list is quicker than searching your whole audience when you know where someone belongs.

1. Go to **Audience** > **Lists** and open the list.
2. Type a name, email address or number in the **Search** box.
3. Press Enter.
4. Select a result to open the subscriber's profile.

Use **Filters** to narrow the list by status or tag.

title: Create an email campaign
aliases: set up a new email blast
body:
A campaign is a one-off email sent to a list or segment.

1. Go to **Campaigns**.
2. Select **New campaign**, then **Email**.
3. Enter a **Campaign name** and choose the **Audience**.
4. Add your subject line and choose a template.
5. Select **Save draft**.

You can come back and finish it at any time.

title: Schedule a campaign for later
aliases: send an email at a set time
body:
Scheduling lets you finish a campaign now and send it at the best time.

1. Open the campaign from **Campaigns**.
2. Go to the **Review and send** step.
3. Select **Schedule** instead of **Send now**.
4. Choose the date, time and time zone.
5. Select **Confirm schedule**.

The campaign status changes to **Scheduled**.

title: Change the send time of a scheduled campaign
aliases: change when a campaign goes out
body:
You can move a scheduled campaign to a new time without rebuilding it.

1. Go to **Campaigns** and open the **Scheduled** tab.
2. Select the campaign, then **Edit schedule**.
3. Choose a new date and time.
4. Select **Update schedule**.

If the new time has already passed, the campaign will not be saved.

title: Cancel a scheduled campaign
aliases: pull a mailout before it sends
body:
You can cancel a campaign any time before it starts sending.

1. Go to **Campaigns** and open the **Scheduled** tab.
2. Select the campaign.
3. Select **More**, then **Unschedule**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Move to drafts**.

The campaign returns to **Drafts** with all content intact, so you can reschedule it later.

title: Send a campaign immediately
body:
Use this when your campaign is ready and you do not need to wait.

1. Open the draft from **Campaigns**.
