2. Select **Review and send** and check the audience and subject line.
3. Select **Send now**.
4. Confirm in the dialog.

Sending cannot be undone once it starts, so check the preview first.

title: Send a test email
aliases: preview a campaign in my inbox
body:
Test emails show how your campaign looks in a real inbox.

1. Open the campaign in the editor.
2. Select **Preview and test**.
3. Select **Send test email**.
4. Enter up to five email addresses, separated by commas.
5. Select **Send**.

Test emails have [TEST] added to the subject line and do not count towards your reports.

title: Duplicate a campaign
body:
Duplicating saves time when you send a similar email regularly.

1. Go to **Campaigns**.
2. Find the campaign you want to copy.
3. Select **More**, then **Duplicate**.
4. Rename the copy and select **Create copy**.

The copy is saved as a draft and keeps the content, but not the schedule or results.

title: Delete a campaign
aliases: get rid of an old mailout
body:
You can delete drafts and sent campaigns you no longer need.

1. Go to **Campaigns**.
2. Select the checkbox next to the campaign.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete campaign** to confirm.

Deleting a sent campaign also removes its report, so export the results first if you need them.

title: Archive a sent campaign
aliases: move a mailout out of the way
body:
Archiving keeps the campaign and its report but hides it from your main list.

1. Go to **Campaigns** and open the **Sent** tab.
2. Select the campaign.
3. Select **More**, then **Archive**.

To see archived campaigns, select **Filters** and turn on **Show archived**.

title: Set up an A/B test on a subject line
body:
An A/B test sends two versions to a small share of your audience, then sends the winner to everyone else.

1. Create or open an email campaign.
2. On the **Subject** step, select **Add A/B test**.
3. Enter a subject line for version A and version B.
4. Set the **Test size** and the **Winning metric**, such as **Opens**.
5. Choose how long to wait before the winner is sent.

title: Choose who receives a campaign
aliases: select a list to send to
body:
Every campaign needs an audience before it can be sent.

1. Open the campaign and go to the **Audience** step.
2. Select **Choose audience**.
3. Pick one or more **Lists** or **Segments**.
4. To skip people, select **Exclude** and choose a list.
5. Select **Save audience**.

Harbour Mail shows the estimated number of recipients after duplicates are removed.

title: Skip subscribers who got an email recently
aliases: stop sending to people twice in a week
body:
This setting protects your engagement rates by limiting how often people hear from you.

1. Open the campaign and go to the **Audience** step.
2. Select **Sending limits**.
3. Turn on **Skip recent recipients**.
4. Choose the period, for example **3 days**.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Edit the subject line and preview text
aliases: rename the subject of a draft
body:
Both fields appear in the inbox before someone opens your email.

1. Open the draft from **Campaigns**.
2. Go to the **Subject** step.
3. Update **Subject line** and **Preview text**.
4. Select **Save**.

Keep the subject under 60 characters so it does not get cut off on phones.

title: Add a label to a campaign
aliases: add a note tag to a campaign
body:
Labels help you filter campaigns and compare reports by theme.

1. Go to **Campaigns** and open the campaign.
2. Select **Details**.
3. In **Labels**, type a name and press Enter.
4. Select **Save**.

To find labelled campaigns later, use **Filters** then **Label**.

title: Add an internal note to a campaign
aliases: leave a comment on a draft
write a note for my team
body:
Notes are visible to your team only and never appear in the email.

1. Open the campaign from **Campaigns**.
2. Select the **Notes** tab.
3. Type your note.
4. Select **Add note**.

Each note records your name and the date.

title: Export a campaign's recipients to CSV
body:
You can download the list of people a campaign was sent to.

1. Go to **Campaigns** and open a sent campaign.
2. Select the **Recipients** tab.
3. Select **Export**, then **CSV**.
4. Choose the columns you need and select **Download**.

The file is also emailed to you if it has more than 50,000 rows.

title: Resend a campaign to people who did not open it
body:
Resending can lift your overall open rate without writing a new email.

1. Go to **Campaigns** and open the **Sent** tab.
2. Select the campaign, then **More**, then **Resend to non-openers**.
3. Change the subject line if you wish.
4. Choose a send time and select **Confirm**.

You can resend each campaign once, at least 48 hours after the first send.

title: Create an email template
body:
Templates let your team reuse a consistent design.

1. Go to **Templates**.
2. Select **New template**.
3. Choose **Blank** or a starting layout.
4. Name the template and select **Create**.
5. Build your design in the editor, then select **Save**.

title: Save a campaign as a template
aliases: turn an email into a template
body:
Save a design you like so you can start from it again.

1. Open the campaign in the editor.
2. Select **Save** then **Save as template**.
3. Enter a **Template name**.
4. Select **Save template**.

The template appears under **Templates** and in the template picker for new campaigns.

title: Rename a template
body:
Clear names make templates easier to find.

1. Go to **Templates**.
2. Find the template and select **More**.
3. Select **Rename**.
4. Type the new name and select **Save**.

Campaigns already using the template are not affected. You can rename a template as often as you like, and the new name shows straight away in the template picker.

title: Duplicate a template
aliases: make a variant of a template
body:
Copy a template to try changes without touching the original.

1. Go to **Templates**.
2. Select **More** beside the template.
3. Select **Duplicate**.
4. Rename the copy and select **Create copy**.

The copy keeps all blocks, styles and images from the original, and appears at the top of your **Templates** list. You can then edit it freely without affecting the first version.

title: Delete a template
aliases: get rid of an old layout
body:
Deleting a template does not change campaigns that were built from it.

1. Go to **Templates**.
2. Select **More** beside the template.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete template** to confirm.

Deleted templates cannot be restored. If other people on your team use this template, check with them first.

title: Add an image to an email
aliases: put a photo in my newsletter
upload a graphic into the editor
body:
Images should be under 5 MB and at least 600 pixels wide.

1. In the editor, drag an **Image** block onto the canvas.
2. Select **Upload** or choose one from the **Image library**.
3. Add **Alt text** that describes the image.
4. Select **Insert**.

Alt text helps people using screen readers and shows when images are blocked.

title: Add a button to an email
aliases: put a link button in my email
body:
Buttons make your main call to action easy to tap.

1. In the editor, drag a **Button** block onto the canvas.
2. Select the block.
3. In the side panel, enter the **Button text** and **Link**.
4. Adjust the colour and shape under **Style**.

Use one clear button per section for the best click rates.

title: Personalise an email with the subscriber's first name
aliases: put someone's name in the greeting
body:
Merge tags are replaced with each subscriber's own details when the email is sent.

1. In the editor, click where you want the name.
2. Select **Insert merge tag**.
3. Choose **First name**.
4. Type a fallback such as **there**, for people with no name saved.

The email will then read, for example, Hi there.

title: Show content to certain subscribers only
aliases: hide a section for some people
body:
Conditional blocks let one email serve different audiences.

1. Select the block you want to restrict.
2. Select **Visibility** in the side panel.
3. Choose **Show only to** and pick a segment.
4. Select **Apply**.

Use the **Preview as subscriber** option to check the result.

title: Update the footer address and company name
aliases: fix the postal address in the footer
body:
Australian anti-spam law requires every marketing email to show who sent it.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **Email footer**.
2. Update the **Business name** and **Postal address**.
3. Select **Save**.

The change applies to new campaigns. Drafts need the footer block to be refreshed.

title: Add social media icons
aliases: link to Facebook from my email
body:
Social icons link readers to your profiles.

1. In the editor, drag a **Social** block onto the canvas.
2. Select the block.
3. Turn on each network you want.
4. Paste your profile address beside each icon.
5. Select **Done**.

title: Restore the unsubscribe link
body:
Every campaign must include an unsubscribe link before it can be sent.

1. In the editor, click where you want the link.
2. Select **Insert merge tag**.
3. Choose **Unsubscribe link**.
4. Select **Save**.

If you removed your footer block, you can drag in a new **Footer** block, which includes the link.

title: Preview an email on mobile
aliases: see how email looks on a phone
body:
Most subscribers read on their phones, so check the mobile layout before sending.

1. Open the campaign in the editor.
2. Select **Preview** at the top.
3. Select the **Mobile** icon.
4. Scroll through the preview to check images and buttons.

Use **Send test email** to check it on your actual phone.

title: Change fonts and colours across an email
body:
Global styles change the whole email at once.

1. In the editor, select **Styles**.
2. Choose a **Heading font** and **Body font**.
3. Pick colours for **Text**, **Links** and **Background**.
4. Select **Apply**.

Styles you set here apply to every block unless you override a block's own style. Web-safe fonts display most reliably across email apps.

title: Save your logo and brand colours
aliases: keep brand colours for all emails
body:
A brand kit makes your logo and colours available in every template.

1. Go to **Templates**, then **Brand kit**.
2. Upload your **Logo**.
3. Add your brand colours using hex codes.
4. Select **Save brand kit**.

After saving, your logo and colours appear as quick options inside the editor, so every email stays on brand.

title: Share a template with another team member
aliases: give a colleague access to a template
let my team use my layout
make a template available to all
body:
Sharing lets colleagues build on a design you have made.

1. Go to **Templates**.
2. Select **More** beside the template.
3. Select **Share**.
4. Choose **Entire team** or pick people by name.
5. Select **Save**.

Shared people can use the template but only editors can change it.

title: Edit the plain text version of an email
body:
Some email apps show only plain text, so it is good practice to check it.

1. Open the campaign in the editor.
2. Select **Content**, then **Plain text**.
3. Turn off **Generate automatically**.
4. Edit the text and select **Save**.

title: Create a welcome email automation
aliases: send an email to new subscribers
body:
A welcome automation sends an email as soon as someone joins a list.

1. Go to **Automations** and select **New automation**.
2. Choose the **Welcome new subscribers** recipe.
3. Select the **List** that triggers it.
4. Choose or design the email.
5. Select **Review**, then **Turn on**.

title: Send a birthday email automatically
body:
This automation uses the **Birthday** field on each subscriber.

1. Go to **Automations** and select **New automation**.
2. Choose the **Date-based** recipe, then **Birthday**.
3. Pick how many days before or after the date to send.
4. Choose the email and select **Turn on**.

Subscribers without a birthday saved are skipped.

title: Add a delay between automation emails
aliases: wait a few days between emails
body:
Delays stop a series from landing in one go.

1. Open the automation from **Automations**.
2. Select the **+** below the step you want to delay.
3. Choose **Wait**.
4. Enter the number of days or hours.
5. Select **Save**.

Changes only apply to people who enter the automation after you save.

title: Add an if/else branch to an automation
body:
Branches send people down different paths depending on what they have done.

1. Open the automation from **Automations**.
2. Select the **+** where you want to split the path.
3. Choose **If/else**.
4. Set the condition, such as **Opened previous email**.
5. Add steps to the **Yes** and **No** paths.

title: Pause an automation
aliases: turn off a workflow for now
body:
Pausing stops new people from entering, and holds anyone already in progress.

1. Go to **Automations**.
2. Find the automation and select the **Status** toggle.
3. Select **Pause** to confirm.

Select the toggle again to resume. People continue from where they stopped.

title: Delete an automation
aliases: get rid of an old automation
body:
Deleting an automation stops it immediately for everyone in progress.

1. Go to **Automations**.
2. Select **More** beside the automation.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete automation** to confirm.

If you may need it again, use **Pause** instead. Deleted automations cannot be restored, although emails already sent remain in your reports.

title: Duplicate an automation
body:
Duplicate an automation to build a similar one quickly.

1. Go to **Automations**.
2. Select **More** beside the automation.
3. Select **Duplicate**.
4. Name the copy and select **Create**.

The copy is created switched off, so you can change it safely.

title: Start an automation when a tag is added
aliases: run workflow when someone is tagged
body:
Tag triggers let you start a series whenever someone is labelled.

1. Open the automation and select the **Trigger** step.
2. Choose **Tag added**.
3. Pick the tag from the list.
4. Select **Save trigger**.

The tag must already exist under **Subscribers**, then **Tags**.

title: Set up an abandoned cart email
body:
This requires a connected online store under **Settings**, then **Integrations**.

1. Go to **Automations** and select **New automation**.
2. Choose **Abandoned cart**.
3. Set how long to wait after someone leaves, for example **2 hours**.
4. Select the email and choose **Turn on**.

title: Create a win-back automation for inactive subscribers
body:
Win-back emails give quiet subscribers a reason to return.

1. Go to **Automations** and select **New automation**.
2. Choose **Win-back**.
3. Define inactive, for example **No opens in 90 days**.
4. Choose the email.
5. Select **Turn on**.

Consider adding a step to remove people who still do not respond.

title: View automation performance
aliases: see how my workflow is doing
body:
Each automation has its own report.

1. Go to **Automations**.
2. Select the automation name.
3. Select the **Report** tab.
4. Choose a date range to see opens, clicks and the number of people who completed each step.

Select any step to see details of that email.

title: See who is currently in an automation
body:
You can check where each person is in the journey.

1. Go to **Automations** and open the automation.
2. Select the **People** tab.
3. Use **Filters** to show **In progress**, **Completed** or **Exited**.
4. Select a person's name to see their history.

title: Remove a subscriber from an automation
aliases: take someone out of a workflow
stop emails to one person in a journey
body:
Use this when one person should not receive the remaining steps.

1. Go to **Automations** and open the automation.
2. Select the **People** tab.
3. Tick the checkbox beside the person.
4. Select **Remove from automation**, then confirm.

The person stays on your list and can receive other emails.

title: Set an exit rule for an automation
aliases: finish the journey on a goal
body:
Exit rules remove people once they have done what the automation was meant to achieve.

1. Open the automation and select **Settings**.
2. Under **Exit rules**, select **Add rule**.
3. Choose an event, such as **Made a purchase**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Edit an email in a live automation
aliases: fix a typo in an automation
body:
You can fix content while an automation is running.

1. Go to **Automations** and open the automation.
2. Select the email step.
3. Select **Edit email**, make your changes, then select **Save**.
4. Select **Update automation** to publish.

New content only reaches people who have not yet received that step.

title: Rename an automation
body:
Renaming helps you keep a growing list of automations easy to scan.

1. Go to **Automations**.
2. Select the automation name.
3. Select the pencil icon beside the title.
4. Type the new name and press Enter.

The name is for your team only and is never shown to subscribers.

title: Send an SMS campaign
body:
You need an approved sender ID or number before sending.

1. Go to **SMS**, then **Campaigns**.
2. Select **New SMS campaign**.
3. Choose the **Audience**.
4. Type your message and select **Next**.
5. Choose **Send now** or **Schedule**.

Check the preview before you send, as texts cannot be recalled once they leave.

title: Schedule an SMS for later
aliases: send a text at a set time
body:
Scheduling lets you prepare a text now and send it at the right time.

1. Open the SMS draft from **SMS**, then **Campaigns**.
2. Select **Schedule**.
3. Choose the date, time and time zone.
4. Select **Confirm**.

Messages are not sent between 9 pm and 8 am in the recipient's local time.

title: Cancel a scheduled SMS
body:
You can cancel an SMS any time before it starts sending.

1. Go to **SMS**, then **Campaigns**.
2. Open the **Scheduled** tab.
3. Select the message, then **Unschedule**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Move to drafts**.

Any credits held for the message are returned to your balance.

title: Send a test SMS
aliases: preview a text on my phone
body:
Test texts show exactly what recipients will see on their phones.

1. Open the SMS draft.
2. Select **Send test**.
3. Enter a mobile number, in international format such as +61.
4. Select **Send**.

Test messages cost one SMS credit each.

title: Personalise an SMS with the customer's name
aliases: insert first name in a text
address people by name in a text
body:
Personalised texts tend to get better replies.

1. Open the SMS message editor.
2. Place your cursor where the name should go.
3. Select **Insert merge tag**.
4. Choose **First name** and add a fallback.
5. Select **Save**.

Names increase the message length, so check the character count.

title: Check SMS length and credits
aliases: how many characters in a text
why did my text use two credits
body:
A standard SMS holds 160 characters. Longer messages are split into parts, and emojis can lower the limit to 70.

1. Open the SMS editor.
2. Look below the message box at the **Characters** and **Credits** counters.
3. Shorten the text until the credits show **1**.

Credits are charged per recipient, per part.

title: Add a short link to an SMS
aliases: include a URL in a text
put a website in a text message
body:
Short links save characters and let you track clicks.

1. Open the SMS editor.
2. Select **Insert link**.
3. Paste the full web address.
4. Select **Shorten**.

Short links let you see clicks under **Reports**. Keep links short and clear, as people are less likely to tap a long or unfamiliar web address.

title: Add opt-out wording to an SMS
body:
Marketing texts in Australia must tell people how to opt out.

1. Open the SMS editor.
2. Select **Insert**, then **Opt-out text**.
3. Choose the wording, such as **Reply STOP to opt out**.
4. Select **Save**.

This wording counts towards your message length, so allow around 20 characters for it.

title: Check who has opted out of SMS
body:
When someone replies STOP, Harbour Mail stops texting them automatically.

1. Go to **Subscribers**.
2. Select **Filters**.
3. Choose **SMS status**, then **Opted out**.
4. Select **Apply**.

You can export this list with **Export**. People on this list cannot receive marketing texts until they opt back in themselves.

title: Update a subscriber's mobile number
body:
Correct numbers mean your texts reach the right person.

1. Go to **Subscribers** and search for the person.
2. Select their name.
3. Next to **Mobile**, select **Edit**.
4. Enter the new number in international format.
5. Select **Save**.

If the person was opted out, changing the number does not opt them back in.

title: Register an SMS sender ID
aliases: set up a sender name for texts
body:
A sender ID is the name, such as HARBOUR, shown instead of a phone number.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **SMS**.
2. Select **Add sender ID**.
3. Enter the name, using up to 11 letters and numbers.
4. Upload any proof requested and select **Submit**.

Approval usually takes two business days.

title: Get a dedicated mobile number
aliases: lease a number for two-way SMS
buy a number to text from
get a number people can reply to
body:
A dedicated number lets customers reply to your messages.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **SMS**.
2. Select **Get a number**.
3. Pick a number from the list.
4. Select **Confirm and subscribe**.

Monthly fees show on your next invoice. Pick a number that matches your region so replies and local delivery work well.

title: Read replies to your SMS
body:
Replies from subscribers arrive in one shared inbox.

1. Go to **SMS**, then **Inbox**.
2. Select a conversation to read it.
3. Use **Unread** to see new replies.
4. Select **Reply** to answer.

Replies are sent from your dedicated number.

title: Assign an SMS conversation to a team member
aliases: hand a customer text to a colleague
give a reply to someone else
body:
Assigning makes it clear who is responsible for a reply.

1. Go to **SMS**, then **Inbox**.
2. Open the conversation.
3. Select **Assign**.
4. Choose a team member and select **Save**.

The person receives a notification. You can reassign it again whenever needed, and the full message history stays attached.

title: Save an SMS template
body:
Templates save you retyping messages you send often.

1. Go to **SMS**, then **Templates**.
2. Select **New SMS template**.
3. Enter a name and the message.
4. Select **Save**.

Templates are available when you create any SMS campaign. Keep your template short, and use merge tags for names to make each message feel personal.

title: Top up SMS credits
body:
You need credits in your balance to send texts.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **Billing**.
2. Select **SMS credits**.
3. Choose a pack, or turn on **Auto top-up**.
4. Select **Pay now**.

Credits do not expire. You will receive a receipt by email, and the new balance shows at the top of the **SMS** page.

title: Export an SMS delivery report
body:
The delivery report shows what happened to every message.

1. Go to **SMS**, then **Campaigns**.
2. Open a sent campaign.
3. Select **Delivery report**.
4. Select **Export**, then **CSV**.

The report lists each recipient as **Delivered**, **Failed** or **Pending**. Failed messages include a reason, such as an invalid number, to help you fix your list.

title: View a campaign report
body:
Reports show how recipients engaged with each campaign.

1. Go to **Reports**, then **Campaigns**.
2. Select the campaign name.
3. Review **Opens**, **Clicks**, **Bounces** and **Unsubscribes** on the **Overview** tab.
4. Use the date picker to change the period.

Opens can take up to 24 hours to settle fully.

title: Export a campaign report to CSV
body:
Export results to share them or analyse them in a spreadsheet.

1. Go to **Reports**, then **Campaigns**.
2. Open the campaign.
3. Select **Export**.
4. Choose **CSV** or **PDF** and select **Download**.

The CSV includes totals for each metric as well as a row for every link in the email, which makes it easy to share with colleagues who do not use Harbour Mail.

title: Compare two campaigns side by side
body:
Comparing campaigns shows what works best for your audience.

1. Go to **Reports**, then **Campaigns**.
2. Tick the checkboxes beside two to four campaigns.
3. Select **Compare**.
4. Switch between **Rates** and **Totals** at the top.

Comparison works best when the campaigns went to similar audiences, so keep that in mind when drawing conclusions.

title: See which links were clicked
aliases: check link clicks in an email
body:
The click map shows your email with a percentage next to each link.

1. Open the campaign report from **Reports**.
2. Select the **Links** tab.
3. Choose **Click map** to see the overlay, or **List** for a table.

Select a link to see who clicked it.

title: See which subscribers clicked a link
body:
You can build a follow-up audience from people who showed interest.

1. Open the campaign report from **Reports**.
2. Select the **Links** tab, then the link name.
3. Select **View clickers**.
4. Select **Create segment** if you want to email them again.

title: View bounced email addresses
body:
A bounce happens when an email cannot be delivered. Soft bounces are temporary and hard bounces are permanent.

1. Go to **Reports**, then **Deliverability**.
2. Select the **Bounces** tab.
3. Use the **Type** filter to choose **Hard** or **Soft**.
4. Select a row for the reason given by the receiving server.

title: Remove hard-bounced subscribers
aliases: clean my list of bad emails
body:
Removing permanently failed addresses keeps your list healthy.

1. Go to **Reports**, then **Deliverability**.
2. Select the **Bounces** tab and filter by **Hard**.
3. Select all rows using the top checkbox.
4. Select **Remove from list**.

Harbour Mail already stops sending to hard bounces, so this simply keeps your list clean.

title: Remove subscribers who never open your emails
body:
Removing unengaged people can improve your deliverability.

1. Go to **Subscribers**, then **Segments**.
2. Select **New segment**.
3. Set **Opens** to **0** in the last **180 days**.
4. Save the segment, then select **Actions**, then **Remove from list**.

Removed people can be added back later, but only if they have given permission to hear from you again.

title: Check spam complaints
aliases: see who marked me as spam
body:
A complaint rate above 0.1 per cent can harm your sender reputation.

1. Go to **Reports**, then **Deliverability**.
2. Select the **Complaints** tab.
3. Choose a date range.
4. Select a row to see the campaign it relates to.

People who complain are unsubscribed automatically.

title: Authenticate your sending domain
body:
Authentication proves to inbox providers that you are allowed to send from your domain.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **Domains**.
2. Select **Add domain** and enter your domain name.
3. Copy the **SPF** and **DKIM** records shown.
4. Add them in your domain provider's DNS settings.
5. Return and select **Verify**.

DNS changes can take up to 48 hours.

title: Add a DMARC record
body:
DMARC tells inbox providers what to do with emails that fail authentication.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **Domains**.
2. Select your domain, then **DMARC**.
3. Choose a policy, starting with **None**.
4. Copy the record and add it to your DNS.
5. Select **Check record**.

title: Check your deliverability score
body:
The score summarises how inbox providers are likely to treat your email.

1. Go to **Reports**, then **Deliverability**.
2. Select the **Overview** tab.
3. Read your **Sender score** and the checklist of suggestions beneath it.
4. Select any item to see how to fix it.

The score updates daily.

title: Email a report to your team on a schedule
body:
Scheduled reports arrive in your inbox without logging in.

1. Go to **Reports**, then **Scheduled reports**.
2. Select **New scheduled report**.
3. Choose the report and how often it should arrive.
4. Add recipient email addresses.
5. Select **Save**.

You can edit or stop the schedule at any time from the same page.

title: Add UTM tracking to links
body:
UTM parameters show which campaigns drive visits to your website.

1. Open the campaign and go to the **Tracking** step.
2. Turn on **Add UTM parameters**.
3. Check the **Source**, **Medium** and **Campaign** values.
4. Select **Save**.

The parameters are added to all links when the email is sent.

title: Turn off open tracking
body:
Some organisations prefer not to track opens.

1. Open the campaign and go to the **Tracking** step.
2. Turn off **Track opens**.
3. Select **Save**.

Open rates will no longer appear for this campaign. To change the default for all campaigns, go to **Settings**, then **Tracking**.

title: See who unsubscribed from a campaign
body:
Reviewing unsubscribes helps you spot content that is not working.

1. Go to **Reports**, then **Campaigns** and open the campaign.
2. Select the **Unsubscribes** tab.
3. Review the list and any reasons they gave.
4. Select **Export** to download it.

title: See which devices and email apps people use
body:
Audience insights show how your subscribers read email.

1. Go to **Reports**, then **Audience insights**.
2. Select **Devices**.
3. Switch between **Device type** and **Email app**.
4. Choose a date range.

Use this to decide whether to focus on mobile layouts.

title: Change the sender name
body:
The sender name appears in the inbox before your subject line.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **Sender details**.
2. Select **Edit** beside **Sender name**.
3. Type the new name.
4. Select **Save**.

New campaigns use the updated name. Existing drafts keep the old one until you change it on the **Subject** step.

title: Change the sender email address
body:
A new sender address must be verified before you can use it.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **Sender details**.
2. Select **Add sender address**.
3. Enter the new email address.
4. Select **Send verification** and open the email we send you.
5. Select the confirmation button.

You can then set it as your default.

title: Verify a sender address that shows Pending
body:
A sender address stays pending until its owner confirms it.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **Sender details**.
2. Find the address marked **Pending**.
3. Select **Resend verification**.
4. Open the email and select **Confirm address**.

Check your spam or junk folder if it does not arrive within a few minutes.

title: Set a different reply-to address
body:
The reply-to address receives responses, even if it differs from your sender address.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **Sender details**.
2. Select **Edit** beside **Reply-to address**.
3. Enter the address.
4. Select **Save**.

Use a monitored inbox so customer replies are not missed. Changes apply to new campaigns straight away.

title: Invite an employee to your account
body:
Team members can work on campaigns with their own login.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **Team**.
2. Select **Invite member**.
3. Enter their name and email address.
4. Choose a role: **Admin**, **Editor** or **Viewer**.
5. Select **Send invitation**.

The invitation expires after seven days.

title: Remove a team member
aliases: revoke access for someone who left
take an employee off my account
body:
Remove access when someone leaves your organisation.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **Team**.
2. Find the person and select **More**.
3. Select **Remove from account**.
4. Select **Remove** to confirm.

Campaigns they created stay on your account. The person loses access straight away, and any active sessions are signed out.

title: Change the billing contact
body:
The billing contact receives invoices and payment notices.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **Billing**.
2. Select **Billing contact**, then **Edit**.
3. Enter the new name and email address.
4. Select **Save**.

Only account owners and admins can change this, and a confirmation email is sent to the new contact so they know about the change.

title: Update your payment card
body:
Replace your card before it expires so your plan is not interrupted.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **Billing**.
2. Select **Payment method**.
3. Select **Replace card**.
4. Enter the new card details and select **Save card**.

Your next invoice will be charged to the new card.

title: Download an invoice
body:
All past invoices are kept in your account.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **Billing**.
2. Select **Invoice history**.
3. Find the invoice by date.
4. Select **Download PDF**.

Invoices show your plan and any SMS credit purchases. If you need invoices in a different name, change the billing contact first.

title: Turn on two-factor authentication
body:
Two-factor authentication adds a code to your sign-in.

1. Select your profile picture, then **My account**.
2. Select **Security**.
3. Turn on **Two-factor authentication**.
4. Scan the QR code with an authenticator app.
5. Enter the six-digit code and select **Verify**.

Save your backup codes in a safe place.

title: Add a tag to subscribers
body:
Tags group subscribers so you can target them later.

1. Go to **Subscribers**.
2. Tick the checkbox beside each person.
3. Select **Actions**, then **Add tag**.
4. Choose a tag or type a new one.
5. Select **Apply**.

You can use tags later to build segments, start automations or filter reports.

title: Export subscribers to CSV
aliases: get my list as a spreadsheet
body:
Export your list to back it up or use it elsewhere.

1. Go to **Subscribers**.
2. Optionally use **Filters** or choose a **Segment**.
3. Select **Export**, then **CSV**.
4. Choose the fields and select **Download**.

Exports include each person's status, so unsubscribed people are marked clearly. Large lists may arrive by email.

title: Delete a subscriber permanently
body:
Deleting removes the person and their history for good.

1. Go to **Subscribers** and search for the person.
2. Select their name.
3. Select **More**, then **Delete subscriber**.
4. Type **DELETE** to confirm.

If you only want to stop emailing them, unsubscribe them instead.

title: Update an employee's phone number
aliases: new phone number for a staff member
fix wrong phone number on profile
body:
Keep contact details current so managers can reach their teams.

1. Go to **People** and select the employee's name.
2. Open the **Personal** tab.
3. Select **Edit** next to **Contact details**.
4. Enter the new number in **Mobile phone**.
5. Select **Save changes**.

The change is recorded in the profile's history.

title: Update an employee's email address
aliases: switch to a new email address
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee's profile.
2. Select the **Personal** tab, then **Edit** next to **Contact details**.
3. Choose **Work email** or **Personal email**.
4. Type the new address and select **Save changes**.

If you change the work email, the employee uses the new address the next time they sign in.

title: Update an employee's home address
body:
A correct address matters for payslips and tax statements.

1. Go to **People** and select the employee.
2. Open the **Personal** tab.
3. Select **Edit** beside **Home address**.
4. Fill in **Street**, **Suburb**, **State** and **Postcode**.
5. Select **Save changes**.

title: Change an employee's preferred name
aliases: display name instead of legal name
body:
The preferred name appears in the directory and org chart. The legal name stays on payroll records.

1. Go to **People** and open the profile.
2. Select the **Personal** tab, then **Edit** next to **Name**.
3. Type a name in **Preferred name**.
4. Select **Save changes**.

title: Upload an employee's profile photo
aliases: add a picture to a profile
body:
1. Go to **People** and select the employee.
2. Select the circle at the top of the profile.
3. Choose **Upload photo** and pick a JPG or PNG file under 5 MB.
4. Drag the frame to crop the image.
5. Select **Save photo**.

Employees can also change their own photo from **My profile**.

title: Add a new employee
body:
Use this when you need a profile without starting a full onboarding checklist.

1. Go to **People** and select **Add employee**.
2. Enter the **First name**, **Last name** and **Work email**.
3. Choose a **Department**, **Job title** and **Start date**.
4. Select **Employment type**.
5. Select **Create employee**.

The new profile appears in the **People** list with the status **Active**.

title: Delete an employee record
body:
Deleting removes the profile and its documents for good. For people who have left, use offboarding instead.

1. Go to **People** and open the profile.
2. Select **More actions**, then **Delete employee**.
3. Read the warning and type the employee's full name to confirm.
4. Select **Delete permanently**.

Employees with payroll history can't be deleted. Archive them instead.

title: Export the employee list to CSV
body:
1. Go to **People**.
2. Use **Filters** to narrow the list if needed, for example by **Department** or **Status**.
3. Select **Export**, then **CSV**.
4. Tick the columns you want, such as **Name**, **Email** and **Start date**.
5. Select **Download**.

The file saves to your browser's download folder.

title: Add a note to an employee's profile
aliases: write a note on a staff member
record a comment about an employee
body:
Notes are private to HR admins and the employee's manager unless you change the visibility.

1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Notes** tab.
3. Select **Add note**.
4. Type your note and choose **Visible to**: **HR only** or **HR and manager**.
5. Select **Save note**.

title: Change an employee's status
body:
Statuses include **Active**, **On leave** and **Inactive**.

1. Go to **People** and open the profile.
2. Select the **Job** tab.
3. Select **Edit** next to **Status**.
4. Pick the new status and enter the **Effective date**.
5. Select **Save changes**.

Leavers should be handled through offboarding rather than set to **Inactive** by hand.

title: Change an employee's job title
body:
1. Go to **People** and select the employee.
2. Open the **Job** tab.
3. Select **Edit** next to **Job title**.
4. Type the new title and set the **Effective date**.
5. Select **Save changes**.

Past titles stay visible under **Job history**.

title: Update an employee's bank details
body:
Bank details control where wages are paid, so check them carefully.

1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Pay** tab.
3. Select **Edit** beside **Bank account**.
4. Enter the **BSB**, **Account number** and **Account name**.
5. Select **Save changes**.

Changes made within one day of a pay run apply to the next pay run.

title: Update an employee's tax details
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the profile.
2. Select the **Pay** tab.
3. Select **Edit** next to **Tax details**.
4. Update the **Tax file number** or **Tax-free threshold** answer.
5. Select **Save changes**.

Only HR admins with payroll access can see this section.

title: Search for an employee
body:
1. Select the search box at the top of any page.
2. Type a name, email address or job title.
3. Choose the person from the results.
4. To narrow the search, select **People** and use **Filters**.

Search also matches preferred names and former names.

title: Merge duplicate employee profiles
body:
Merging keeps one profile and moves documents, notes and history from the other.

1. Go to **People** and select both duplicate profiles using the tick boxes.
2. Select **Merge**.
3. Choose the profile to keep as the **Primary record**.
4. Review any conflicting fields and pick the correct value for each.
5. Select **Merge profiles**.

Merging can't be undone.

title: Add pronouns to an employee's profile
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the profile.
2. Select the **Personal** tab, then **Edit** next to **Name**.
3. Choose from the **Pronouns** list or select **Other** to type your own.
4. Select **Save changes**.

Pronouns show next to the name in the directory unless the employee hides them.

title: Change an employee's employment type
body:
Use this when someone's arrangement changes, such as moving from casual to permanent.

1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Job** tab.
3. Select **Edit** next to **Employment type**.
4. Choose **Full-time**, **Part-time**, **Casual** or **Contractor**.
5. Enter the **Effective date** and select **Save changes**.

title: View an employee's profile change history
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the profile.
2. Select **More actions**, then **View history**.
3. Filter by **Date range** or **Field** if you need to.
4. Select an entry to see the old value, the new value and who made the change.

title: Choose who can see an employee's personal details
body:
You control which fields show in the company directory.

1. Go to **Settings**, then **Employee profiles**.
2. Select **Directory privacy**.
3. Switch each field to **Everyone**, **Managers only** or **HR only**.
4. Select **Save changes**.

The changes apply to all employees straight away.

title: Reactivate a former employee
body:
Rehiring restores the old profile, so history and documents are kept.

1. Go to **People** and select the **Former employees** filter.
2. Open the person's profile.
3. Select **Rehire**.
4. Enter the new **Start date**, **Job title** and **Department**.
5. Select **Reactivate employee**.

title: Create an onboarding checklist template
aliases: make a template for new hires
body:
1. Go to **Onboarding**, then **Templates**.
2. Select **New template** and enter a name, such as "Sales starter".
3. Select **Add task** for each step and set a **Due date** relative to the start date.
4. Choose an **Owner** for each task.
5. Select **Save template**.

title: Start onboarding for a new hire
body:
1. Go to **Onboarding** and select **Start onboarding**.
2. Choose the employee, or select **Add employee** if they don't have a profile yet.
3. Pick a **Template**.
4. Confirm the **Start date**.
5. Select **Start**.

Task owners are notified by email straight away.

title: Assign an onboarding task to someone else
aliases: give a checklist task to IT
body:
1. Go to **Onboarding** and open the new hire's checklist.
2. Select the task.
3. Choose a new person in **Owner**.
4. Select **Save**.

The new owner receives an email with the task details and due date.

title: Mark an onboarding task as complete
body:
1. Go to **Onboarding** and open the checklist.
2. Find the task.
3. Tick the box beside it, or open it and set **Status** to **Done**.
4. Add a short comment if you wish and select **Save**.

Progress bars update immediately.

title: Send a welcome email to a new hire
body:
The welcome email includes a sign-in link and your first-day details.

1. Go to **Onboarding** and open the new hire's checklist.
2. Select **Welcome email**.
3. Edit the message if needed and check the **Send date**.
4. Select **Send now** or **Schedule**.

title: Change a new hire's start date
body:
1. Go to **Onboarding** and open the checklist.
2. Select **Edit** next to **Start date**.
3. Choose the new date.
4. Tick **Adjust task due dates** to move every task with it.
5. Select **Save changes**.

title: Add a task to a live onboarding checklist
body:
Changes affect this employee only, not the template.

1. Go to **Onboarding** and open the checklist.
2. Select **Add task**.
3. Enter a **Task name**, **Owner** and **Due date**.
4. Select **Add**.

You need the **HR admin** role to do this.

title: Assign a buddy to a new hire
aliases: pair new starter with a mentor
body:
1. Go to **Onboarding** and open the checklist.
2. Select **Buddy** in the right-hand panel.
3. Search for a colleague and select their name.
4. Select **Assign buddy**.

The buddy gets an email with the new hire's name and first-day plans.

title: Resend an onboarding invitation
aliases: new hire didn't get the email
body:
1. Go to **Onboarding** and open the new hire's checklist.
2. Select **More actions**, then **Resend invitation**.
3. Check the email address shown and edit it if it's wrong.
4. Select **Send**.

Invitation links stay valid for 7 days.

title: Cancel an onboarding
body:
Cancelling stops reminders and removes the checklist. The employee profile is kept.

1. Go to **Onboarding** and open the checklist.
2. Select **More actions**, then **Cancel onboarding**.
3. Choose a reason from the **Reason** list.
4. Select **Confirm cancellation**.

title: Export onboarding progress to CSV
body:
1. Go to **Onboarding**.
2. Select the **Progress** view.
3. Filter by **Start date** or **Department**.
4. Select **Export**, then **CSV**.

Each row shows one task, its owner and its status.

title: Add a note to an onboarding task
aliases: leave a message on a task
body:
1. Go to **Onboarding** and open the checklist.
2. Select the task.
3. Type your message in the **Comments** box.
4. Select **Post**.

Everyone who can see the checklist can read the comment.

You need the **HR admin** role to do this.

title: Start offboarding for a leaver
body:
1. Go to **Offboarding** and select **Start offboarding**.
2. Choose the employee.
3. Select the **Reason for leaving**.
4. Enter the **Last working day**.
5. Pick an offboarding **Template** and select **Start**.

title: Change a leaver's last working day
body:
1. Go to **Offboarding** and open the leaver's checklist.
2. Select **Edit** next to **Last working day**.
3. Choose the new date.
4. Select **Save changes**.

Task due dates linked to the last day move automatically.

title: Record an employee's reason for leaving
body:
1. Go to **Offboarding** and open the checklist.
2. Select **Edit** beside **Reason for leaving**.
3. Choose a category, such as **Resignation**, **Redundancy** or **End of contract**.
4. Add details in **Comments** if needed.
5. Select **Save**.

These reasons feed the **Turnover** report.

title: Create an offboarding checklist template
body:
1. Go to **Offboarding**, then **Templates**.
2. Select **New template** and enter a name.
3. Select **Add task** for items like "Return laptop" or "Final pay".
4. Set an **Owner** and a **Due date** for each task.
5. Select **Save template**.

title: Remove a leaver's system access
body:
Harbour People can switch off the employee's sign-in on their last day.

1. Go to **Offboarding** and open the leaver's checklist.
2. Select **Access**.
3. Choose **Disable sign-in on last working day**, or **Disable now**.
4. Select **Save**.

You need the **HR admin** role to do this.

title: Schedule an exit interview
body:
1. Go to **Offboarding** and open the checklist.
2. Select the **Exit interview** task.
3. Choose a **Date**, **Time** and **Interviewer**.
4. Select **Send invitation**.

The interviewer and the employee both receive a calendar invite.

title: Flag a leaver for final pay
body:
Flagging makes sure payroll includes accrued leave and any outstanding pay.

1. Go to **Offboarding** and open the leaver's checklist.
2. Select the **Final pay** task.
3. Tick **Pay out leave balance** if it applies.
4. Select **Send to payroll**.

title: Reverse an offboarding
body:
1. Go to **Offboarding** and open the leaver's checklist.
2. Select **More actions**, then **Cancel offboarding**.
3. Choose the reason.
4. Select **Confirm**.

The employee's status goes back to **Active**.

title: Upload a document to an employee's profile
aliases: attach a file to a staff record
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Documents** tab.
3. Select **Upload document**.
4. Choose the file, then pick a **Category** such as **Contract** or **Identification**.
5. Select **Upload**.

Files can be up to 25 MB.

title: Delete a document
aliases: get rid of an uploaded file
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Documents** tab.
3. Select the three dots beside the file, then **Delete**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Delete document**.

Deleted documents stay in the **Recycle bin** for 30 days.

You need the **HR admin** role to do this.

title: Download a document
aliases: save a copy of a file
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Documents** tab.
3. Find the file, using **Search** if needed.
4. Select the three dots, then **Download**.

title: Rename a document
aliases: fix a typo in a document name
body:
1. Open the **Documents** tab on the employee's profile.
2. Select the three dots beside the file.
3. Choose **Rename**.
4. Type the new name and select **Save**.

Renaming doesn't change the file itself.

title: Set an expiry date on a document
body:
Expiry dates let Harbour People remind you before something lapses, such as a working visa.

1. Open the **Documents** tab on the employee's profile.
2. Select the three dots beside the document, then **Edit details**.
3. Enter a date in **Expires on**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Request a document from an employee
aliases: ask staff to upload a file
get a signed form from new hire
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Documents** tab, then **Request document**.
3. Choose a **Category** and write a short message.
4. Set a **Due date**.
5. Select **Send request**.

The employee uploads the file from **My documents**.

title: Send a document for e-signature
body:
1. Open the **Documents** tab on the employee's profile.
2. Select the document, then **Request signature**.
3. Add any extra signers, such as the manager.
4. Select **Send**.

Signed copies are saved to the profile automatically.

You need the **HR admin** role to do this.

title: Create a document template
body:
Templates use merge fields such as {{first_name}} so each document is filled in for you.

1. Go to **Documents**, then **Templates**.
2. Select **New template**.
3. Name the template and choose a **Category**.
4. Write or paste the text and insert merge fields with **Add field**.
5. Select **Save template**.

title: Add a document category
body:
1. Go to **Settings**, then **Documents**.
2. Select **Categories**.
3. Select **Add category**.
4. Enter a name and choose who can see it: **HR only** or **Employee and HR**.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Export a list of documents to CSV
body:
1. Go to **Documents**.
2. Choose a **Category** or **Date range** to filter the list.
3. Select **Export**, then **CSV**.
4. Select **Download**.

The export lists file names, owners and expiry dates, not the files themselves.

title: Add a note to a document
aliases: write a note against a document
body:
1. Open the **Documents** tab on the employee's profile.
2. Select the document name.
3. In the side panel, select **Add note**.
4. Type your note and select **Save**.

title: Replace a document with a new version
body:
1. Open the **Documents** tab on the employee's profile.
2. Select the three dots beside the file, then **Upload new version**.
3. Choose the updated file.
4. Add a **Version note** and select **Upload**.

The earlier version is kept in the version history.

title: View a document's version history
aliases: see old versions of a file
body:
1. Open the **Documents** tab on the employee's profile.
2. Select the document name.
3. Select **Version history**.
4. Select a version to preview it, or choose **Restore** to make it current.

title: Make a document visible to HR only
body:
1. Open the **Documents** tab on the employee's profile.
2. Select the three dots beside the file, then **Edit details**.
3. Change **Visible to** to **HR only**.
4. Select **Save**.

The employee and their manager will no longer see the file.

title: Upload several documents at once
body:
1. Go to **Documents** and select **Bulk upload**.
2. Drag your files into the box.
3. Match each file to an employee using the **Employee** column.
4. Choose a **Category** and select **Upload all**.

Name each file with the employee's number to match automatically.

title: Share a company policy with all employees
body:
1. Go to **Documents**, then **Company documents**.
2. Select **Add policy** and upload the file.
3. Choose who to share it with: **All employees** or a **Department**.
4. Select **Publish**.

title: Check who has acknowledged a policy
body:
1. Go to **Documents**, then **Company documents**.
2. Open the policy.
3. Select the **Acknowledgements** tab.
4. Filter by **Not yet acknowledged**.
5. Select **Send reminder** to nudge those employees.

You need the **HR admin** role to do this.

title: Set up reminders for expiring documents
body:
1. Go to **Settings**, then **Documents**.
2. Select **Expiry reminders**.
3. Choose how many days before expiry to send a reminder, such as 30 and 7.
4. Pick who receives it: **HR admins**, **Manager** or **Employee**.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Approve a document uploaded by an employee
body:
Employee uploads wait for review before they count as complete.

1. Go to **Documents**, then **Pending review**.
2. Open the document to check it.
3. Select **Approve**, or **Reject** and add a reason.
4. The status changes to **Approved** and the employee is notified.

title: Generate an employment letter
body:
1. Open the employee's profile and select the **Documents** tab.
2. Select **Generate document**.
3. Choose a template, such as **Employment verification**.
4. Preview the letter and select **Save to profile**.

You can also download the letter as a PDF.

title: Create a department
body:
1. Go to **Org chart**, then **Departments**.
2. Select **Add department**.
3. Enter a **Name** and, if you like, a **Code**.
4. Choose a **Department head**.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Rename a department
body:
1. Go to **Org chart**, then **Departments**.
2. Select the department.
3. Select **Edit** and change the **Name**.
4. Select **Save**.

Employee profiles pick up the new name straight away.

You need the **HR admin** role to do this.

title: Delete a department
aliases: get rid of an empty department
body:
A department can only be deleted when it has no employees.

1. Go to **Org chart**, then **Departments**.
2. Open the department.
3. Select **More actions**, then **Delete department**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Delete**.

If it still has people, move them first or use **Deactivate department**.

title: Assign an employee to a department
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Job** tab, then **Edit** next to **Department**.
3. Choose the new department.
4. Enter the **Effective date** and select **Save changes**.

To move many people at once, use **Bulk actions** in the **People** list.

title: Change an employee's manager
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Job** tab.
3. Select **Edit** next to **Reports to**.
4. Search for the new manager and select their name.
5. Set an **Effective date** and select **Save changes**.

The org chart updates for everyone straight away.

title: Set a department head
body:
1. Go to **Org chart**, then **Departments**.
2. Open the department.
3. Select **Edit** next to **Department head**.
4. Search for an employee and select them.
5. Select **Save**.

Department heads can approve leave requests for their team.

title: Merge two departments
body:
Merging moves all employees and sub-departments into one department.

1. Go to **Org chart**, then **Departments**.
2. Select the department you want to remove.
3. Select **More actions**, then **Merge into**.
4. Choose the department to keep.
5. Select **Merge departments**.

You need the **HR admin** role to do this.

title: View the org chart
body:
1. Select **Org chart** in the main menu.
2. Use the **Zoom** controls or drag the chart to move around.
3. Select a person's box to see their name, title and email.
4. Select the arrow on a box to show or hide their direct reports.

title: Export the org chart as a PDF
body:
1. Select **Org chart** in the main menu.
2. Use **Filters** to choose the **Department** or **Location** you want.
3. Select **Export**, then **PDF**.
4. Choose a **Page size** and select **Download**.

title: Export the department list to CSV
body:
1. Go to **Org chart**, then **Departments**.
2. Select **Export**.
3. Choose **CSV**.
4. Tick the columns to include, such as **Name**, **Head** and **Headcount**, and select **Download**.

Changes take effect straight away and are visible to people with access.

title: Add a cost centre to a department
body:
Cost centres show up in payroll reports so you can see wages by team.

1. Go to **Org chart**, then **Departments**.
2. Open the department and select **Edit**.
3. Type a code in **Cost centre**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Create a sub-department
aliases: add a team under a department
add a group inside a department
body:
1. Go to **Org chart**, then **Departments**.
2. Open the parent department.
3. Select **Add sub-department**.
4. Enter a **Name** and choose a **Department head**.
5. Select **Save**.

You need the **HR admin** role to do this.

title: Move a department under another department
aliases: relocate a team in the hierarchy
body:
1. Go to **Org chart**, then **Departments**.
2. Open the department you want to move.
3. Select **Edit** next to **Parent department**.
4. Choose the new parent.
5. Select **Save**.

Employees and sub-departments move with it.

title: Add a vacant position to the org chart
body:
1. Go to **Org chart** and select **Add position**.
2. Enter the **Job title** and choose a **Department**.
3. Select who it **Reports to**.
4. Switch **Status** to **Vacant** and select **Save**.

Vacant positions appear as dotted boxes on the chart.

title: Fill a vacant position
body:
1. Go to **Org chart** and select the vacant box.
2. Select **Fill position**.
3. Choose an existing employee, or select **Add employee** for a new hire.
4. Set the **Start date** and select **Confirm**.

title: Add a note to a department
body:
1. Go to **Org chart**, then **Departments**.
2. Open the department.
3. Select the **Notes** tab.
4. Select **Add note**, type your message and select **Save**.

title: Deactivate a department
body:
Inactive departments are hidden from the org chart and can't take new employees.

1. Go to **Org chart**, then **Departments**.
2. Open the department.
3. Select **Edit** and change **Status** to **Inactive**.
4. Select **Save**.

You can switch it back to **Active** at any time.

title: Search the org chart for an employee
aliases: find a person on the chart
jump to employee on org chart
body:
1. Select **Org chart** in the main menu.
2. Type a name in **Search the chart**.
3. Select the person from the list.
4. The chart centres on their box and highlights their reporting line.

title: Update a department's contact email
aliases: edit shared mailbox for a department
body:
1. Go to **Org chart**, then **Departments**.
2. Open the department.
3. Select **Edit** and go to **Contact email**.
4. Type the new address.
5. Select **Save**.

You can repeat these steps at any time to make further changes.

title: Filter the org chart by location
body:
1. Select **Org chart** in the main menu.
2. Select **Filters**.
3. Choose one or more locations in **Location**.
4. Select **Apply**.

Select **Clear filters** to see the whole company again.

title: Add an emergency contact
aliases: who to call if something happens
enter contact person for an employee
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Emergency contacts** tab.
3. Select **Add contact**.
4. Enter the **Name**, **Relationship** and **Mobile phone**.
5. Select **Save**.

You can add up to five contacts for each employee.

title: Update an emergency contact's phone number
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Emergency contacts** tab.
3. Select **Edit** beside the contact.
4. Type the new number in **Mobile phone**.
5. Select **Save**.

You need the **HR admin** role to do this.

title: Update an emergency contact's email address
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Emergency contacts** tab.
3. Select **Edit** beside the contact.
4. Enter the new address in **Email**.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Delete an emergency contact
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Emergency contacts** tab.
3. Select the three dots beside the contact.
4. Choose **Delete** and confirm.

An employee must keep at least one contact if emergency contacts are mandatory.

title: Set a primary emergency contact
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Emergency contacts** tab.
3. Select the three dots beside the contact you want.
4. Choose **Make primary**.

The primary contact is shown first on printed sheets.

title: Change an emergency contact's relationship
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Emergency contacts** tab, then **Edit** beside the contact.
3. Choose a new option in **Relationship**, such as **Partner**, **Parent** or **Friend**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Update your own emergency contacts
aliases: I need to edit my next of kin
body:
Employees can keep their own details up to date from **My profile**.

1. Select your name at the top right, then **My profile**.
2. Open the **Emergency contacts** tab.
3. Select **Add contact** or **Edit** beside an existing one.
4. Enter the details and select **Save**.

HR is notified if you remove your last contact.

title: Ask employees to confirm their emergency contacts
aliases: get staff to verify next of kin
body:
1. Go to **People**, then **Emergency contacts**.
2. Select **Request confirmation**.
3. Choose who to include, such as a **Department** or **All employees**.
4. Set a **Due date** and select **Send request**.

title: Export emergency contacts to CSV
body:
1. Go to **People**, then **Emergency contacts**.
2. Filter by **Department** or **Location** if needed.
3. Select **Export**, then **CSV**.
4. Select **Download**.

You can repeat these steps at any time to make further changes.

title: Add a note to an emergency contact
aliases: write a note about next of kin
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Emergency contacts** tab, then **Edit** beside the contact.
3. Type your message in **Notes**, such as "Call after 5 pm".
4. Select **Save**.

title: View emergency contacts for a department
aliases: who are the contacts in this department
body:
1. Go to **People**, then **Emergency contacts**.
2. Select **Filters** and choose a **Department**.
3. Select an employee row to expand their contacts.

Managers can see this list for their own team only.

title: Print an emergency contact sheet
body:
A printed sheet is handy for fire wardens and site managers.

1. Go to **People**, then **Emergency contacts**.
2. Choose a **Department** or **Location**.
3. Select **Print sheet**.
4. Pick **Primary contact only** or **All contacts**.
5. Select **Print** or **Save as PDF**.

title: Add an alternate phone number to an emergency contact
aliases: home number for next of kin
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Emergency contacts** tab, then **Edit** beside the contact.
3. Select **Add another phone**.
4. Choose **Home** or **Work** and enter the number.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Mark an emergency contact as no longer valid
body:
Keep the record for reference but stop it showing on contact sheets.

1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Emergency contacts** tab.
3. Select the three dots beside the contact, then **Mark as invalid**.
4. Choose a reason and select **Save**.

HR will see the employee in the **Needs attention** list.

title: Record an employee's medical alerts
body:
Only add information the employee has agreed to share.

1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Emergency contacts** tab.
3. Select **Edit** under **Medical alerts**.
4. Enter details such as allergies or medication.
5. Select **Save**.

This section is visible to HR admins and first aid officers.

title: Set the minimum number of emergency contacts
body:
1. Go to **Settings**, then **Emergency contacts**.
2. Under **Minimum contacts**, choose 1, 2 or 3.
3. Select **Save changes**.

Employees below the minimum will see a prompt next time they sign in.

title: Require emergency contacts during onboarding
aliases: new starters must add a contact
body:
1. Go to **Onboarding**, then **Templates**.
2. Open the template you want to change.
3. Select **Add task** and choose **Add emergency contact**.
4. Tick **Required** and select **Save template**.

You need the **HR admin** role to do this.

title: Add an address to an emergency contact
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Emergency contacts** tab, then **Edit** beside the contact.
3. Select **Add address**.
4. Fill in the street, suburb, state and postcode.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Find employees with no emergency contact
body:
1. Go to **People**, then **Emergency contacts**.
2. Select **Filters**.
3. Choose **No contacts on file**.
4. Select **Send reminder** to ask them to add one.

You can repeat these steps at any time to make further changes.

title: Change the order of emergency contacts
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee.
2. Select the **Emergency contacts** tab.
3. Drag the handle beside a contact to a new position.
4. Select **Save order**.

Changes take effect straight away and are visible to people with access.

title: Request annual leave
body:
1. Go to **Leave** and select **My leave**.
2. Select **Request leave**.
3. Choose **Annual leave** from the **Leave type** list.
4. Pick your **Start date** and **End date**.
5. Check the **Hours requested** total, which updates automatically.
6. Add a message for your manager if you wish.
7. Select **Submit request**.

Your manager is notified straight away and you will get an email when they respond.

title: Cancel a leave request
aliases: I don't need the days off any more
body:
1. Go to **Leave** and select **My leave**.
2. Open the **Requests** tab.
3. Find the request you want to cancel and select it.
4. Select **Cancel request**.
5. Confirm by selecting **Yes, cancel**.

If the leave was already approved, the hours go back into your balance and your manager is told about the change.

title: Approve a leave request
body:
1. Go to **Leave** and select **Approvals**.
2. Open the **Pending** tab.
3. Select the request to see the dates, hours and the employee's remaining balance.
4. Check the **Team calendar** panel for clashes.
5. Select **Approve**.

The employee is emailed and the leave appears on the team calendar.

title: Decline a leave request
body:
1. Go to **Leave** and select **Approvals**.
2. Open the **Pending** tab and select the request.
3. Select **Decline**.
4. Enter a reason in the **Message to employee** box. This is required.
5. Select **Confirm decline**.

The employee is emailed your reason and their balance is left unchanged.

title: Check your leave balance
aliases: how much leave do I have
body:
1. Go to **Leave** and select **My leave**.
2. Look at the **Balances** panel at the top of the page.
3. Select a leave type to see its history, including accruals and leave taken.
4. Turn on **Show projected balance** and choose a future date to see what you will have by then.

Balances are shown in hours. Select **Show in days** to switch the view.

title: Add a leave type
aliases: create a new kind of leave
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Leave**.
2. Select **Leave types**, then **Add leave type**.
3. Enter a **Name**, such as Study leave.
4. Choose whether the leave is **Paid** or **Unpaid**.
5. Choose whether it **Accrues** over time or is a **Fixed allowance**.
6. Select the employees or groups it applies to.
7. Select **Save**.

title: Adjust an employee's leave balance
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee's profile.
2. Select the **Leave** tab.
3. Select **Adjust balance** next to the leave type.
4. Enter the number of hours to add or remove.
5. Enter a **Reason**. It is saved in the audit history.
6. Select **Apply adjustment**.

title: Set the leave accrual rate
aliases: change how fast leave builds up
how many hours of leave per pay run
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Leave**.
2. Select **Leave types** and open the leave type.
3. Under **Accrual**, choose **Per hour worked** or **Per pay run**.
4. Enter the **Hours accrued**.
5. Set a **Maximum balance** if you want a cap.
6. Select **Save**.

Changes apply from the next pay run and do not alter past balances.

title: Add a leave request for an employee
aliases: enter leave for my team member
log leave on behalf of staff
body:
1. Go to **Leave** and select **Approvals**.
2. Select **New request**.
3. Search for and select the **Employee**.
4. Choose the **Leave type** and enter the dates.
5. Turn on **Approve immediately** if no approval is needed.
6. Select **Submit**.

title: View the team leave calendar
body:
1. Go to **Leave** and select **Team calendar**.
2. Use **Week**, **Month** or **Quarter** to change the view.
3. Select **Filter** and choose a **Department** or **Location**.
4. Hover over a coloured bar to see the employee, dates and leave type.

Pending requests appear striped, and approved leave appears solid.

title: Export a leave report to CSV
aliases: get leave taken as a file
body:
1. Go to **Leave** and select **Reports**.
2. Choose **Leave balances** or **Leave taken**.
3. Set the **Date range** and any **Department** filter.
4. Select **Run report**.
5. Select **Export** and choose **CSV**.

The file downloads to your browser's usual downloads folder.

title: Add a note to a leave request
aliases: write a remark on time off
leave a message on someone's leave
body:
1. Go to **Leave** and select **Approvals**.
2. Open the request you want to comment on.
3. Select the **Notes** tab.
4. Type your comment in the box.
5. Choose **Visible to employee** or **Managers only**.
6. Select **Add note**.

title: Request half a day of leave
body:
1. Go to **Leave** and select **My leave**.
2. Select **Request leave**.
3. Choose the **Leave type**.
4. Pick the date and turn on **Partial day**.
5. Enter the **Start time** and **End time**, or the number of hours.
6. Select **Submit request**.

The hours are deducted from your balance once the request is approved.

title: Set up leave carry-over rules
aliases: use it or lose it leave
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Leave**.
2. Open the leave type you want to change.
3. Select **Carry-over**.
4. Choose **Carry over all**, **Carry over up to a limit** or **Reset to zero**.
5. If you chose a limit, enter the maximum **Hours**.
6. Select the **Rollover date**.
7. Select **Save**.

title: Attach a medical certificate to sick leave
body:
1. Go to **Leave** and select **My leave**.
2. Open the sick leave request from the **Requests** tab.
3. Select **Add attachment**.
4. Choose a PDF or image file from your device.
5. Select **Upload**, then **Save**.

Only you, your manager and payroll administrators can see the attachment.

title: Process a leave cash-out
body:
1. Go to **Payroll** and select **Leave cash-outs**.
2. Select **New cash-out**.
3. Search for and select the **Employee**.
4. Enter the **Hours** to pay out. The remaining balance is shown.
5. Choose the **Pay run** the payment will be included in.
6. Select **Save**.

The hours are deducted when the pay run is finalised.

title: Delete a leave type
aliases: get rid of old leave type
body:
You can only delete a leave type that has no leave booked against it. Otherwise, archive it.

1. Go to **Settings** and select **Leave**.
2. Select **Leave types**.
3. Open the leave type.
4. Select **Delete leave type** and confirm.

To keep the history, select **Archive** instead. Archived types cannot be chosen for new requests.

title: Start a pay run
body:
1. Go to **Payroll** and select **Pay runs**.
2. Select **New pay run**.
3. Choose the **Pay schedule**.
4. Check the **Pay period** and **Payment date**.
5. Select **Create draft**.
6. Review each employee's hours and earnings.
7. Select **Finalise** when everything looks right.

Finalising locks the pay run and generates payslips.

title: View a payslip
aliases: check how much I was paid
body:
1. Go to **Payroll** and select **My payslips**.
2. Select the payslip for the pay date you want.
3. Review the **Earnings**, **Tax**, **Super** and **Net pay** sections.
4. Select **Year to date** to compare totals.

You can review the result in the pay run summary before anything is paid.

title: Download a payslip as a PDF
aliases: get a copy of my pay slip
body:
1. Go to **Payroll** and select **My payslips**.
2. Open the payslip you need.
3. Select **Download PDF**.
4. Save the file to your device.

You can download any payslip from the last seven years.

You can review the result in the pay run summary before anything is paid.

title: Email payslips to employees
aliases: employee did not get their payslip
body:
1. Go to **Payroll** and select **Pay runs**.
2. Open a finalised pay run.
3. Select the **Payslips** tab.
4. Tick the employees to send to, or tick **Select all**.
5. Select **Email payslips**.
6. Select **Send**.

Each email goes to the employee's work email address on their profile.

title: Update an employee's super fund
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee's profile.
2. Select the **Pay** tab, then **Superannuation**.
3. Select **Add fund** or **Change fund**.
4. Search by fund name or enter the **USI** and **Member number**.
5. Select **Save**.

Super contributions use the new fund from the next pay run.

title: Add an allowance to an employee
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee's profile.
2. Select the **Pay** tab, then **Pay items**.
3. Select **Add pay item**.
4. Choose the **Allowance** category and pick the item.
5. Enter the **Amount** and how often it is paid.
6. Set the **Start date**.
7. Select **Save**.

title: Add a one-off bonus to a pay run
body:
1. Go to **Payroll** and open the draft pay run.
2. Select the employee's row.
3. Select **Add earnings line**.
4. Choose **Bonus** as the pay item.
5. Enter the **Amount**.
6. Select **Save**.

The bonus is included in this pay run only.

title: Correct a finalised pay run
body:
1. Go to **Payroll** and select **Pay runs**.
2. Open the finalised pay run.
3. Select **More**, then **Reverse pay run**.
4. Enter a **Reason**.
5. Select **Reverse**.
6. Create a new pay run with the correct figures.

Reversing is not possible once the payment file has been sent to the bank.

title: Delete a draft pay run
aliases: cancel a pay run I started
body:
1. Go to **Payroll** and select **Pay runs**.
2. Open the pay run marked **Draft**.
3. Select **More**, then **Delete draft**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Delete**.

Finalised pay runs cannot be deleted. Reverse them instead.

You can review the result in the pay run summary before anything is paid.

title: Export a pay run to CSV
body:
1. Go to **Payroll** and select **Pay runs**.
2. Open the pay run.
3. Select **Export**.
4. Choose **CSV** and select the **Summary** or **Detailed** layout.
5. Select **Download**.

You can review the result in the pay run summary before anything is paid.

title: Set up a pay schedule
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Payroll**.
2. Select **Pay schedules**, then **Add schedule**.
3. Enter a **Name**.
4. Choose the **Frequency**: weekly, fortnightly or monthly.
5. Select the **First pay date**.
6. Select the employees on this schedule.
7. Select **Save**.

title: Add a note to a pay run
aliases: leave a remark on a pay run
record why a pay run changed
body:
1. Go to **Payroll** and select **Pay runs**.
2. Open the pay run.
3. Select the **Notes** tab.
4. Type your note.
5. Select **Add note**.

Notes are visible to payroll administrators only.

You can review the result in the pay run summary before anything is paid.

title: Mark a pay run as paid
body:
1. Go to **Payroll** and select **Pay runs**.
2. Open a finalised pay run with the status **Awaiting payment**.
3. Select **Change status**.
4. Choose **Paid**.
5. Enter the date the money left your bank account.
6. Select **Save**.

You can review the result in the pay run summary before anything is paid.

title: Process a final pay
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee's profile.
2. Select **More**, then **End employment**.
3. Enter the **Last day of work** and the **Reason**.
4. Select **Calculate final pay**.
5. Review the unused leave payout and any other amounts.
6. Select **Add to pay run**.

title: Enter hours on your timesheet
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select **My timesheet**.
2. Select the week using the arrows at the top.
3. Select **Add entry** on the day you worked.
4. Enter the **Start time** and **End time**.
5. Choose the **Project** if one applies.
6. Select **Save**.

Your hours are saved as a draft until you submit them.

title: Submit a timesheet for approval
aliases: send my timesheet to my manager
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select **My timesheet**.
2. Check that every day shows the correct hours.
3. Select **Submit for approval**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Submit**.

The status changes from **Draft** to **Submitted**.

title: Approve a timesheet
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select **Approvals**.
2. Select a timesheet marked **Submitted**.
3. Check the daily totals and any notes.
4. Select **Approve**.

Approved hours flow into the next pay run automatically.

title: Reject a timesheet
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select **Approvals**.
2. Open the submitted timesheet.
3. Select **Reject**.
4. Enter what needs to change in the **Reason** box.
5. Select **Send back**.

The employee is emailed and can edit and resubmit.

title: Recall a submitted timesheet
aliases: I made a mistake after submitting
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select **My timesheet**.
2. Open the week you submitted.
3. Select **Recall**.
4. Make your changes.
5. Select **Submit for approval** again.

You can only recall a timesheet that has not been approved yet.

title: Add a note to a timesheet entry
aliases: write a remark on a time entry
leave a note on a shift
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select **My timesheet**.
2. Select the entry you want to explain.
3. Select **Add note**.
4. Type your note, for example the reason for the overtime.
5. Select **Save**.

Your manager sees the note when they review your timesheet.

title: Clock in and out on the mobile app
aliases: start my shift on my phone
body:
1. Open the Harbour People app and tap **Time clock**.
2. Tap **Clock in** when you start work.
3. Tap **Start break** and **End break** as needed.
4. Tap **Clock out** when you finish.
5. Check the entry under **Timesheets**.

If location checks are on, allow the app to use your location.

title: Add a project code
aliases: new project to book time against
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Timesheets**.
2. Select **Projects**, then **Add project**.
3. Enter a **Name** and **Code**.
4. Choose whether it is **Billable**.
5. Select who can book time to it.
6. Select **Save**.

title: Delete a project code
aliases: get rid of a job code
stop time being booked to a project
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Timesheets**.
2. Select **Projects**.
3. Open the project.
4. Select **Delete project** and confirm.

If hours are already booked to the project, select **Archive** instead.

title: Delete a timesheet entry
aliases: clear a line on my timesheet
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select **My timesheet**.
2. Select the entry you want to remove.
3. Select **Delete entry**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Delete**.

You cannot delete entries on a timesheet that has been approved.

title: Export timesheets to CSV
aliases: get time data in a file
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select **Reports**.
2. Choose **Hours by employee** or **Hours by project**.
3. Set the **Date range**.
4. Select **Run report**.
5. Select **Export**, then **CSV**.

title: Set overtime rules
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Timesheets**.
2. Select **Overtime**.
3. Choose **Daily**, **Weekly** or **Both** as the trigger.
4. Enter the number of hours before overtime starts.
