5. Choose the **Pay rate multiplier**, such as 1.5.
6. Select **Save**.

title: Set a timesheet reminder
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Timesheets**.
2. Select **Reminders**.
3. Turn on **Remind employees to submit**.
4. Choose the **Day** and **Time**.
5. Select **Save**.

Employees who have already submitted are not reminded.

title: Copy last week's timesheet
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select **My timesheet**.
2. Select the current week.
3. Select **More**, then **Copy previous week**.
4. Review the copied entries.
5. Adjust anything that has changed and select **Save**.

title: Lock a timesheet period
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select **Periods**.
2. Find the pay period you want to close.
3. Select **Lock**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Lock period**.

Locked periods cannot be edited. Select **Unlock** if you need to make a change.

title: Approve several timesheets at once
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select **Approvals**.
2. Tick the box next to each timesheet, or tick **Select all**.
3. Select **Approve selected**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Approve**.

Timesheets with warnings are skipped so you can review them one by one.

title: Reopen an approved timesheet
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select **Approvals**.
2. Open the **Approved** tab.
3. Select the timesheet.
4. Select **Change status**, then **Reopen**.
5. Enter a **Reason** and select **Save**.

You cannot reopen a timesheet that is already in a finalised pay run.

title: Create a review cycle
body:
1. Go to **Performance** and select **Review cycles**.
2. Select **New cycle**.
3. Enter a **Name** and choose a **Template**.
4. Select the **Participants**.
5. Set the due dates for self-reviews and manager reviews.
6. Select **Launch cycle**.

Participants are emailed when the cycle launches.

title: Complete your self-review
body:
1. Go to **Performance** and select **My reviews**.
2. Open the review marked **Self-review due**.
3. Answer each question and choose a **Rating**.
4. Select **Save draft** to finish later.
5. Select **Submit** when you are done.

You cannot change your answers after you submit.

title: Write a manager review
body:
1. Go to **Performance** and select **Team reviews**.
2. Open the employee's review.
3. Read their self-review.
4. Enter your comments and choose a **Rating** for each question.
5. Select **Save draft** or **Complete review**.

title: Add a goal
body:
1. Go to **Performance** and select **Goals**.
2. Select **Add goal**.
3. Enter a **Title** and **Description**.
4. Set the **Due date**.
5. Choose how it is measured: **Percentage** or **Milestones**.
6. Select **Save**.

title: Update goal progress
body:
1. Go to **Performance** and select **Goals**.
2. Open the goal.
3. Select **Update progress**.
4. Enter the new percentage or tick the completed milestone.
5. Add a comment if you wish.
6. Select **Save**.

Choose **Completed** from the **Status** list to close the goal.

title: Delete a goal
body:
1. Go to **Performance** and select **Goals**.
2. Open the goal.
3. Select **More**, then **Delete goal**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Delete**.

Deleted goals are removed from any open reviews.

title: Request peer feedback
body:
1. Go to **Performance** and select **Feedback**.
2. Select **Request feedback**.
3. Choose the employee the feedback is about.
4. Search for and select up to eight colleagues.
5. Choose a **Question set**.
6. Select **Send requests**.

title: Add a private note to a review
aliases: hidden note about an employee review
write a note employee can't see
body:
1. Go to **Performance** and select **Team reviews**.
2. Open the review.
3. Select the **Notes** tab.
4. Type your note.
5. Choose **Managers only** as the visibility.
6. Select **Add note**.

title: Share a completed review with an employee
body:
1. Go to **Performance** and select **Team reviews**.
2. Open a review with the status **Completed**.
3. Select **Share with employee**.
4. Choose whether to include your **Rating**.
5. Select **Share**.

The employee is emailed and can view the review under **My reviews**.

title: Reopen a completed review
aliases: review status back to in progress
body:
1. Go to **Performance** and select **Review cycles**.
2. Open the cycle and select the employee's review.
3. Select **Change status**.
4. Choose **In progress**.
5. Enter a **Reason** and select **Save**.

If the review was already shared, the employee will no longer see it until you share it again.

title: Export review results to CSV
aliases: get performance data as a file
body:
1. Go to **Performance** and select **Reports**.
2. Select **Review results**.
3. Choose the **Review cycle**.
4. Select **Run report**.
5. Select **Export**, then **CSV**.

The file opens in Excel or any spreadsheet program and includes one row for each employee in the cycle.

title: Add a rating scale
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Performance**.
2. Select **Rating scales**, then **Add scale**.
3. Enter a **Name**.
4. Add each level with a **Label** and a **Score**.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Change a review due date
body:
1. Go to **Performance** and select **Review cycles**.
2. Open the cycle.
3. Select **Edit dates**.
4. Choose a new date for **Self-reviews** or **Manager reviews**.
5. Select **Save**.

Employees who have not finished are emailed about the new date.

title: Create a review template
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Performance**.
2. Select **Templates**, then **New template**.
3. Enter a **Name**.
4. Select **Add question** and choose the type, such as **Rating** or **Free text**.
5. Drag questions to reorder them.
6. Select **Save**.

title: Send recognition to a colleague
body:
1. Go to **Performance** and select **Recognition**.
2. Select **Give recognition**.
3. Search for and select a colleague.
4. Choose a **Value**, such as Teamwork.
5. Write a short message.
6. Select **Send**.

Recognition appears on the colleague's profile and in their next review.

title: Set review reminders
body:
1. Go to **Performance** and select **Review cycles**.
2. Open the cycle and select **Reminders**.
3. Turn on **Send reminders**.
4. Choose how many days before the due date to send them.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Submit an expense claim
body:
1. Go to **Expenses** and select **My claims**.
2. Select **New claim**.
3. Enter the **Date**, **Amount** and **Merchant**.
4. Choose a **Category**.
5. Attach your receipt.
6. Select **Submit for approval**.

You can add several expenses to one claim before you submit.

title: Attach a receipt to an expense
body:
1. Go to **Expenses** and select **My claims**.
2. Open the expense.
3. Select **Add receipt**.
4. Choose a photo or PDF from your device, or take a picture in the mobile app.
5. Select **Upload**.

Each receipt can be up to 10 MB.

title: Edit a draft expense claim
body:
1. Go to **Expenses** and select **My claims**.
2. Open the **Drafts** tab.
3. Select the claim.
4. Change the details you need, such as the **Amount** or **Category**.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Delete an expense claim
body:
1. Go to **Expenses** and select **My claims**.
2. Open the claim.
3. Select **More**, then **Delete claim**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Delete**.

You can only delete claims that are in **Draft** or **Submitted** status.

title: Approve an expense claim
body:
1. Go to **Expenses** and select **Approvals**.
2. Open a claim marked **Submitted**.
3. Check the receipt, amount and category.
4. Select **Approve**.

Approved claims are ready to be paid in the next pay run.

title: Reject an expense claim
body:
1. Go to **Expenses** and select **Approvals**.
2. Open the claim.
3. Select **Reject**.
4. Enter a reason, such as a missing receipt.
5. Select **Confirm**.

The employee can edit the claim and submit it again.

title: Add an expense category
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Expenses**.
2. Select **Categories**, then **Add category**.
3. Enter a **Name**.
4. Choose whether a **Receipt is required**.
5. Enter the **Account code** used by your accountant.
6. Select **Save**.

title: Set an expense spending limit
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Expenses**.
2. Select **Categories** and open a category.
3. Under **Spending limit**, enter the **Maximum amount**.
4. Choose **Per claim** or **Per month**.
5. Choose whether to **Block** or **Warn** when the limit is passed.
6. Select **Save**.

title: Export expenses to CSV
aliases: get expense data as a file
body:
1. Go to **Expenses** and select **Reports**.
2. Select **All claims**.
3. Set the **Date range** and **Status**.
4. Select **Run report**.
5. Select **Export**, then **CSV**.

You can follow the progress of any claim under **Expenses**. Changes take effect immediately, and you can undo them at any time by repeating the steps.

title: Add a mileage claim
aliases: claim for using my own car
body:
1. Go to **Expenses** and select **My claims**.
2. Select **New claim**, then **Mileage**.
3. Enter the **Date**, **From**, **To** and the **Distance** in kilometres.
4. Choose the **Vehicle type**.
5. Check the calculated **Amount**.
6. Select **Submit for approval**.

title: Reimburse expense claims in a pay run
body:
1. Go to **Payroll** and open a draft pay run.
2. Select **Add reimbursements**.
3. Tick the approved claims to include.
4. Select **Add to pay run**.

The claims change to **Paid** when you finalise the pay run.

title: Add a note to an expense claim
body:
1. Go to **Expenses** and open the claim.
2. Select the **Notes** tab.
3. Type your note.
4. Select **Add note**.

The approver is notified when a note is added to a submitted claim.

title: Mark an expense claim as paid
body:
1. Go to **Expenses** and select **Approvals**.
2. Open the **Approved** tab.
3. Select the claim.
4. Select **Change status**, then **Paid**.
5. Enter the **Payment date** and select **Save**.

title: Add a company card
aliases: link a card to an employee
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Expenses**.
2. Select **Company cards**, then **Add card**.
3. Enter the **Card name** and the last four digits.
4. Select the **Cardholder**.
5. Select **Save**.

Card transactions appear on the cardholder's **My claims** page for matching.

title: Claim an expense in a foreign currency
body:
1. Go to **Expenses** and select **My claims**.
2. Select **New claim**.
3. Choose the currency from the **Currency** list.
4. Enter the **Amount** in that currency.
5. Check the **Exchange rate** and converted amount.
6. Attach the receipt and select **Submit for approval**.

title: Copy a previous expense claim
body:
1. Go to **Expenses** and select **My claims**.
2. Open the claim you want to copy.
3. Select **More**, then **Duplicate**.
4. Update the **Date** and **Amount**.
5. Attach a new receipt.
6. Select **Submit for approval**.

title: Set an expense approver
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Expenses**.
2. Select **Approval rules**.
3. Choose a **Department** or employee.
4. Select the **Approver**.
5. Enter a **Backup approver** if needed.
6. Select **Save**.

title: Add a note to an employee record
aliases: write a note on someone's profile
log a note about an employee
body:
1. Go to **People** and select **Employees**.
2. Open the employee's profile.
3. Select the **Notes** tab.
4. Select **Add note**.
5. Type your note and choose who can see it.
6. Select **Save**.

The change is recorded in the audit history under **Settings**.

title: Add a department
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Company**.
2. Select **Departments**, then **Add department**.
3. Enter a **Name**.
4. Choose a **Department head**.
5. Select **Save**.

The change is recorded in the audit history under **Settings**. Changes take effect immediately, and you can undo them at any time by repeating the steps.

title: Update the company logo
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Company**.
2. Select **Branding**.
3. Select **Upload logo**.
4. Choose a PNG or JPG file, at least 400 pixels wide.
5. Select **Save**.

The new logo appears on payslips and emails sent from now on.

title: Update company details
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Company**.
2. Select **Company details**.
3. Select **Edit**.
4. Update the **Legal name**, **ABN** or **Address**.
5. Select **Save**.

The change is recorded in the audit history under **Settings**. Changes take effect immediately, and you can undo them at any time by repeating the steps.

title: Invite an administrator
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Users**.
2. Select **Invite user**.
3. Enter their **Email**.
4. Choose the **Role**, such as **Payroll admin** or **HR admin**.
5. Select **Send invitation**.

The invitation link expires after seven days.

The change is recorded in the audit history under **Settings**.

title: Change a user's permissions
aliases: restrict what a user can see
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Users**.
2. Open the user.
3. Select **Edit role**.
4. Choose a different **Role**, or select **Custom** to tick individual permissions.
5. Select **Save**.

The change is recorded in the audit history under **Settings**.

title: Reset an employee's password
body:
1. Go to **People** and select **Employees**.
2. Open the employee's profile.
3. Select **More**, then **Send password reset**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Send**.

The employee receives an email with a link that works for 24 hours.

The change is recorded in the audit history under **Settings**.

title: Set public holidays
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Calendar**.
2. Select **Public holidays**.
3. Choose your **State or region** to load the standard holidays.
4. Select **Add holiday** to enter a custom day.
5. Select **Save**.

The change is recorded in the audit history under **Settings**.

title: Import employees from a CSV file
body:
1. Go to **People** and select **Employees**.
2. Select **Import**.
3. Select **Download template** and fill it in.
4. Select **Upload file** and choose your CSV.
5. Match any columns that are not recognised.
6. Select **Import**.

Rows with errors are listed so you can fix them and try again.

title: Turn on two-step verification
aliases: require a code when signing in
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Security**.
2. Under **Two-step verification**, select **Turn on**.
3. Scan the QR code with your authenticator app.
4. Enter the six-digit code.
5. Select **Verify**.

Select **Require for all users** to make it mandatory for your company.

title: Add a deduction to an employee's pay
body:
1. Go to **People** and open the employee's profile.
2. Select the **Pay** tab, then **Pay items**.
3. Select **Add pay item**.
4. Choose the **Deduction** category and pick the item, such as **Union fees**.
5. Enter the **Amount** and how often it is taken.
6. Set the **Start date** and, if needed, an **End date**.
7. Select **Save**.

Deductions appear on the employee's payslip from the next pay run.

title: Create a project
body:
Every piece of work in Harbour Projects lives in a project.
1. In the left sidebar, select **Projects**.
2. Select **New project**.
3. Enter a **Project name** and, if you like, a short **Description**.
4. Choose a **Start date** and **Due date**.
5. Select **Create project**.
The project opens on its **Overview** tab, ready for tasks.

title: Create a project from a template
aliases: use a template for a new project
body:
Templates save you rebuilding the same tasks and columns each time.
1. Select **Projects** in the left sidebar.
2. Select the arrow next to **New project**, then choose **From template**.
3. Pick a template from the **Template library**.
4. Enter a **Project name** and set the **Start date**. Task dates shift to match.
5. Select **Create project**.

title: Save a project as a template
aliases: make a template from a project
body:
Save a project you are happy with so your team can reuse its tasks, columns and settings.
1. Open the project and select the **More** menu (three dots) at the top right.
2. Select **Save as template**.
3. Enter a **Template name**.
4. Choose whether to **Include tasks** and **Include files**.
5. Select **Save template**.
Comments and time logs are never copied into a template.

title: Rename a project
body:
1. Open the project.
2. Select the **Settings** tab.
3. Under **General**, edit the **Project name** field.
4. Select **Save changes**.
The new name appears straight away in the sidebar, in reports and on any task notifications sent from now on. Old notifications keep the previous name.

title: Edit a project description
aliases: add a description to a project
body:
The description sits at the top of the **Overview** tab and helps new members understand the project.
1. Open the project and select the **Overview** tab.
2. Select **Edit description**.
3. Type or paste your text. You can use bold and bullet lists.
4. Select **Save**.
Guests with access to the project can read the description too.

title: Change a project’s start and due dates
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Settings** tab.
2. Under **Schedule**, select the **Start date** or **Due date** field.
3. Choose the new date from the calendar.
4. To move tasks with the project, tick **Shift task dates by the same amount**.
5. Select **Save changes**.
Tasks that now fall outside the project dates are flagged with an amber warning on the **Timeline**.

title: Change a project’s status
body:
Status tells your team and clients where a project stands.
1. Open the project.
2. Select the status badge next to the project name, for example **On track**.
3. Choose **On track**, **At risk**, **Off track**, **On hold** or **Complete**.
4. Add a short note if you wish.
5. Select **Update status**.
Each change is recorded in the **Status history** on the **Overview** tab.

title: Post a project status update
aliases: add a progress note to a project
body:
Status updates give stakeholders a written summary without a meeting.
1. Open the project and select the **Overview** tab.
2. Select **New update**.
3. Choose a **Status** and write your summary.
4. Tick **Notify guests** if clients should receive it.
5. Select **Post update**.
Project members get an email and an in-app notification.

title: Archive a project
body:
Archiving removes a project from your active list but keeps everything in it.
1. Open the project.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Archive project**.
3. Select **Archive** to confirm.
Archived projects are read-only. Members and guests can still view them, but nobody can add tasks or comments until the project is restored.

title: Restore an archived project
body:
1. Select **Projects** in the left sidebar.
2. Select the **Filter** button and choose **Archived**.
3. Open the project you want to bring back.
4. Select **Restore project** at the top of the page.
5. Choose a status, such as **On track**, then select **Restore**.
The project returns to your active list with all tasks, files and comments intact.

title: Delete a project
body:
Only project owners and account admins can delete a project. Deleting is permanent after 30 days.
1. Open the project and select the **Settings** tab.
2. Scroll to **Danger zone**.
3. Select **Delete project**.
4. Type the project name to confirm.
5. Select **Delete forever**.
If you may want the work later, archive the project instead.

title: Duplicate a project
aliases: make a copy of an existing project
body:
1. Select **Projects** in the left sidebar.
2. Hover over the project and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Duplicate**.
4. Enter a name for the copy.
5. Choose what to include: **Tasks**, **Files**, **Members** and **Board layout**.
6. Select **Duplicate project**.
Comments and time logs are not copied. Use a template if you plan to repeat this often.

title: Export a project’s tasks to CSV
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Tasks** tab.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots) above the task list.
3. Select **Export to CSV**.
4. Choose the columns you need, such as **Assignee**, **Due date** and **Status**.
5. Select **Export**.
The file downloads to your browser’s usual download folder. Subtasks appear on their own rows.

title: Add a team member to a project
aliases: invite a colleague to a project
give someone access to a project
body:
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Select **Add member**.
3. Start typing the person’s name or email address and choose them from the list.
4. Pick a **Role**: **Manager**, **Contributor** or **Viewer**.
5. Select **Add**.
They receive a notification and the project appears in their **Projects** list. To include someone outside your company, invite them as a guest instead.

title: Remove a member from a project
aliases: revoke project access for a colleague
body:
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Find the person in the **Members** list.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots) beside their name, then **Remove from project**.
4. Choose whether to **Reassign their open tasks** to another member or leave them unassigned.
5. Select **Remove**.
Their past comments and completed work stay in the project.

title: Change a member’s role in a project
body:
Roles control what each member can do in a project.
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Find the member in the list.
3. Select their current role, for example **Contributor**.
4. Choose **Manager**, **Contributor** or **Viewer**.
5. Select **Save**.
The change takes effect immediately.

title: Transfer project ownership
aliases: make someone else the project owner
body:
Each project has one owner who can delete it and manage billing codes.
1. Open the project and select the **Settings** tab.
2. Under **General**, select the **Owner** field.
3. Choose a current **Manager** from the list.
4. Select **Transfer ownership**.
5. Confirm by selecting **Yes, transfer**.
You stay on the project as a **Manager**.

title: Set a project budget
aliases: add a budget to a project
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Settings** tab.
2. Select **Budget**.
3. Choose **Budget type**: **Hours** or **Amount**.
4. Enter the budget figure and, for amounts, the **Currency**.
5. Select **Save changes**.
A progress bar appears on the **Overview** tab and turns amber when 80 per cent is used. Logged time updates it automatically.

title: Change a project’s colour and icon
aliases: pick a colour for a project
customise how a project looks in the sidebar
body:
Colours make projects easy to tell apart at a glance.
1. Open the project and select the **Settings** tab.
2. Under **Appearance**, select the coloured square.
3. Choose a colour and an icon.
4. Select **Save changes**.
The new look shows in the sidebar, on the **Projects** page and on your board cards.

title: Filter the projects list
body:
1. Select **Projects** in the left sidebar.
2. Select **Filter** above the list.
3. Choose one or more conditions, such as **Status**, **Owner** or **Client**.
4. Select **Apply**.
5. To keep the filter for next time, select **Save view** and name it.
Select **Clear all** to see every project again. Use the search box to find a project by name.

title: Create a task
aliases: add a new task to a project
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Tasks** tab.
2. Select **Add task**.
3. Type the task name and press **Enter**.
4. Select the task to open its details.
5. Add an **Assignee**, **Due date** and **Description**.
Select **Save** if you changed any details. Tasks you create inside a column on the **Board** are placed in that column automatically.

title: Add a subtask to a task
aliases: break a task into smaller steps
create a checklist item under a task
body:
Subtasks split bigger jobs into steps that can each have an owner and due date.
1. Open the task.
2. Under **Subtasks**, select **Add subtask**.
3. Type a name and press **Enter**.
4. Repeat for each step.
The parent task shows progress, such as 2 of 5 complete. Subtasks can sit one level below a task only.

title: Assign a task to someone
aliases: give a task to a colleague
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Assignee** field.
3. Start typing a name and choose the person from the list.
4. To add more people, select **Add assignee**.
5. Close the task panel.
The person receives a notification. Only project members can be assigned tasks. Guests can be mentioned in comments but not assigned.

title: Change a task’s due date
aliases: move the deadline on a task
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Due date** field.
3. Choose the new date from the calendar, or select **Clear** to remove it.
4. Optionally add a time under **Due time**.
The assignee is notified of the change. If other tasks depend on this one, a prompt asks whether to move them as well.

title: Set a task’s priority
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Priority** field.
3. Choose **Low**, **Medium**, **High** or **Urgent**.
Priority shows as a coloured flag on the task list and on board cards. You can sort the **Tasks** tab by priority by selecting the **Priority** column heading.

title: Change a task’s status
body:
Every task has a status that matches the columns on your board.
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Status** field.
3. Choose a status, such as **To do**, **In progress**, **Blocked** or **Done**.
On the **Board**, the card moves to the matching column straight away. Admins can rename statuses under **Settings**, then **Workflow**.

title: Mark a task as complete
body:
1. Find the task in the **Tasks** tab or on your **My tasks** page.
2. Select the circle to the left of the task name.
The circle turns green and the task moves to **Done**. If it has open subtasks, you will be asked whether to complete them too.
To complete a task from inside its details, select **Mark complete** at the top.

title: Reopen a completed task
aliases: mark done task as not done
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Tasks** tab.
2. Select **Show completed** at the bottom of the list.
3. Open the task.
4. Select **Reopen task**.
5. Choose the status it should return to, such as **To do**.
The assignee is notified and the task reappears in the active list with its comments and files intact.

title: Add a label to a task
aliases: add a tag to a task
body:
Labels help you group and filter tasks across a project.
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Labels** field.
3. Choose an existing label, or type a new name and select **Create label**.
4. Press **Esc** to close the list.
You can add several labels to one task. Admins can edit or delete labels under **Settings**, then **Labels**.

title: Add a time estimate to a task
aliases: estimate how long a task will take
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Estimate** field.
3. Enter the time, for example **4h** or **1d 2h**.
4. Press **Enter**.
Estimates are added up on the **Overview** tab and compared with logged time in the **Reports** area. Subtask estimates roll up into the parent task.

title: Log time on a task
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Time** tab.
3. Select **Log time**.
4. Enter the **Duration**, the **Date** and an optional note.
5. Select **Save**.
You can also select **Start timer** and stop it when you finish. Time you log counts towards the project budget if one is set.

title: Delete a task
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots) at the top of the task panel.
3. Select **Delete task**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.
Deleted tasks go to the project’s **Trash** for 30 days, where a manager can restore them. Subtasks are deleted along with the parent.

title: Duplicate a task
aliases: make a copy of a task
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Duplicate task**.
4. Choose whether to include **Subtasks**, **Assignee** and **Attachments**.
5. Select **Duplicate**.
The copy is named with the word Copy at the end and appears in the same column or list.

title: Turn a subtask into a task
aliases: make a subtask its own task
body:
Use this when a step has grown into a job of its own.
1. Open the parent task.
2. Hover over the subtask under **Subtasks**.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Convert to task**.
The subtask becomes a task in the same project, keeping its assignee, due date and comments. It is no longer counted in the parent’s progress.

title: Move a task to another project
aliases: put task in a different project
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Move to project**.
3. Search for and select the destination project.
4. Choose a **Status** in that project.
5. Select **Move**.
Comments and files travel with the task. Assignees who are not members of the new project are removed from the task.

title: Make a task repeat
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the **Repeat** field.
3. Choose how often: **Daily**, **Weekly**, **Monthly** or **Custom**.
4. Pick an end: **Never** or **On a date**.
5. Select **Save**.
When someone completes the task, Harbour Projects creates the next one with the same assignee and a new due date.

title: Link a task that depends on another
aliases: make one task wait for another
body:
1. Open the task that has to wait.
2. Select **Dependencies**, then **Add dependency**.
3. Choose **Waiting on** and search for the other task.
4. Select **Add**.
The task shows a **Blocked** label until the one it is waiting on is complete. On the **Timeline**, an arrow connects the two bars.

title: Edit several tasks at once
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Tasks** tab.
2. Tick the box beside each task you want to change.
3. Select **Edit selected** in the bar that appears.
4. Choose the field to change, such as **Assignee**, **Status** or **Due date**.
5. Enter the new value and select **Apply**.
You can edit up to 200 tasks at a time.

title: Export your tasks to CSV
aliases: download all my tasks to a spreadsheet
body:
1. In the left sidebar, select **My tasks**.
2. Select **Filter** to narrow the list, if needed.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Export to CSV**.
4. Select **Export**.
The CSV includes the task name, project, assignee, status and due date. To export one project only, use the export option on that project’s **Tasks** tab.

title: Import tasks from a CSV file
aliases: bring in tasks from a file
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Tasks** tab.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Import from CSV**.
3. Select **Choose file** and pick your CSV.
4. Match each column in your file to a Harbour field, such as **Task name** and **Due date**.
5. Select **Import**.
Download the sample file first if you are unsure of the layout.

title: Add a column to a board
aliases: add a stage to my kanban board
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Board** tab.
2. Scroll to the right-hand edge and select **Add column**.
3. Type a name, such as **In review**.
4. Press **Enter**.
New columns become statuses you can use on every task in the project. Drag the column by its heading to change where it sits.

title: Rename a board column
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Board** tab.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots) at the top of the column.
3. Select **Rename**.
4. Type the new name and press **Enter**.
Tasks in the column keep their place, and their status updates to the new name.

title: Delete a board column
aliases: remove a column from the board
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Board** tab.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots) at the top of the column.
3. Select **Delete column**.
4. Choose a column to **Move tasks to**.
5. Select **Delete**.
Tasks are never deleted with the column. Each one moves to the column you chose and takes on its status.

title: Set a work-in-progress limit on a column
body:
A limit helps your team finish work before starting more.
1. Open the **Board** tab.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots) on the column.
3. Select **Set limit**.
4. Enter the maximum number of cards.
5. Select **Save**.
The column count turns red when the limit is exceeded. Cards can still be added, so the limit acts as a warning.

title: Move a card between columns
aliases: drag a card to another column
change a task’s stage on the board
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Board** tab.
2. Click and hold the card.
3. Drag it to the new column and release.
To move a card without dragging, open it, select the **Status** field and choose the column name. The task’s status updates to match, and the assignee is notified if the new status is **Done**.

title: Collapse a column
aliases: hide a column on the board
body:
1. Open the **Board** tab.
2. Select the small arrow at the top left of the column heading.
The column folds into a narrow strip showing only its name and card count. Select the arrow again to expand it.
Your choice is remembered for you only. It does not change the board for other members.

title: Filter the cards on a board
body:
1. Open the **Board** tab.
2. Select **Filter** at the top of the board.
3. Choose conditions such as **Assignee**, **Label**, **Priority** or **Due date**.
4. Select **Apply**.
A blue dot on the **Filter** button shows a filter is active. Select **Clear all** to see every card again.

title: Group a board into swimlanes
body:
Swimlanes add horizontal rows so you can see each person’s work across all columns.
1. Open the **Board** tab.
2. Select **Group by** at the top of the board.
3. Choose **Assignee**, **Priority** or **Label**.
Select **None** to return to a single row. Rows can be collapsed with the arrow beside each name.

title: Choose what shows on board cards
body:
1. Open the **Board** tab.
2. Select **Card settings**, shown as a small sliders icon.
3. Tick or untick the fields to show, such as **Due date**, **Assignee**, **Labels** and **Subtask progress**.
4. Select **Done**.
This setting applies to everyone using the board and needs a **Manager** role.

title: Change a card’s colour
body:
1. Open the **Board** tab.
2. Hover over the card and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Card colour**.
4. Choose a colour.
The colour appears as a stripe along the card’s left edge. To colour every card by priority or label instead, use **Colour by** in the board’s **Card settings**.

title: Archive completed cards
body:
Archiving keeps a long board tidy without losing any work.
1. Open the **Board** tab.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots) on the **Done** column.
3. Select **Archive all cards**.
4. Select **Archive** to confirm.
Tasks remain in the project and can be found under **Show completed** on the **Tasks** tab.

title: Save a board view
body:
1. Open the **Board** tab and set up your filters and grouping.
2. Select **Views** at the top of the board.
3. Select **Save current view**.
4. Enter a name, such as **My open work**.
5. Choose **Only me** or **Everyone in project**.
6. Select **Save**.
Saved views appear in the **Views** list for quick switching.

title: Switch from the board to the timeline
aliases: see my project as a gantt chart
body:
1. Open the project.
2. Select the **Timeline** tab.
Each task with a start and due date appears as a bar. Tasks without dates are listed in the **Unscheduled** panel on the left.
Your filters from the **Board** are carried across, so you see the same set of tasks.

title: Zoom the timeline in or out
aliases: see the whole project on one screen
body:
1. Open the **Timeline** tab.
2. Select **Zoom** at the top right.
3. Choose **Days**, **Weeks**, **Months** or **Quarters**.
Select **Fit to project** to scale the timeline so the whole project is visible. You can also hold **Ctrl** and scroll your mouse wheel.

title: Reschedule a task on the timeline
aliases: drag task bar to new dates
change start and end date on the gantt
shift a task on the timeline
body:
1. Open the **Timeline** tab.
2. Drag a task bar left or right to move both dates.
3. Drag the left or right edge of the bar to change only the start date or due date.
4. Release to save.
Tasks linked by a dependency move together if you tick **Move dependent tasks** at the top of the timeline.

title: Add a milestone to the timeline
body:
Milestones mark key dates, such as a client sign-off or launch.
1. Open the **Timeline** tab.
2. Select **Add**, then **Milestone**.
3. Enter a **Name** and choose a **Date**.
4. Select **Create**.
A diamond appears on the timeline. You can drag it to a new date or link tasks to it so it moves when they do.

title: Show or hide dependency arrows
body:
1. Open the **Timeline** tab.
2. Select **Display** at the top of the timeline.
3. Switch **Dependencies** on or off.
With arrows on, any task that runs late is outlined in red. Switch dependencies off if the timeline looks cluttered. This only changes your own view.

title: Save a baseline on the timeline
body:
A baseline captures your current plan so you can see how far work has slipped.
1. Open the **Timeline** tab.
2. Select **Baseline**, then **Save baseline**.
3. Name the baseline, for example **Kick-off plan**.
4. Select **Save**.
Grey bars appear under each task showing the original dates. Only **Managers** can save or delete baselines.

title: Export the timeline as a PDF
body:
1. Open the **Timeline** tab and choose the zoom level you want.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots) at the top right.
3. Select **Export as PDF**.
4. Choose a **Page size** and **Orientation**.
5. Select **Export**.
The PDF shows what is on screen, including any filters, so clear them first if you want every task.

title: Add a client
body:
1. In the left sidebar, select **Clients**.
2. Select **New client**.
3. Enter the **Client name**.
4. Add a **Primary contact**, **Email** and **Phone**.
5. Select **Save client**.
You can link projects to the client afterwards. Clients are kept separate from your team, so adding one does not use a user seat.

title: Update a client’s phone number
body:
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Open the client.
3. On the **Details** tab, select **Edit**.
4. Update the **Phone** field.
5. Select **Save**.
The new number shows on the client page and on any project linked to that client. Previous numbers are not kept.

title: Update a client’s email address
aliases: new email for a client contact
body:
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Open the client.
3. On the **Details** tab, select **Edit**.
4. Change the **Email** field.
5. Select **Save**.
Notifications to the client contact are sent to the new address from now on. If the contact is also a guest, update their sign-in email separately from the **People** tab.

title: Delete a client
body:
Only account admins can delete clients.
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Open the client.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Delete client**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.
Linked projects are not deleted. They simply lose their client. If you want to keep the record, set the client to inactive instead.

title: Mark a client as inactive
aliases: hide a client I no longer work with
body:
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Open the client.
3. Select the **Status** field and choose **Inactive**.
4. Select **Save**.
Inactive clients are hidden from the default **Clients** list and cannot be chosen for new projects. Select **Filter**, then **Inactive** to find them again.

title: Merge duplicate clients
body:
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Tick the two records you want to combine.
3. Select **Merge**.
4. Choose which record to keep as the main one.
5. Review the fields and select **Merge clients**.
Projects, notes and guests from both records move to the one you kept. A merge cannot be undone.

title: Add a billing contact to a client
aliases: new billing person for a customer
body:
The billing contact receives budget and time reports if you share them.
1. Open the client from **Clients**.
2. Select the **Contacts** tab.
3. Select **Add contact**.
4. Enter their name, email and phone.
5. Tick **Billing contact**.
6. Select **Save**.

title: Change a client’s billing contact
body:
1. Open the client from **Clients**.
2. Select the **Contacts** tab.
3. Find the contact you want to make the billing contact.
4. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Make billing contact**.
5. Select **Confirm**.
The previous billing contact stays on the client as a regular contact. A client can have only one billing contact at a time.

title: Add a note to a client
aliases: record a call with a client
log a conversation with a customer
body:
Notes are visible to your team only. Clients and guests never see them.
1. Open the client from **Clients**.
2. Select the **Notes** tab.
3. Select **Add note**.
4. Type your note. You can mention a teammate with @.
5. Select **Save note**.
Notes are listed with the newest first and show who wrote them.

title: Link a project to a client
aliases: assign a client to a project
set the client for a project
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Settings** tab.
2. Under **General**, select the **Client** field.
3. Search for and choose the client.
4. Select **Save changes**.
The project now appears on the client’s **Projects** tab. You can invite that client’s contacts as guests from the **People** tab.

title: See all projects for a client
aliases: find work done for a customer
body:
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Open the client.
3. Select the **Projects** tab.
The list shows every project linked to the client, with its status, owner and due date. Select **Show archived** to include finished work. Select a project name to open it.

title: Export your clients to CSV
body:
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Use **Filter** if you only need some clients.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Export to CSV**.
4. Choose the columns to include, such as **Client name**, **Email**, **Phone** and **Status**.
5. Select **Export**.
The file downloads straight away. Only admins and managers can export clients.

title: Import clients from a CSV file
aliases: bring clients in from a spreadsheet
body:
1. Select **Clients** in the left sidebar.
2. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Import from CSV**.
3. Select **Choose file**.
4. Match your columns to fields such as **Client name** and **Email**.
5. Select **Import**.
Rows with an email that already exists are skipped and listed in a summary you can download.

title: Set a client’s default hourly rate
aliases: set billing rate for a customer
add a rate to a client
body:
1. Open the client from **Clients**.
2. Select the **Billing** tab.
3. Select **Edit rates**.
4. Enter the **Hourly rate** and choose the **Currency**.
5. Select **Save**.
New projects linked to this client use the rate by default. Existing projects keep their current rate unless you change it in the project’s **Budget** settings.

title: Invite a guest to a project
aliases: give a client access to a project
share a project with an outsider
body:
Guests are people outside your company, such as clients, who can see only the projects you share.
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Select **Invite guest**.
3. Enter their email address.
4. Choose a **Permission**: **Can view**, **Can comment** or **Can approve**.
5. Select **Send invite**.

title: Resend a guest invitation
body:
Invitations expire after 14 days.
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Find the guest under **Pending invites**.
3. Select **Resend invite**.
A fresh email goes to the guest with a new link. If it still does not arrive, ask them to check their spam folder, or correct the address by removing the guest and inviting them again.

title: Change a guest’s permission
body:
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Find the guest under **Guests**.
3. Select their current permission.
4. Choose **Can view**, **Can comment** or **Can approve**.
5. Select **Save**.
Guests on **Can comment** can add comments but cannot edit tasks. Guests on **Can approve** can also approve tasks marked **Needs approval**.

title: Remove a guest from a project
aliases: stop sharing project with someone outside
body:
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Find the guest under **Guests**.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Remove guest**.
4. Select **Remove** to confirm.
The guest can no longer open the project. Their comments stay in place. If they are a guest on other projects, those are not affected.

title: Set an end date for a guest’s access
body:
1. Open the project and select the **People** tab.
2. Find the guest under **Guests**.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots), then **Set access end date**.
4. Choose a date.
5. Select **Save**.
Harbour Projects emails the guest and the project owner seven days before access ends. After that, the guest cannot open the project.

title: Choose what guests are emailed about
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Settings** tab.
2. Select **Guest notifications**.
3. Tick the events guests should hear about, such as **Status updates**, **New comments** and **Files shared**.
4. Select **Save changes**.
This applies to all guests on the project. Guests can still turn off emails for themselves from their own profile.

title: Upload a file to a project
aliases: put a file in the project
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Files** tab.
2. Select **Upload**.
3. Choose one or more files from your computer, or drag them onto the page.
4. Wait for the progress bar to finish.
Each file can be up to 500 MB. To attach a file to one task instead, open the task and select **Attach file** under **Attachments**.

title: Upload a new version of a file
aliases: replace a file with an updated one
add version two of a file
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Files** tab.
2. Hover over the file and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Upload new version**.
4. Choose the updated file.
5. Add a short **Version note**, then select **Upload**.
The name and any comments stay the same. Earlier versions are kept in the file’s history.

title: Download a file
aliases: save a file to my computer
get a copy of an attachment
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Files** tab.
2. Find the file, or open the task it is attached to.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots) beside the file.
4. Select **Download**.
The latest version downloads to your browser’s usual folder. To download older versions, open the file’s **Version history**.

title: Download all project files as a zip
aliases: get everything in the Files tab
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Files** tab.
2. Select **Select all**, or tick individual files and folders.
3. Select **Download** at the top of the list.
4. Wait for the zip to be prepared.
Large downloads can take a few minutes. Harbour Projects emails you a download link if the zip is bigger than 1 GB.

title: Rename a file
aliases: edit the name of a document
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Files** tab.
2. Hover over the file and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Rename**.
4. Type the new name. Keep the file extension, such as .pdf.
5. Press **Enter**.
The new name shows wherever the file is attached, including in tasks and comments.

title: Create a folder for files
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Files** tab.
2. Select **New folder**.
3. Type a name, for example **Signed contracts**.
4. Press **Enter**.
To put files inside, drag them onto the folder, or use **Move to folder** from the file’s **More** menu. Folders can be nested up to five levels deep.

title: Move a file into a folder
aliases: put a file in a different folder
body:
1. Open the **Files** tab.
2. Hover over the file and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Move to folder**.
4. Choose the destination folder, or select **New folder** to make one.
5. Select **Move**.
You can also drag a file onto a folder in the list.

title: Delete a file
aliases: remove a file from a project
body:
1. Open the **Files** tab.
2. Hover over the file and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete file** to confirm.
All versions of the file are moved to **Trash**. They are removed for good after 30 days. Removing an attachment from a task also deletes the file from the project.

title: Restore a deleted file
aliases: get a file back from trash
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Files** tab.
2. Select **Trash** at the top of the page.
3. Find the file. Use the search box if the list is long.
4. Select **Restore**.
The file returns to its original folder with its comments and versions. Files in **Trash** for more than 30 days cannot be recovered.

title: Restore an earlier version of a file
aliases: go back to an old version
body:
1. Open the **Files** tab and select the file.
2. Select **Version history** in the side panel.
3. Find the version you need. Each shows who uploaded it and when.
4. Select **Restore this version**.
5. Select **Restore** to confirm.
The restored copy becomes the newest version. Nothing is overwritten, so the other versions stay in the list.

title: Choose whether guests can see a file
aliases: make a file visible to guests
body:
New files are visible to guests by default.
1. Open the **Files** tab.
2. Hover over the file and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Visibility**.
4. Choose **Team only** or **Team and guests**.
5. Select **Save**.
A small lock icon marks files that are team only.

title: Add a comment to a task
aliases: leave a message on a task
post an update on a task
body:
1. Open the task.
2. Select the box labelled **Add a comment** at the bottom of the panel.
3. Type your message.
4. To include a file, select the paperclip icon.
5. Select **Send**.
Assignees and watchers are notified. Press **Ctrl+Enter** (**Cmd+Enter** on Mac) to send faster.

title: Edit a comment
aliases: fix a typo in a comment
body:
1. Open the task and find your comment.
2. Hover over it and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Edit**.
4. Change the text.
5. Select **Save**.
An **Edited** label appears beside the time. You can edit your own comments at any time, but not other people’s.

title: Delete a comment
aliases: erase a message on a task
body:
1. Open the task and find the comment.
2. Hover over it and select the **More** menu (three dots).
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete comment** to confirm.
You can delete your own comments. **Managers** can delete anyone’s comment in their project. Replies stay in place and show a note that the original was removed.

title: Mention someone in a comment
aliases: notify a teammate in a comment
body:
1. Open the task and select the **Add a comment** box.
2. Type @ followed by the person’s name.
3. Choose them from the list that appears.
4. Finish your comment and select **Send**.
The person gets an email and an in-app notification, even if they are not watching the task. If they are not a member of the project, you will be asked whether to add them.

title: Reply to a comment
aliases: reply to someone on a task
body:
Replies keep related messages together.
1. Open the task and find the comment.
2. Select **Reply** beneath it.
3. Type your response.
4. Select **Send**.
Replies appear indented under the original comment. The person you reply to is notified automatically.

title: Resolve a comment thread
body:
Resolving tells everyone the feedback has been dealt with.
1. Open the task or file and find the thread.
2. Select **Resolve** at the top of the first comment.
The thread collapses and moves to **Resolved**. To reopen it, select **Resolved comments**, find the thread and select **Reopen**.

title: Make a comment visible to the team only
body:
Use internal comments for discussion you do not want guests to read.
1. Open the task and select the **Add a comment** box.
2. Select the **Visible to** drop-down below the box.
3. Choose **Team only**.
4. Type your message and select **Send**.
A padlock marks internal comments. The setting cannot be changed after sending, so delete and repost if you chose wrongly.

title: Attach a file to a comment
aliases: add a document to a message
send a file with my comment
include a screenshot in a comment
body:
1. Open the task and select the **Add a comment** box.
2. Select the paperclip icon.
3. Choose a file from your computer, or drag one into the box.
4. Type your message.
5. Select **Send**.
The file also appears on the project’s **Files** tab. To paste a screenshot, copy it and press **Ctrl+V** in the comment box.

title: Turn off email notifications for comments
body:
1. Select your profile picture at the top right, then **Notification settings**.
2. Under **Comments**, switch off **Email me about new comments**.
3. Select **Save**.
You will still see comments in your in-app **Inbox**. To mute a single task, open it and select **Unwatch**.

title: Print a board
aliases: get a paper copy of the board
save board as PDF to print
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Board** tab.
2. Apply any filters you want to appear on the printout.
3. Select the **More** menu (three dots) at the top right.
4. Select **Print board**.
5. Choose a **Page size** and select **Print**.
Only cards that match your current filters are included. Archived cards are never printed.

title: Start a timer on a task
body:
1. Open the task from **Projects**.
2. Select the **Start timer** button beside the task name.
3. Work as normal. The timer keeps running if you change pages.
4. Select **Stop timer** when you finish.
5. Check the entry in **Timesheets** and select **Save** to keep it.

title: Edit a time entry
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and open the week containing the entry.
2. Select the entry you want to change.
3. Update the hours, task or date.
4. Select **Save changes**.
You can only edit entries on timesheets that are still in **Draft** or **Rejected** status.

title: Delete a time entry
aliases: get rid of a timesheet entry
remove hours I booked by mistake
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and open the week containing the entry.
2. Select the entry you want to remove.
3. Select **Delete entry**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Delete**.
Deleted entries cannot be restored, so log the time again if you removed it by mistake.

title: Submit a timesheet for approval
aliases: send my timesheet to my manager
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and open the week you want to submit.
2. Check that each day shows the hours you expect.
3. Select **Submit for approval**.
4. Confirm in the dialog.
The status changes to **Submitted** and your approver is notified.

title: Approve a timesheet
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select the **To approve** tab.
2. Select the member whose timesheet you want to review.
3. Check the entries and any notes.
4. Select **Approve**.
The member is notified and the hours become available for reports and invoices.

title: Reject a timesheet and ask for changes
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select the **To approve** tab.
2. Open the submitted timesheet.
3. Select **Reject**.
4. Type a short reason in the **Comment** box.
5. Select **Send back**.
The status changes to **Rejected** so the member can edit and resubmit.

title: Mark a time entry as billable
aliases: charge the client for an entry
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and open the week containing the entry.
2. Select the entry.
3. Switch on the **Billable** toggle.
4. Select **Save changes**.
Billable hours use the billing rate set for that member or project, and appear when you generate an invoice.

title: Add a note to a time entry
aliases: write a comment on my hours
attach a description to logged time
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and open the week you want.
2. Select the entry you want to describe.
3. Type your text in the **Note** box. Keep it short and specific.
4. Select **Save changes**.
Notes show on approver screens and on invoices if you choose to include them.

title: Set a member's weekly hours target
body:
1. Go to **Workspace** and select **Members**.
2. Select the member's name.
3. In the **Working hours** section, enter the number of hours per week.
4. Select **Save**.
Timesheets show the target so members can see how close they are to it.

title: Export timesheets to CSV
aliases: save timesheet data as a CSV file
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select the **All timesheets** tab.
2. Choose a date range using the **Period** filter.
3. Filter by member or project if needed.
4. Select **Export** and choose **CSV**.
The file downloads to your device and includes one row per time entry.

title: Lock a timesheet period
aliases: close the month for time entry
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Time tracking**.
2. Under **Locked periods**, select **Add lock**.
3. Choose the date up to which timesheets should be locked.
4. Select **Lock period**.
Members can no longer add or edit time before that date. Only workspace admins can remove a lock.

title: Log time for another member
aliases: book hours for a team member
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and select **Switch member**.
2. Choose the person from the list.
3. Add a row and enter their hours as you would your own.
4. Select **Save**.
Only project managers and admins can log time for others. The entry shows who created it.

title: Reopen a submitted timesheet
aliases: pull back a timesheet I already sent
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and open the submitted week.
2. Select **Recall**.
3. Confirm by selecting **Return to draft**.
4. Make your changes.
5. Select **Submit for approval** again.
You cannot recall a timesheet once it has been approved. Ask an approver to reject it instead.

title: Copy last week's rows into this week
aliases: reuse my rows from last week
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and open the current week.
2. Select the **More** menu in the top right.
3. Select **Copy last week**.
4. Choose whether to copy rows only or rows with hours.
5. Select **Copy**.
You can then adjust the hours for each day before you submit.

title: Add an activity type
aliases: add a category such as Design or Meetings
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Time tracking**.
2. Select **Activity types**.
3. Select **New activity type**.
4. Enter a name and choose whether it is billable by default.
5. Select **Save**.
Members can pick the new type when they log time.

title: Turn on time rounding
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Time tracking**.
2. Switch on **Round time entries**.
3. Choose an increment such as 6, 15 or 30 minutes.
4. Choose **Round up** or **Round to nearest**.
5. Select **Save**.
Rounding applies to new entries only. Existing entries stay as they are.

title: Edit a project budget
body:
1. Open the project from **Projects**.
2. Select the **Budget** tab.
3. Select **Edit budget**.
4. Enter the new value and a reason in the **Note** box.
5. Select **Save**.
Each change is kept in the **Budget history** so approvers can see who changed it and when.

title: Set a budget alert threshold
aliases: warn me when a project is nearly over budget
get notified at 80 percent of budget
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Budget** tab.
2. Select **Alerts**.
3. Enter the percentage of the budget that should trigger a warning, for example 80.
4. Choose who should be notified.
5. Select **Save**.
Alerts are sent once when the threshold is passed.

title: Add a billing rate
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Billing rates**.
2. Select **New rate**.
3. Enter a name, such as Senior consultant, and the hourly amount.
4. Choose the currency.
5. Select **Save**.
You can then assign the rate to members or projects.

title: Update a member's billing rate
aliases: give a person a new charge-out rate
switch a member to a different rate
body:
1. Go to **Workspace** and select **Members**.
2. Select the member's name.
3. In the **Billing rate** section, choose a rate or enter a custom amount.
4. Select an **Effective from** date.
5. Select **Save**.
Time logged before the effective date keeps the old rate.

title: Delete a billing rate
aliases: remove a rate from the rate card
get rid of an old hourly rate
how do I delete a billing rate
body:
1. Go to **Settings** and select **Billing rates**.
2. Find the rate you no longer need.
3. Select the **More** menu beside it, then **Delete**.
4. If members use the rate, choose a replacement rate.
5. Confirm by selecting **Delete rate**.
Existing invoices are not affected.

title: Set a client-specific rate
aliases: charge one client a different rate
body:
1. Go to **Clients** and select the client.
2. Select the **Rates** tab.
3. Select **Add override**.
4. Choose the rate to replace and enter the client's amount.
5. Select **Save**.
Overrides apply to all that client's projects unless a project has its own rate.

title: Add an expense to a project
body:
1. Open the project from **Projects**.
2. Select the **Budget** tab, then **Expenses**.
3. Select **Add expense**.
4. Enter the date, amount, category and a description.
5. Select **Save**.
Expenses count towards the project budget.

title: Delete an expense
aliases: take off an expense I added twice
how do I delete an expense
body:
1. Open the project from **Projects**.
2. Select the **Budget** tab, then **Expenses**.
3. Select the expense you want to remove.
4. Select **Delete expense**.
5. Confirm by selecting **Delete**.
The budget total updates immediately. Expenses already invoiced cannot be deleted.

title: Mark an expense as billable
aliases: pass a cost on to the client
charge an expense to the customer
body:
1. Open the project and select **Budget**, then **Expenses**.
2. Select the expense.
3. Switch on **Billable**.
4. Optionally enter a markup percentage.
5. Select **Save changes**.
Billable expenses are added to the next invoice you generate.

title: Export a project budget to CSV
aliases: get budget data in a spreadsheet
body:
1. Open the project from **Projects**.
2. Select the **Budget** tab.
3. Select **Export** in the top right.
4. Choose **CSV**.
The file includes budget, spend, remaining amount and a row for each expense.
Changes take effect straight away for everyone in the workspace.

title: Change a budget from hours to amount
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Budget** tab.
2. Select **Edit budget**.
3. Change **Budget type** to **Amount**.
4. Enter the new total. Harbour does not convert hours automatically.
5. Select **Save**.
Spend is recalculated using each member's billing rate.

title: Update a client's billing contact email
body:
1. Go to **Clients** and select the client.
2. Select the **Billing** tab.
3. Select **Edit** beside **Billing contact**.
4. Enter the new name and email address.
5. Select **Save**.
Future invoices are sent to the new address. Invoices already sent are not resent.

title: Generate an invoice from tracked time
body:
1. Go to **Billing** and select **New invoice**.
2. Choose the client and project.
3. Select the date range to include.
4. Review the approved billable time and expenses, and untick anything to leave out.
5. Select **Create draft**.
Check the draft, then select **Send** to email it to the billing contact.

title: Send an invoice payment reminder
body:
1. Go to **Billing** and select the **Unpaid** tab.
2. Open the overdue invoice.
3. Select **Send reminder**.
4. Edit the message if you like.
5. Select **Send**.
The reminder goes to the client's billing contact and is logged on the invoice.

title: Mark an invoice as paid
body:
1. Go to **Billing** and open the invoice.
2. Select **Record payment**.
3. Enter the payment date and amount.
4. Select **Save**.
If the full amount is recorded, the status changes to **Paid** and the invoice no longer appears under **Unpaid**.

title: Create a template from an existing project
aliases: save a project as a template
turn a project into a template
body:
1. Open the project from **Projects**.
2. Select the **More** menu, then **Save as template**.
3. Enter a name and description.
4. Choose whether to keep members and budget settings.
5. Select **Create template**.
Logged time and comments are never copied into a template.

title: Start a new project from a template
aliases: spin up a project from a template
body:
1. Go to **Templates**.
2. Find the template you want and select **Use template**.
3. Enter the project name and choose a client.
4. Set the start date. Task due dates shift to match.
5. Select **Create project**.
The new project opens with all template tasks, milestones and roles in place.

title: Rename a template
aliases: how do I rename a template
body:
1. Go to **Templates** and open the template.
2. Select **Edit details**.
3. Type the new name in the **Name** field.
4. Select **Save**.
Projects already created from the template keep their own names.

title: Edit a template's description
aliases: update what a template is for
how do I edit a template's description
body:
1. Go to **Templates** and open the template.
2. Select **Edit details**.
3. Update the text in the **Description** box.
4. Select **Save**.
A clear description helps other members choose the right template.
The change is recorded in the activity log for your workspace.

title: Duplicate a template
aliases: make a variation of a template
body:
1. Go to **Templates**.
2. Select the **More** menu beside the template.
3. Select **Duplicate**.
4. Enter a name for the copy.
5. Select **Create copy**.
The copy starts in **Draft** status, so you can edit it before sharing.

title: Delete a template
aliases: get rid of a template I don't need
how do I delete a template
body:
1. Go to **Templates**.
2. Select the **More** menu beside the template.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Delete template**.
Projects already created from it are not affected. If you might need the template later, archive it instead.

title: Archive a template
body:
1. Go to **Templates**.
2. Select the **More** menu beside the template.
3. Select **Archive**.
Archived templates no longer appear when people start a new project. Select the **Archived** filter to see them, and restore them whenever you need.

title: Restore an archived template
aliases: how do I restore an archived template
body:
1. Go to **Templates**.
2. Select the **Archived** filter.
3. Select the **More** menu beside the template.
4. Select **Restore**.
The template returns to the main list with its previous status.
The change is recorded in the activity log for your workspace.

title: Add a task to a template
aliases: put a new task in a template
add a step to a template
how do I add a task to a template
body:
1. Go to **Templates** and open the template.
2. Select the **Tasks** tab.
3. Select **Add task**.
4. Enter a task name and set the **Due after** value, such as 5 days after the project starts.
5. Select **Save**.
Tasks can be reordered by dragging them in the list.

title: Edit a task in a template
aliases: update task details in a template
how do I edit a task in a template
body:
1. Go to **Templates** and open the template.
2. Select the **Tasks** tab.
3. Select the task you want to change.
4. Update the name, description or **Due after** value.
5. Select **Save**.
Changes only affect projects created from the template in future.

title: Remove a task from a template
aliases: take a step out of a template
how do I remove a task from a template
body:
1. Go to **Templates** and open the template.
2. Select the **Tasks** tab.
3. Select the **More** menu beside the task.
4. Select **Remove task**.
5. Confirm in the dialog.
Subtasks of the task are removed too.

title: Add a milestone to a template
aliases: put a milestone in a template
set key dates in a template
how do I add a milestone to a template
body:
1. Go to **Templates** and open the template.
2. Select the **Milestones** tab.
3. Select **Add milestone**.
4. Enter a name and the number of days after the project start.
5. Select **Save**.
Milestones appear on the project timeline when the template is used.

title: Set default roles in a template
aliases: how do I set default roles in a template
body:
1. Go to **Templates** and open the template.
2. Select the **Roles** tab.
3. Select **Add role** and enter a name such as Designer.
4. Choose a billing rate for the role.
5. Select **Save**.
When someone starts a project, they assign a real member to each role.

title: Share a template with the whole workspace
aliases: make a template available to everyone
body:
1. Go to **Templates** and open your private template.
2. Select **Share**.
3. Choose **Everyone in workspace**.
4. Select **Publish**.
Other members can use it but only you and admins can edit it. Change the status back to **Private** at any time.

title: Import template tasks from a CSV file
aliases: bulk add tasks from a spreadsheet
how do I import template tasks from a csv file
body:
1. Go to **Templates** and open the template.
2. Select the **Tasks** tab.
3. Select **Import**, then **Choose CSV file**.
4. Match the columns in your file to **Name**, **Description** and **Due after**.
5. Select **Import tasks**.
Rows with errors are skipped and listed so you can fix them.

title: Turn on email notifications
body:
1. Select your profile picture and choose **Notification settings**.
2. Open the **Email** tab.
3. Switch on **Email notifications**.
4. Tick the events you want, such as task assignments and approvals.
5. Select **Save**.
Emails are sent to the address on your profile.

title: Turn off task assignment emails
aliases: stop emails when I'm assigned a task
how do I turn off task assignment emails
body:
1. Select your profile picture and choose **Notification settings**.
2. Open the **Email** tab.
3. Untick **Task assigned to me**.
4. Select **Save**.
You will still see assignments in the notification bell inside Harbour.
You can reverse this at any time by repeating the steps.

title: Change the email address for notifications
aliases: send alerts to a different email
body:
1. Select your profile picture and choose **Profile**.
2. Select **Edit** beside **Email**.
3. Enter your new email address.
4. Select **Save** and confirm using the code we email you.
All notifications will go to the new address once it is verified.

title: Switch to a daily digest email
aliases: get one summary email a day
body:
1. Select your profile picture and choose **Notification settings**.
2. Open the **Email** tab.
3. Under **Delivery**, choose **Daily digest**.
4. Pick the time you want it sent.
5. Select **Save**.
Urgent items such as rejected timesheets are still sent straight away.

title: Mute a project's notifications
body:
1. Open the project from **Projects**.
2. Select the bell icon at the top of the page.
3. Select **Mute project**.
4. Choose how long to mute it, or select **Until I turn it on**.
Direct mentions still reach you. Select **Unmute** from the same menu to resume everything else.

title: Unmute a project
aliases: turn alerts back on for a project
how do I unmute a project
body:
1. Open the project from **Projects**.
2. Select the bell icon at the top of the page.
3. Select **Unmute project**.
You will receive notifications for the project again, based on your usual settings.
You can reverse this at any time by repeating the steps.

title: Set quiet hours
body:
1. Select your profile picture and choose **Notification settings**.
2. Open the **Schedule** tab.
3. Switch on **Quiet hours**.
4. Choose a start and end time and the days it applies to.
5. Select **Save**.
Notifications are held and delivered when quiet hours end.

title: Turn on mobile push notifications
aliases: how do I turn on mobile push notifications
body:
1. Open the Harbour Projects app on your phone.
2. Select **More**, then **Notification settings**.
3. Switch on **Push notifications**.
4. Allow notifications when your phone asks.
5. Choose the events you want.
Push settings are separate for each device.

title: Add a mobile number for text alerts
aliases: update my phone number for SMS
get text messages for urgent alerts
change my mobile number for alerts
body:
1. Select your profile picture and choose **Notification settings**.
2. Open the **Text message** tab.
3. Select **Edit number** and enter your mobile number.
4. Enter the code we text you.
5. Select **Verify**.
Text alerts are only sent for overdue deadlines and rejected timesheets.

title: Choose how you are notified of mentions
aliases: how do I choose how you are notified of mentions
body:
1. Select your profile picture and choose **Notification settings**.
2. Find **Mentions**.
3. Choose **Email**, **Push**, or both.
4. Select **Save**.
Mentions are always shown in the notification bell, whichever delivery options you pick.
You can reverse this at any time by repeating the steps.

title: Set reminders for overdue tasks
aliases: remind me when tasks are late
how do I set reminders for overdue tasks
body:
1. Select your profile picture and choose **Notification settings**.
2. Open the **Reminders** tab.
3. Switch on **Overdue tasks**.
4. Choose how often to be reminded: daily or weekly.
5. Select **Save**.
Reminders list only tasks assigned to you.

title: Turn off timer reminders
aliases: how do I turn off timer reminders
body:
1. Select your profile picture and choose **Notification settings**.
2. Open the **Reminders** tab.
3. Switch off **Timer still running**.
4. Select **Save**.
You can switch it back on at any time. Workspace admins may also set a default for new members.

title: Mark all notifications as read
body:
1. Select the bell icon at the top of any page.
2. Select **Mark all as read**.
Notifications stay in the list for 30 days, so you can open them later. Select **Unread** to show only the ones you have not seen yet.

title: Delete a single notification
aliases: how do I delete a single notification
body:
1. Select the bell icon at the top of any page.
2. Point to the notification you want to remove.
3. Select the **X** that appears on the right.
Deleting a notification only removes it from your list. It does not change the task or comment it refers to.

title: Choose who receives budget alerts
aliases: change who is warned about budget
send budget warnings to the project manager
how do I choose who receives budget alerts
body:
1. Open the project and select the **Budget** tab.
2. Select **Alerts**.
3. In **Recipients**, add or remove members.
4. Select **Save**.
Recipients receive alerts by email and in the notification bell, based on their own settings.

title: Unsubscribe a guest from notifications
aliases: how do I unsubscribe a guest from notifications
body:
1. Go to **Workspace** and select **Guests**.
2. Select the guest's name.
3. Switch off **Email notifications**.
4. Select **Save**.
The guest can still open the projects they have access to. They can turn notifications back on from the link in any email.

title: Notify an approver when you submit a timesheet
aliases: how do I notify an approver when you submit a timesheet
body:
1. Go to **Timesheets** and open the week you want to submit.
2. Select **Submit for approval**.
3. Tick **Send a message to my approver**.
4. Type your message and select **Submit**.
Approvers are always notified of a submission. This option adds your note to the email.

title: Run a utilisation report
aliases: see how busy my team is
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and select **Utilisation**.
2. Choose a date range.
3. Select the members or teams to include.
4. Select **Run report**.
The report shows billable hours as a percentage of each person's weekly target. Use **Group by** to switch between members and teams.

title: Run a time by member report
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and select **Time**.
2. Set **Group by** to **Member**.
3. Choose a date range and projects.
4. Select **Run report**.
Select any row to see the individual time entries behind it.
Changes take effect straight away for everyone in the workspace.

title: Run a budget versus actual report
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and select **Budget vs actual**.
2. Choose the projects or clients to include.
3. Select **Run report**.
Each project shows budget, spend to date, remaining amount and a status bar. Projects over budget are marked in red.

title: Run a project profitability report
aliases: how much profit did we make
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and select **Profitability**.
2. Choose a date range.
3. Select **Run report**.
4. Compare **Revenue**, **Cost** and **Margin** for each project.
Cost uses each member's cost rate, which admins can set under **Members**.

title: Change a report's date range
body:
1. Open the report from **Reports**.
2. Select the **Date range** button.
3. Choose a preset such as **Last month**, or select **Custom** and enter dates.
4. Select **Apply**.
The report refreshes automatically.
You can reverse this at any time by repeating the steps.

title: Filter a report by client
aliases: narrow a report to a customer
how do I filter a report by client
body:
1. Open the report from **Reports**.
2. Select **Filters**.
3. Choose **Client** and select one or more clients.
4. Select **Apply**.
The filter applies to this view only unless you save the report.
Changes take effect straight away for everyone in the workspace.

title: Change how a report is grouped
aliases: group by project instead of member
how do I change how a report is grouped
body:
1. Open the report from **Reports**.
2. Select **Group by**.
3. Choose an option such as **Project**, **Client**, **Member** or **Week**.
The table and chart update straight away. Select **Save report** if you want to keep the new layout.

title: Export a report to CSV
aliases: download a report as a spreadsheet
body:
1. Open the report from **Reports**.
2. Run it with the date range and filters you want.
3. Select **Export**.
4. Choose **CSV**.
The file downloads to your device with the figures as shown on screen.

title: Export a report as a PDF
aliases: download report to share with client
make a PDF of a report
body:
1. Open the report from **Reports**.
2. Run it with the date range and filters you want.
3. Select **Export**.
4. Choose **PDF**.
5. Select **Include chart** if you want the graph at the top.
The PDF uses your workspace logo and name in the header.

title: Save a report
aliases: how do I save a report
body:
1. Open the report and set the filters and grouping you want.
2. Select **Save report**.
3. Enter a name.
4. Choose **Only me** or **Everyone in workspace**.
5. Select **Save**.
Saved reports appear under **Saved** on the **Reports** page.

title: Rename a saved report
aliases: how do I rename a saved report
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and select **Saved**.
2. Select the **More** menu beside the report.
3. Select **Rename**.
4. Enter the new name and select **Save**.
Scheduled emails will use the new name from the next send.

title: Delete a saved report
aliases: get rid of an old report
how do I delete a saved report
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and select **Saved**.
2. Select the **More** menu beside the report.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Confirm by selecting **Delete report**.
Any schedule attached to the report is deleted too. You can only delete reports that you created, unless you are an admin.

title: Schedule a report to be emailed
aliases: email me a report each month
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and open a saved report.
2. Select **Schedule**.
3. Choose how often to send it: weekly or monthly.
4. Add the email addresses of the people who should receive it.
5. Select **Save schedule**.
Recipients get a PDF and a CSV attached.

title: Stop a scheduled report
aliases: how do I stop a scheduled report
body:
1. Go to **Reports** and select **Scheduled**.
2. Find the report you want to stop.
3. Select the **More** menu, then **Delete schedule**.
4. Confirm in the dialog.
The saved report itself is kept. Only the automatic emails stop.

title: Add a note to a saved report
aliases: write a comment on a report
how do I add a note to a saved report
body:
